author: trowsey
body:
## Summary

Steam Linux build brown-screens because three native libraries — \`libMCDCoreExt.so\`, \`libgodotsteam.linux.template_release.x86_64.so\`, \`libsentry.linux.release.x86_64.so\` — are missing from the shipped zip (or present at the wrong path). Without them, \`SceneManager\` and \`CrashReporter\` autoloads fail to parse because \`BuildInfo\` and \`GameServerProxy\` never register, and Godot renders its default clear color.

## Root cause

Godot 4.6's single-file export (\`embed_pck=true\` → \`.x86_64\`/\`.exe\`) **flattens** every GDExtension library + dependency into the output directory, ignoring the nested paths declared in the \`.gdextension\` files. The same \`.gdextension\` files get baked into the embedded pck, and at runtime the engine reads them from \`res://\` — which resolves to paths relative to the installed exe. So e.g. \`res://bin/MCDCoreExt.gdextension\` expects \`<game>/bin/lib/Linux-x86_64/libMCDCoreExt.so\` on disk, not the flat \`exports/libMCDCoreExt.so\` Godot actually produces.

The old \`Stage Artifacts\` block half-worked around it for MCDCoreExt (re-nested into \`lib/…\` instead of \`bin/lib/…\` — still wrong) and wrote a root-level \`MCDCoreExt.gdextension\` the runtime never consulted. \`libgodotsteam.*\`, \`libsentry.*\`, \`crashpad_handler\`, \`crashpad_wer.dll\` never made it into the zip at all.

## Fix

- Re-nest every Godot-emitted library into the path its matching \`.gdextension\` declares, for both Linux and Windows:
  - \`bin/lib/{Linux-x86_64,Windows-x86_64}/\` → MCDCoreExt + MinGW runtime DLLs
  - \`addons/godotsteam/{linux64,win64}/\` → libgodotsteam + libsteam_api / steam_api64
  - \`addons/sentry/bin/{linux,windows}/x86_64/\` → libsentry + crashpad_handler(.exe) + crashpad_wer.dll
- Drop the hand-written root-level \`MCDCoreExt.gdextension\` — redundant with the pck-embedded one, and only served to mask the real layout bug.
- Add a post-stage existence check for every expected artifact so a future Godot version change that renames an output fails loudly instead of silently producing a half-populated zip.
- Move MinGW deps (\`libcrypto-3-x64.dll\`, \`libssl-3-x64.dll\`, \`libwinpthread-1.dll\`) next to \`MCDCoreExt.dll\` rather than the exe root — that's where Windows' DLL search looks first for a loaded module's dependencies.

One shared-library change → both \`MCDClient-Main\` and \`MCDClient-Release\` pick it up on the next build through \`@Library('mcd-shared')\`. No MCDClient-repo changes needed, so nothing to cherry-pick between its main and release branches.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run MCDClient-Main; verify zip contents match the \`.gdextension\` layout (\`unzip -l\` should show nested paths + all 5 Linux libs / 8 Windows libs).
- [ ] Run MCDClient-Release; same check on the release zip.
- [ ] Re-run MCDSteam-Upload with the new release build, set-live the new build on Steamworks, launch from Steam on Linux, confirm no \"GDExtension dynamic library not found\" in \`~/.local/share/Steam/logs/console-linux.txt\` and the title screen loads.
- [x] New inline \`for f in …\` existence check will short-circuit the stage if Godot changes an output name in a future upgrade — no separate unit test needed for a one-file shell change.

author: goggledefogger
body:
## Summary

Hotfix on top of #17. Live OAuth sign-in was failing with "PKCE code verifier not found in storage" because our callback page was racing Supabase's built-in code exchange.

## Root cause

Two things were trying to consume the same OAuth code:

1. **Supabase's `detectSessionInUrl: true`** (in `src/lib/supabase.ts`) — on client init, GoTrue detects `?code=...` in the URL, reads the PKCE verifier from localStorage, exchanges the code for a session, and **removes the verifier from storage**.
2. **Our manual `exchangeCodeForSession(code)`** in `AuthCallbackPage.tsx` — runs a moment later in the `useEffect`, reads the same code from `searchParams` (which didn't clear because auto-detect used `history.replaceState`, which doesn't poke React Router), looks for the verifier, finds nothing, returns a user-facing error.

Net: auto-detect wins the race → session is actually created → but our code also runs, fails, and shows the error card over the already-logged-in session. User bounces to "Back to login" instead of `/channels`.

## Fix

Remove the manual exchange. Let auto-detect be the single consumer of the code. Match the pattern `ResetPasswordPage.tsx` already uses: wait for the session via `getSession()` + `onAuthStateChange`, navigate when it appears, show an error if nothing lands within 8s.

Why this over "disable `detectSessionInUrl`": the reset-password flow (`ResetPasswordPage.tsx:30,36`) depends on auto-detect to pick up `PASSWORD_RECOVERY` tokens from the email link. Disabling it breaks that flow. Keeping auto-detect on and letting it handle both callbacks is the cleaner choice.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run build` — TypeScript clean
- [x] `npm test` — 43/43 pass
- [ ] Manual: https://magic-brooms.vercel.app/login → Continue with GitHub → lands on `/channels` with a GitHub display name + avatar
- [ ] Manual: `/reset-password` flow still works (password recovery email → click link → set new password)

author: jeff-roche
body:
Closes forge-ide/forge#355

## Summary
- Add `read_frame_with_deadline` to forge-ipc, wrapping the existing `read_frame` in `tokio::time::timeout`.
- Apply a 10s handshake deadline to the `Hello` and `Subscribe` reads inside `handle_connection`.
- Apply a 5min post-handshake idle timeout on the client → daemon command-reader task; a stalled peer now surfaces to the outer `select!` as a closed channel and the connection is torn down.
- Deadlines are tunable via `FORGE_IPC_HANDSHAKE_DEADLINE_MS` and `FORGE_IPC_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS` for tests and operator override.
- Regression tests: silent peer disconnected within handshake deadline; half-handshaked peer disconnected before `Subscribe` deadline; fully handshaked-but-idle peer disconnected within idle timeout.

## Threat closed
Local same-uid peer opens the UDS socket, sends zero bytes (or a partial length prefix), and pins a session task indefinitely — CWE-400 / CWE-770, same finding class as F-044's per-user runtime-dir invariant, now with inter-frame starvation covered.

## Test plan
- `cargo test --workspace` passes (8 handshake tests; 3 are new).
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes.
- Manual reproduction from the issue (`socat - UNIX-CONNECT:<sock>` then send nothing) now disconnects within 10s instead of hanging forever.

## Verification status
PR is open; DoD and code-review gates are pending in the parent context (per the forge-finish-task handoff protocol).

body:
## Actual Execution Path
- `launch_field_analysis_latest_local.cmd`
- `app_field_analysis_latest.py`
- `field_analysis.app_ui`
- `src/field_analysis/app_ui.py` loader
- `src/field_analysis/app_ui_snapshot.py`
- `run_app()` / `run_quick_lut_app()`
- `_run_app_shell()`
- `_render_quick_lut_tab_v2()`

## Actual Modeling Changes
- Kept the Quick LUT scalar route field-first and added explicit field-only metadata so the returned recommendation now states that the target shape is fixed to `rounded_triangle`, the target pp is fixed to `100`, and shape selection excludes `current`, `gain`, `hardware`, and `lcr`.
- Added a fixed field target helper in `src/field_analysis/lut.py` and a finite-cycle normalization helper that constrains the LUT route to the allowed cycle set: `1.0`, `1.25`, `1.5`, `1.75`.
- Kept `waveform_type` as support/input waveform family only and separated it in metadata from the fixed target field shape.

## UI / Real Usage Path Changes
- Quick LUT now labels the waveform selector as support/input waveform family instead of implying it chooses the target field shape.
- The main Quick LUT screen now makes `Field-only`, `Rounded-triangle target`, and `100pp fixed` visible before the user clicks anything.
- The old field/current target selector and the `20.0` field/current-looking default input were removed from the main path. The waveform compensation button now stays on the field path and uses the same fixed field target philosophy as the scalar LUT path.
- Finite-cycle selection in Quick LUT is constrained in the UI to the intended allowed set instead of free numeric entry.

## Export / Debug / Readiness / Diagnostics
- No export code changes.
- No run readiness changes.
- No diagnostics changes.
- Debug/equipment wording in the Quick LUT screen was updated only where needed to make it clear that current/gain/hardware are reference-only for the main scalar route.

## User-Visible Checks In App
- The Quick LUT screen immediately shows `Field-only / rounded-triangle / 100pp fixed`.
- The waveform selector is clearly described as support/input waveform family only.
- The scalar LUT result now shows fixed target shape metadata separately from support waveform family metadata.
- The waveform compensation action stays on the field path and no longer exposes current mode as the main operating choice.

## Tests Run
- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_lut_field_only_core.py tests/test_repository_smoke.py tests/test_file_size_guardrails.py`
- `python -m pytest -q`
- `python -m py_compile src/field_analysis/lut.py src/field_analysis/app_ui_snapshot.py tests/test_lut_field_only_core.py`

## Remaining Limits
- The compensation runtime is still a larger legacy path and was intentionally not refactored here.
- Export payloads still include legacy scalar fields; this PR only aligns the Quick LUT UI and scalar route behavior/metadata.
- The full app still contains older non-Quick-LUT screens whose wording may not yet reflect the same field-only operating language.

## Next B Handoff
- Codex B can build on the new fixed-target metadata if follow-up work is needed in compensation/export layers.
- The next useful B task is to align waveform-compensation result summaries and downstream artifacts with the same `support waveform family vs fixed rounded-triangle field target` separation without widening the main shape-selection basis.

body: ## Summary Closes out the remaining Phase 1 (Architecture Proof) spec items and kicks off Phase 2 by putting the Wasabi adapter on real AWS SDK v2 calls. **Phase 1 spec items** - `tests/control_plane/no_data_test.go`: reflection-based contract test that walks the manifest, tenant, placement, and billing types and fails if any field is typed `io.Reader`/`io.ReadCloser`/`io.Writer`/`[]byte`/`*bytes.Buffer`. Also walks `ManifestStore` method signatures. - `metadata/erasure_coding`: `ErasureCodingProfile` with 6+2 / 8+3 / 10+4 constants, `Validate`, and `StorageOverhead`. Divisibility check between `StripeSize` and `DataShards` was **removed** — real RS codecs pad the final sub-stripe, and the standard 4 MiB stripe is not divisible by 6 or 10. - `metadata/tenant`: `Tenant` type matching PROPOSAL.md §5.5 (`contract_type`, `license_tier`, `keys`, `placement_default`, `budgets`, `abuse`, `billing`) with `Validate` and JSON/YAML round-trip. - `tests/benchmark/suite.go`: declarative target metrics (PUT/GET p50/p95/p99, cache-hit ratio > 90 %, Wasabi origin egress ≤ 1.0, LIST at 10M/100M/1B). - `cache/hot_object_cache`: adds `PromotionPolicy`, `EvictionPolicy` (LRU with hot-pin), tier-based defaults, and NVMe/block-storage sizing guidance in the package comment. - `providers/wasabi/guardrails.go`: fair-use types (`FairUseEgressBudget`, `MinStorageTracker`, `CacheHitRatioTarget`, `AlertThresholds`, composite `Guardrails`) encoding the ≤1.0 egress/storage ratio and 90-day minimum storage. **Wasabi adapter on AWS SDK v2** - `providers/s3_generic/generic.go` is rewritten to implement PUT / GET (with `Range`) / HEAD / DELETE / LIST-V2 against `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/s3`. Exposes an `S3API` interface for test injection. - `providers/wasabi/wasabi.go` now embeds `*s3_generic.Provider` and overrides `Capabilities` (90-day min storage), `CostModel`, and `PlacementLabels`. - The conformance suite is extracted into `tests/providers/conformance` with an `Options` struct. `TestStorageProvider_LocalFSDev` runs as before; a new `TestStorageProvider_Wasabi` runs the suite against an in-memory S3 fake so CI needs no Wasabi credentials. **Docs** - `docs/PROGRESS.md`: all Phase 1 boxes checked with implementing-file references; status flipped to `COMPLETE`; decision-gate outcome recorded (**Ceph RGW** selected as the Phase 2+ local-DC base, SeaweedFS retained as fallback). ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Wasabi adapter has not been run against real Wasabi.** CI only exercises the in-memory fake. Before relying on it, run `TestStorageProvider_Wasabi` (or the equivalent) with real credentials and endpoint to confirm auth, region handling, and metadata round-tripping work. Verify behaviour differences flagged in the conformance `Options` (S3 delete is idempotent; S3 keys allow `/` and `..`) match production expectations. - [ ] **Confirm the Ceph RGW decision recorded in `PROGRESS.md` reflects stakeholder sign-off** and not just Devin's summary of the existing comparison table. - [ ] Skim `tests/control_plane/no_data_test.go`: the detection uses `reflect.PtrTo(ft).Implements(banned)` which will also flag any future struct with a `Read`/`Write` method, even unrelated to customer data. Decide if that over-broad catch is what you want or if the rule should be tightened. - [ ] Sanity-check the decision to drop the `StripeSize % DataShards == 0` check in `erasure_coding.Validate` — the three standard profiles now validate, but if any downstream code assumed no padding this will silently break it. - [ ] Build + run the suite locally: `go build ./... && go test ./...` should pass (it does on Devin's VM). ### Notes - `go.mod` adds `aws-sdk-go-v2/credentials` and `service/s3`. `yaml.v3` was already introduced earlier in the session for `metadata/tenant`. - This PR touches 22 files and adds ~2.7k lines; most of the new volume is declarative spec types and tests. author: kalverra
body:
Includes a new tool, `tools/test` that provides a simpler way for devs to run /chainlink unit tests, and includes features to help hunt down flakes and races.

## Simpler Test Runs

Running tests in /chainlink requires chaining together 2-3 make commands, and you can miss steps. Not anymore!
```sh
# Help menu for all available commands
go -C ./tools/test run . -h

# Spin up a Postgres container, run go tests, and tear it down all with one command!
go -C ./tools/test run . run -v -count=1 -p 4 ./core/...
# Or use make
make new_test ARGS="-v -p 4 ./core/..."

# Use gotestsum if you prefer!
go -C ./tools/test run . gotestsum --format=dots -- -count=1 ./core/...
# Even with make!
make new_gotestsum ARGS="--format=dots -- -count=1 ./core/..."
```

### Why not just `go test ./...`?

I'd love to, but the problem is overhead. 

`go test` doesn't have any sort of "before all test runs" control. So, to make `go test ./...` work, we'd need to launch a new PostgreSQL test container for every package that needs a real DB. This can cause serious memory, processing, and runtime overhead.

_It is possible this isn't a big deal, and we could reduce/eliminate this concern with some refactoring, but that's outside the scope of this approach._

## `diagnose`

You can now easily diagnose test issues with a single command, re-running tests, packages, and suites, and generating summarized results. With one command, you can exhaustively search for:
* Flakes
* Races
* Slow tests
* Deadlocks

```sh
# Run a package 25 times to look for slow tests (30s or more)
go -C ./tools/test run . diagnose --iterations 25 --slow-threshold 30s -- ./core/services/ocr2/plugins/ocr2keeper/...
# Run all of core 10 times with race (will take a while!)
go -C ./tools/test run . diagnose --iterations 10 -- --timeout=10m -race ./core/...
```

## Future Plans/Improvements

- Add `/diagnose-tests` AI skill
- Use `go tool test` instead of `go -C ./tools/test` once https://github.com/smartcontractkit/chainlink-testing-framework/pull/2510 is merged.

author: yichehnc
body:
Closes #385

## Summary

Mobile-responsive fixes across the Vibe Raising founder flow — every visible break-at-mobile layout issue we hit during design review, plus a small dev infrastructure improvement so teammates don't need the live backend running to iterate locally.

## Fixes

### Responsive layout
- **Metric card grids now wrap on mobile.** The five-column grid (`grid-cols-5`) on the founder *My Updates* view and the create-update form was squishing metric cards into a cramped row on phones. Switched to a mobile-first `grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-3 md:grid-cols-5` across both pages (seven grids in total). (c20a3be, 3717405)
- **Preview + feedback sidebar now stack on mobile.** The update-preview used an unconditional `flex` row with a fixed 224px sidebar, so on a 375px phone the preview got squeezed to ~150px wide. Now stacked below `lg`, side-by-side from `lg+`. (d5eaf1a)
- **Equal-width Record/Select-file pair.** The two dropzone action buttons had intrinsic widths, so the row reflowed whenever "Record" became "Stop Recording." Made them `flex-1` so they share space equally, plus stacked on phones. Also tightened outer dropzone padding (`p-12` → `p-6 sm:p-12`) so the zone doesn't eat the whole viewport on mobile. (228bc4c)

### Visual hierarchy
- **Demoted the AI Grade from a 4xl standalone card to a small pill badge inside the company identity card.** As shipped the grade drew more visual weight than the update preview it was grading. Company name is now the largest element in the sidebar; grade is supporting info. (d5eaf1a)

### Dev infrastructure
- **Env-gated backend stubs for local dev.** Adds opt-in stubs (set `VITE_STUB_BACKEND=true` in a gitignored `.env.local`) that short-circuit all `api.mlai.au` calls with fake data: logged-in founder, seeded company, three seeded monthly updates, empty array for everything else. Nothing fires in normal dev or production. Solves the "I can't work on UI while the backend is down" problem. (083ade8)
- **Remove `package-lock.json`** in favour of `bun.lock`. Having both caused rollup / tailwind-oxide / lightningcss native-binding install failures on fresh Windows clones when tooling fell back to npm. (28fd9ab)

## Test plan

- [ ] Open `/vibe-raising` at 375px — metric cards wrap to 2 per row
- [ ] Resize to 640px — 3 per row
- [ ] Resize to ≥768px — 5 per row (original layout preserved)
- [ ] Open `/vibe-raising/create-update` at 375px — preview + feedback stack vertically, AI Grade appears as a small pill on the identity card
- [ ] Resize to ≥1024px — sidebar returns to the right, sticky, with grade still as a pill
- [ ] On the same page, dropzone buttons: "Record" and "Select file" stack on mobile, side-by-side from `sm+`, both equal width. Toggle to "Stop Recording" — width doesn't change
- [ ] To preview any of this without a running backend: add `VITE_STUB_BACKEND=true` to `.env.local`, restart `bun run dev`

## Notes / caveats

- Commit `fd2cc5d` ("chore: test commit") is noise from the very first push on this branch — one whitespace character in `authors.ts` plus a permissions tweak in `.claude/settings.local.json`. Consider **squash-merging** this PR so it doesn't land in `main` history.
- The dev-stub adapter returns `{ data: [] }` for *any* unseeded endpoint, so some UI sections will show "empty state" locally. For fuller simulation later, we'd graduate to MSW (Mock Service Worker) with stateful handlers.

# What does this implement/fix?

<!-- Quick description and explanation of changes -->

Exposes temperature unit for climate and water_heater, with corresponding changes in home-assistant/core, aioesphome, esphome, and esphome-docs, to enable native Fahrenheit measurements on those entities. Usecase is to enable accurate temperature settings on a Fahrenheit hot tub, controlled via RS485-UART. Rather than round tripped from F -> C -> C, with various floating point errors and weirdnesses, this just makes it stay F the entire way and work much more reliably.

Tests still need to be added where appropriate - that's on the todo - but the code has been validated. 

When esphome is updated, but core is not, as long as you do not set the temperature unit on a climate/water heater, everything works the same as it currently is. If you do set it, you will convert from F -> "F", as home assistant will think the incoming value from ESPHome is C, without reading the UOM. If ESPHome does not have F specified, it continues to default to C.

When HA is updated, but ESPHome is on an old version, it maintains legacy behavior of treating all climate/water_heaters as using C.

author: dieshen
body:
## Summary
Closes #66. Filters `use std::*` paths out of both Rust and Go codegen `emit_prelude`, because `std::*` in Gust is a virtual namespace for stdlib machines/types — emitting it literally collides with Rust's own `std` crate and produces an invalid Go import path.

## Discovery
PR #65 (workflow_engine example rewrite for Corsac) hit this immediately: `use std::EngineFailure;` is the canonical import for the EngineFailure stdlib type, but the generated `workflow.g.rs` wouldn't compile. The workaround there was a brittle `build.rs` hack (copy engine_failure.gu, compile separately, strip the broken line).

## Treatment
The consumer's build pipeline is responsible for compiling stdlib sources alongside the dependent machine (placing them in the same module/package), so no target-language `use`/`import` needs to be emitted. Both codegens now skip `use_paths` whose first segment is `"std"`.

## Tests
- `std_imports_stripped_from_rust_codegen` — bare `use std::EngineFailure;` produces no `use std::...` line in Rust output.
- `std_imports_stripped_from_go_codegen` — no `"std/EngineFailure"` or `"std"` in Go import list.
- `non_std_imports_still_emitted_after_std_filter` — mixed `use std::...` + `use crate::...` confirms the filter is scoped; real imports survive.

## Impact on Corsac
Without this fix, the documented onboarding path (use `EngineFailure` via `use std::EngineFailure;`, see the workflow-runtime guide in PR #62) doesn't actually work. This unblocks it.

## Follow-up
PR #65's `build.rs` stripping hack can be deleted once this lands. Small cleanup PR after merge.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-features` — 42 test suites green
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean
- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings -D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps --all-features` — clean
- [ ] CI green

Closes #66

author: mmshad
body:
Closes #63.

## What

Make declared per-op timeouts on init and coordination collectives actually enforce. Today they fall through to the 1800s process-group default, so a wedged peer hangs the job for 30 minutes regardless of the caller's intent.

- `kempnerforge/resilience/health.py::check_nccl_health` switches to `async_op=True` + `Work.wait(timeout=timedelta(seconds=timeout_sec))` and returns `False` on either timeout signaling path (RuntimeError on modern PyTorch, `False` return on legacy backends).
- `kempnerforge/distributed/setup.py` adds `_barrier_with_timeout(seconds, reason)` and uses it for the DeviceMesh-construction barrier with a 60s budget. Timeouts raise `RuntimeError` with the reason string attached so the failure points at the right phase of init.
- `kempnerforge/training/eval.py` wraps the PP eval loss broadcast in a 300s budget with a `nan` fallback so a wedged PP stage surfaces as a clear bad-iteration signal instead of a half-hour hang.
- `kempnerforge/distributed/setup.py::_set_nccl_env` `setdefault`s `TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` and logs a warning when a user has explicitly set it to `0`. Without this, every per-op bound in this patch is advisory.

## Known limit, train_state broadcast

The original commit also wired a 600s `async_op=True` budget around the train_state broadcast in `CheckpointManager.load`. PyTorch 2.11's `dist.broadcast_object_list` does not accept `async_op` (TypeError at runtime), so the second commit on this branch reverts that one site to the plain synchronous form and leaves an explanatory comment. The other three call sites still get fast-fail; a wedged rank surfaces via those before the broadcast hits the 1800s default.

## Tests

`tests/unit/test_collective_timeouts.py` (10 new tests, all passing locally):
- `TestCheckNcclHealthTimeout` covers `Work.wait(timedelta(...))` forwarding, `RuntimeError` and `False`-return timeout paths, and the not-initialized early return.
- `TestBarrierWithTimeout` covers the reason-string error message, the `False`-return path, and the success path.
- `TestNcclAsyncErrorHandlingEnvGuard` covers the unset/explicit-1/explicit-0 cases for `TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING`.

The test file documents the absence of a `TestCheckpointBroadcastTimeout` class with a comment pointing at the PyTorch 2.11 limitation.

body:
## What does this PR do?

Implements the `_dequantize()` method for `TorchAoHfQuantizer`, enabling `model.dequantize()` to convert TorchAO-quantized models back to standard float weights.

### Changes

1. **Add `_dequantize()` method**: Iterates all `nn.Linear` modules, calls `weight.dequantize()` on `TorchAOBaseTensor` weights, replaces them with standard `nn.Parameter`, and resets any overridden `extra_repr`.

2. **Fix `_verify_if_layer_quantized`**: Added `isinstance(module.weight, TorchAOBaseTensor)` check so that dequantized layers (which are still `nn.Linear` but with plain tensor weights) are correctly detected as non-quantized.

author: kaizenman
body:
Method-by-method walk through the remaining parser functions (\`_parseTrack\`, \`_parseTrackProperty\`, \`_parseMasterTrackNode\`, \`_parseBeatProperties\`, \`_parseNoteProperties\`, \`_parseRhythm\`, \`_parseDirections\`, \`_parseFermata\`, \`_parseMasterBar\`, \`_parseBar\`, \`_parseConcertPitch\`, \`_parseRSE\`, \`_parseChannelStripParameters\`, \`_parsePartSounding\`, \`_parseTranspose\`) found five more alphaTab-parity gaps.

## 1. \`<Track><Properties>\` dual-dispatch

alphaTab's \`_parseTrackProperty\` handles Tuning / DiagramCollection / CapoFret at **track** level in addition to staff level (legacy GPIF path). PyGuitarPro only checked inside \`<Staff><Properties>\`. Modern GP7/GP8 files never trip the track-level path, but GP6 files and back-compat exports that emit Properties directly on \`<Track>\` would lose their tuning / capo / chord diagrams.

**Fix.** Extracted the Property loop into a shared \`_apply_track_properties()\` helper and wired it at both levels.

## 2. Property-form whammy middle-offset edge case

alphaTab emits one middle whammy point per non-null offset:
\`\`\`
offset1=25, offset2=None → 1 point at 25
offset1=None, offset2=50 → 1 point at 50
offset1=None, offset2=None + middleValue → 1 point at maxPosition/2
\`\`\`

PGP's old code always emitted a point at \`offset1 or fallback-6\`, then conditionally another at offset2. With \`offset1=None + offset2=50\` it emitted **TWO** points (at 6 and 50) — a spurious midpoint at the fallback position.

## 3. Note \`<Bended>\` curve — same edge case

Same pattern as whammy, same fix.

## 4. QuadrupleWhole (Long) duration

alphaTab has 11 \`<NoteValue>\` tokens; PyGuitarPro had 10. Missing: \`Long\` → \`QuadrupleWhole = -4\` (four whole notes). A rhythm with \`<NoteValue>Long</NoteValue>\` silently mapped to the default Quarter in PGP. Added \`Duration.quadrupleWhole\` sentinel and the \`_DURATION_MAP\` entry; \`time\` property returns \`quarterTime * 16\` for the longa.

## 5. \`<MasterTrack><Anacrusis/>\` dead code in PGP

**alphaTab**: reads at MasterTrack level, applies to the first MasterBar ([line 1354-1356, 413-415](https://github.com/CoderLine/alphaTab/blob/main/packages/alphatab/src/importer/GpifParser.ts#L413-L415)).

**PGP**: looked for \`<Anacrusis>\` inside each MasterBar — but GPIF never emits it there. The anacrusis flag was **never set**, regardless of whether the file had it.

**Fix.** \`_read_master_track\` stashes \`self._has_anacrusis\`; \`_build_measure_header\` copies it onto the first bar. Verified on \`tests/gp7/anacrusis.gp\` — now correctly reports True (was silently False before).

## How these slipped through prior audits

- **#1** (track-level Properties): coverage gate sees \`\"Tuning\"\` / \`\"CapoFret\"\` in gp7.py and marks them covered. The gap was the *entry point*, not the handlers.
- **#2 & #3** (edge-case middle-offset): both hidden inside existing Bend / Whammy assembly logic. Coverage gate can't see control-flow bugs.
- **#4** (Long): lowercase / short tokens were filtered out of the coverage snapshot until PR #43 expanded it. Even after, \`Long\` wasn't a new token — it just never had a handler in PGP's lookup table.
- **#5** (anacrusis): the literal \`\"Anacrusis\"\` **was** in gp7.py, so the coverage gate happily marked it covered. The gap was *where* it was looked for.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pytest tests/\` — **1609 passed, 0 skipped**.
- [x] Manually verified anacrusis.gp reports \`_anacrusis = True\` (was False before the fix).

## Summary
Backport of PR #884 (merged to main) to `release/v3.x`.

- `is_safe_db_activated()` previously returned `Ok(result.is_ok())`, collapsing transport, auth, HTTP 5xx, and unrelated JSON-RPC errors into `Ok(false)`. Operators saw misleading "enable SafeDB" errors when the real issue was an unreachable/unhealthy L2 node.

author: tommyk154
body:
Adds a single GitHub Actions workflow that handles both production deploys (on `main` push) and per-PR preview deploys (on PR open/sync/close). Establishes the "stable main, preview-per-PR" pattern we agreed on so you can review Claude's changes on a public URL *before* merging to main.

## What the workflow does

**`deploy-main` job** (runs only on push to `main`):
- Uses the official `actions/configure-pages` + `upload-pages-artifact` + `deploy-pages` chain.
- Publishes the repo root directory to GitHub Pages as production.

**`deploy-preview` job** (runs on every PR open / sync / close):
- Uses [`rossjrw/pr-preview-action@v1`](https://github.com/rossjrw/pr-preview-action) — battle-tested, ~1.5k stars, handles the entire preview lifecycle.
- On **open / sync**: publishes the PR head to `gh-pages` branch under `pr-preview/pr-<N>/`, comments the preview URL on the PR.
- On **close** (merged or not): cleans up the `pr-preview/pr-<N>/` subpath.

**Concurrency**: one-per-PR for preview jobs, one for main — so rapid pushes don't fight each other.

## Resulting URL layout after this merges

| URL | Serves |
|---|---|
| `https://tommyk154.github.io/test-claude-ios-vibe/` | The current `main` (what visitors see) |
| `https://tommyk154.github.io/test-claude-ios-vibe/pr-preview/pr-23/` | Live preview of open PR #23, auto-updates on every push, 404s after merge |

Production URL is never disrupted by PR activity.

## One manual step required after merging

In the repo UI: **Settings → Pages → Source: switch from "Deploy from a branch" to "GitHub Actions"**. Takes ~10 seconds. Without this, the workflow will run but GitHub Pages won't pick up its deployments.

Suggested sequence:
1. Merge PR #20 (remove session debug features) first — production auto-updates via the existing `main` deploy.
2. Merge this PR (#21).
3. Flip Pages source to "GitHub Actions" in Settings.
4. Push any trivial commit to `main` (e.g. a README typo) — confirms the new pipeline works. Production re-publishes via the workflow.
5. Next time Claude opens a PR, a preview URL appears as a PR comment ~1–2 min after push.

## Why `rossjrw/pr-preview-action` instead of writing our own

Rolling our own would require: creating / maintaining `gh-pages` branch, computing PR-number-subpaths, commenting on PRs via API, cleanup on close. That's ~150 lines of workflow YAML and edge cases. The action does all of it in one `uses:` line. If we ever outgrow it we can inline the logic — but for a 3-file static site, definitely not worth the setup cost.

## Files changed

- `.github/workflows/pages.yml` — one new file, 45 lines

## Verification (after Pages source switch)

- [ ] Push a throwaway branch with a visible change (e.g. add `console.log("preview test")` somewhere) and open a PR. Within ~2 min, a comment appears with a preview URL. Open it on phone — change is visible.
- [ ] Push another commit to the same PR → preview auto-updates.
- [ ] Close the PR without merging → preview URL 404s.
- [ ] Open a real PR, merge it → preview cleans up AND production re-deploys with the merged code.
- [ ] Production URL (`/test-claude-ios-vibe/`) is unaffected by any of the above PR activity — only updates when `main` moves.

## Rollback

Delete `.github/workflows/pages.yml` via a revert PR, flip Pages source back to "Deploy from a branch" in Settings. Production site keeps serving from `main` via the old mechanism.

body:
## Summary of Changes

`split_env_var` in `torch_rbln/_internal/tvm_libinfo.py` kept empty strings produced by separators like a trailing colon in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (`".../lib64:"` splits to `[".../lib64", ""]`). Later, `os.path.realpath("")` resolves to the current working directory and passes `os.path.isdir`, so the cwd silently becomes a `librbln.so` search directory. When the cwd happens to contain a shadow symlink to `librbln.so` (e.g. a `build/` directory that links into `.venv`), the walk picks the symlink first. Since `dlopen` evaluates `$ORIGIN` from the path it was given — not the symlink target — the library's `$ORIGIN/../rebel_compiler.libs` RPATH points at the wrong directory and the bundled `libgomp` fails to load.

Fix drops empty entries at split time.

author: firelizzard18
body:
`NodeLauncher.tryGetCompiledFile` uses the breakpoint predictor to remap a non-`.js` `program` path to its compiled output before launching. In most cases this is helpful, but it has a failure mode: if the source file appears in a source map as a *dependency* of another entry point (e.g. a bundled tool), the predictor resolves `program` to that other entry point instead of the file you specified. There is currently no way to opt out.

**[Reproduction](https://github.com/firelizzard18/vscode-js-debug-issue-2349):**

- `some-lib.mjs` contains `if (esMain(import.meta)) { ... }` for running standalone
- `some-tool.mjs` imports `some-lib.mjs` and has been compiled, producing a source map that references `some-lib.mjs` as a source
- Launch config: `"program": "${workspaceFolder}/some-lib.mjs"`
- Result: the debugger silently launches `some-tool.mjs` instead

Deleting build output doesn't help — the predictor just picks a different unrelated entry point. There is no warning or indication that remapping occurred.

This also affects projects using Node's `--experimental-strip-types` flag to run `.ts` files directly with no compilation step. In that workflow there is no compiled output, yet the predictor will still attempt remapping if any source map in the workspace references the file.

**Fix:**

Adds a `debug.javascript.resolveDebugEntrypoint` workspace setting (default `true`, preserving existing behavior). When set to `false`, `tryGetCompiledFile` returns the `program` path as-is.

```jsonc
// .vscode/settings.json
{
  "debug.javascript.resolveDebugEntrypoint": false
}
```

author: cwhitehouse
body:
## Summary

- User messages sent during workflow stages are now passed to the agent as plain text — no `<!orkestra:resume:...:user_message>` marker wrapper, no structured-output enforcement. The `ResumeType::UserMessage` arm in `build_prompt.rs` short-circuits and returns the raw message directly instead of rendering a template.
- The `ResumeMarkerType::UserMessage` enum variant and its `user_message.md` template are fully removed, shrinking the parser and prompt-builder surfaces.
- `run_async.rs` gains an `else` branch that emits `LogEntry::UserMessage` for raw (markerless) prompts, fixing a silent logging gap where user messages were never recorded in the activity log.

## Decisions

- **Raw pass-through instead of a lightweight template**: The previous design wrapped every user message in a template that instructed the agent to address the request and respond in JSON. Since user messages are conversational — not structured workflow handoffs — the template added friction without value. Returning `message.clone()` from `build_prompt` keeps the contract minimal.
- **Removing the variant, not gating on it**: `ResumeMarkerType::UserMessage` no longer exists in the type system. The parser's `"user_message"` match arm is gone; old-format markers fall through to `_ => return None`, which routes them to the new `else` branch in `run_async.rs` (graceful degradation). A future partial-parser gap (`malformed_output`, `pr_comments` markers not recognized by `parse_resume_marker`) is documented in `CLAUDE.md` rather than fixed here, since fixing it would widen scope.

## Change Walkthrough

### Affected area

The user-message path spans three crates: **orkestra-prompt** (builds the prompt string), **orkestra-agent** (spawns the agent and logs events), and **orkestra-parser** (parses the resume marker back out of the prompt for logging).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["ResumeType::UserMessage { message }"] -->|before| B["build_prompt renders user_message.md\n(marker + JSON instruction)"]
    A -->|after| C["build_prompt returns message.clone()\n(raw text, no marker)"]
    C --> D["run_async.rs\nparse_resume_marker → None\n→ else branch"]
    D --> E["LogEntry::UserMessage emitted"]
    B --> F["parse_resume_marker → Some(UserMessage)\n→ if let Some branch"]
    F --> G["LogEntry::UserMessage emitted"]
```

### File map

| File | What changed | Why |
|------|-------------|-----|
| `orkestra-prompt/src/interactions/resume/build_prompt.rs` | `UserMessage` arm returns `message.clone()` instead of rendering a template | Core simplification — no wrapper, no structured output |
| `orkestra-prompt/src/templates/resume/user_message.md` | Deleted | Template is no longer used |
| `orkestra-parser/src/types.rs` | Removed `ResumeMarkerType::UserMessage` variant and `as_str()` arm | Variant is dead; raw messages have no marker to parse |
| `orkestra-parser/src/interactions/stream/parse_resume_marker.rs` | Removed `"user_message"` match arm; updated tests to assert it returns `None` | Parser must not recognize the old format |
| `orkestra-agent/src/interactions/agent/run_async.rs` | Added `else` branch to emit `LogEntry::UserMessage` for markerless prompts | Fixes silent log gap — user messages were previously unrecorded |
| `orkestra-agent/src/mock.rs` | Updated test to verify raw prompts don't parse as markers | Test now matches the actual contract |
| `crates/orkestra-core/tests/e2e/helpers.rs` | `assert_resume_prompt_contains` skips marker assertion for `user_message` type | Helper must accept raw-text prompts in e2e tests |
| `crates/orkestra-agent/CLAUDE.md` | Documents the parser asymmetry (`malformed_output`/`pr_comments` markers not recognized) | Future maintainers need to know about the mislabeling edge case |
| `crates/orkestra-prompt/CLAUDE.md` | Updated `UserMessage` variant description | Docs reflect the new pass-through behavior |

### Key flow change in `build_prompt.rs`

```rust
// Before
ResumeType::UserMessage { message } => (
    RESUME_USER_MESSAGE,
    serde_json::json!({ "message": message }),
),
// … rendered through template engine with marker prefix

// After
ResumeType::UserMessage { message } => return Ok(message.clone()),
```

The early return bypasses the shared rendering path (which prepends `<!orkestra:resume:STAGE:TYPE>` and enforces a JSON response schema).

### Logging gap fix in `run_async.rs`

Previously, `run_async` only emitted `LogEntry::UserMessage` inside the `if let Some(marker) = parse_resume_marker(prompt)` branch. Raw prompts (no marker) fell through silently. The new `else` branch covers them:

```rust
} else {
    // Raw user message (no marker prefix) — sent directly during workflow stages.
    let _ = tx.send(RunEvent::LogLine(LogEntry::UserMessage {
        resume_type: "user_message".to_string(),
        content: prompt.clone(),
        sections: prompt_sections,
    }));
}
```

**Known asymmetry (documented, not fixed here):** The `else` branch fires for any prompt `parse_resume_marker` returns `None` on — including `malformed_output` and `pr_comments` markers that `build_prompt` emits but the parser doesn't recognize. These would be logged with `resume_type: "user_message"` (mislabeled). Production impact is nil since nothing branches on that string, but a future fix could guard with `!prompt.trim_start().starts_with("<!orkestra:")` or extend the parser.

### 3. Vercel Analytics Integration
**File Modified:** `frontend/pages/_app.js`

Added the Analytics component following the official documentation for Next.js Pages Router:

```javascript
import { Analytics } from '@vercel/analytics/react';
import '../styles/globals.css';

function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }) {
  return (
    <>
      <Component {...pageProps} />
      <Analytics />
    </>
  );
}

export default MyApp;
```

This integration enables:
- ✅ Automatic page view tracking
- ✅ User interaction monitoring
- ✅ Performance metrics collection
- ✅ Web Vitals tracking

### Package Installation
- Used `npm install` (the project's package manager)
- Package: `@vercel/analytics@1.6.1`

### Framework-Specific Configuration
- Framework: Next.js (Pages Router)
- Import Path: `@vercel/analytics/react`
- Component Placement: In the root `_app.js` file, after the page component

### Why These Choices?

1. **Pages Router vs App Router**: The project structure uses the Pages Router pattern (`pages/` directory), so I used `@vercel/analytics/react` import as specified in the official documentation.

author: rzbdz
body:
## Problem

When a user types `/model claude-sonnet-4.6` while on a custom provider (e.g. `smt-claude`), the switch fails with:

```
✗ Note: `claude-sonnet-4.6` was not found in this custom endpoint's model listing (https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models).
  Similar models: `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6`, ...
```

The session then silently falls back to the custom provider group's default model instead of switching. Three root causes:

1. **`cli.py`**: `_handle_model_switch` only loaded `custom_providers` in the picker path (no-args). When a model name was given, `switch_model` was called with `custom_providers=None`.

2. **`model_switch.py`**: No step searched the user's `custom_providers` models catalog before falling through to a live API probe. The probe could hit the wrong URL (e.g. OpenRouter) if base_url state was stale.

3. **`model_switch.py`**: The `is_custom` guard only matched `"custom"` and `"local"` exactly — not `custom:smt-claude` slugs — so `detect_provider_for_model()` could incorrectly re-route the model to OpenRouter.

4. **`models.py`**: `validate_requested_model` didn't treat `custom:*` slugs as `"custom"`, so named custom providers fell through to the generic error path.

## Fix

- **`_find_model_in_custom_providers()`** — new helper that scans every `custom_providers` entry's `models` dict/list for a matching model name. Matching is case-insensitive and normalises dots↔hyphens (`claude-sonnet-4.6` matches `claude-sonnet-4-6`).
- Inserted as **step c2** in PATH B of `switch_model()` — runs before the live API probe, so configured models always win.
- `is_custom` guard extended to cover `custom:*` slugs.
- `cli.py` loads `custom_provs` unconditionally before calling `switch_model()`.
- `validate_requested_model` normalises `custom:*` → `"custom"`.

## Testing

5 new tests in `tests/hermes_cli/test_model_switch_custom_providers.py`:
- `test_find_model_in_custom_providers_dict_format`
- `test_find_model_in_custom_providers_singular_model`
- `test_find_model_in_custom_providers_no_match`
- `test_switch_model_bare_name_resolves_via_custom_providers`
- `test_switch_model_bare_name_dot_hyphen_normalisation`

All 2440 existing tests pass (2 pre-existing failures in `test_gateway_service.py` are unrelated).

## Summary

1. **Full-session ground truth fixture** (`tests/fixtures/extraction-ground-truth-full-session.json`) — 16 expected independent characters, PC alias rules, must-not-merge pairs, coreference groups, staleness targets, location/faction coverage for turns 1-345

Run 9 had 4 false alias merges, 5 missing characters, Kael fragmented across 6 IDs, and 279-turn staleness for The Elder — all invisible to existing evaluation. Running `validate_extraction.py` against Run 9 catalogs correctly reports: **PASS: 9, WARN: 3, FAIL: 24**.

python tools/validate_extraction.py --catalog-dir framework-local/catalogs

1.  **CMake Upgrade**: The minimum required version is bumped to 3.18 to support modern features and policies.
2.  **Modern FindOpenSSL**: Replaced manual path configurations with `find_package(OpenSSL REQUIRED)` and updated target linking to use `OpenSSL::SSL` and `OpenSSL::Crypto` imported targets. This ensures better cross-platform compatibility and adherence to modern CMake best practices.
3.  **Cleanup**: Removed the bundled `OpenSSL_1_1_0` directory and all its references in `CMakeLists.txt`, `.travis.yml`, and `update_cmake.py`.
4.  **CI Update**: Updated the Travis configuration to install `libssl-dev` from the system package manager instead of building OpenSSL from source.

The build was verified on Linux using GCC 13.3.0 and OpenSSL 3.0.13.

💡 What: Optimized `TeacherController` by eager loading student counts for assigned class sections using `withCount('students')` on the `classSection` relationship.

author: proofofprints
body:
Three focused improvements. `main` jumps from v1.0.12 → v1.0.14 in one merge; `versionCode 13 → 15`.

## Fixed

### Landscape orientation
Rotating the phone hid the **START MINING** button below a non-scrolling viewport with no way to reach it. The dashboard used `Modifier.fillMaxSize` without `verticalScroll` because `Spacer(Modifier.weight(1f))` — the weighted spacer that pushes the button toward the bottom in portrait — only works inside a bounded-height parent. Now orientation-aware: portrait keeps the existing weighted layout; landscape switches to a scrollable column with the weighted spacer omitted.

### Locale-safe numeric formatting
`String.format("%.2f …")` uses the JVM's default Locale. On French/German/Italian/Spanish/Dutch/etc. systems that renders `1,52 MH/s` instead of `1.52 MH/s`. Every user-visible numeric format now passes `Locale.US` explicitly — `formatHashrate`, `formatHashes`, the DIFF string, the foreground-notification text, and the APK size in the update dialog. Hex formats used internally by the stratum/mining code are integer-only and locale-safe already.

## Changed

### Thermal status uses the OS's bucket directly
On Android 10+ (API 29+), `PowerManager.getCurrentThermalStatus()` returns `NONE`/`LIGHT`/`MODERATE`/`SEVERE`/`CRITICAL`/`EMERGENCY`/`SHUTDOWN`. Previously we converted that to a synthetic CPU temperature and ran it back through our fixed 45/50/55°C thresholds — a lossy round-trip. Now the OS bucket maps directly onto our `NORMAL`/`WARNING`/`THROTTLE`/`CRITICAL` state.

### TEMP card falls back to battery temperature
On phones where `/sys/class/thermal/` is locked down (common on retail Android where OEMs restrict sensor access), the TEMP card used to show `--`. It now falls back to battery temperature from `ACTION_BATTERY_CHANGED`'s `EXTRA_TEMPERATURE`. Battery sits next to the SoC on every phone so its temperature is a decent proxy during mining.

### BATTERY percent fallback
Falls back to `EXTRA_LEVEL / EXTRA_SCALE` when `BatteryManager.BATTERY_PROPERTY_CAPACITY` returns −1 or 0 (some OEMs don't implement the newer API reliably). BATTERY should now read correctly on every Android device.

## Test plan

- [ ] Portrait: dashboard unchanged — hashrate centered, button near bottom, no scroll
- [ ] Landscape: dashboard is scrollable, START MINING reachable
- [ ] Numeric rendering uses period decimal on a device with non-US locale (System → Languages → add French)
- [ ] Phone where TEMP previously showed `--` now shows a number (battery temp fallback)
- [ ] Phone where BATTERY previously read 0 now shows a real percentage (EXTRA_LEVEL/SCALE fallback)
- [ ] THERMAL card reflects the OS's thermal bucket as the device warms up from mining

author: copilot
body:
`flusort` stores partial subtype patterns directly in the DB (`H1xx`, `xxN1`, `H3xx`, `xxN2`). The download filter used an exact `=` match against the normalized value (`H1N1`), silently missing every record stored with a partial pattern.

## Changes

- **SQL filter**: replaced `subtype='H1N1'` with `subtype IN ('H1N1', 'H1xx', 'xxN1')` so partial and complete patterns are all matched in one pass
- **Grouping**: replaced flat `subtypes` list + `set()` loop with a `defaultdict` that groups each raw pattern under its normalized subtype, then iterates over those groups to build the `IN` clause
- **`raw_subtypes`**: added complete subtypes (`H1N1`, `H3N2`) to cover records uploaded from non-flusort sources that are already fully typed
- **`normalize_subtype`**: replaced loose `or`-based substring checks with explicit set membership — prevents ambiguous patterns like `H3N1` from silently mapping to `H1N1`

```python
# Before — misses 'H1xx' and 'xxN1' records in DB
"--filters", f"subtype='{subtype}'"   # subtype='H1N1'

# After — matches all partial and complete variants
in_values = ", ".join(f"'{p}'" for p in raw_patterns)
"--filters", f"subtype IN ({in_values})"  # subtype IN ('H1N1', 'H1xx', 'xxN1')
```

## 💡 What:
Fixed broken table alignment in the CLI output summary when text contains ANSI color codes.

## 🎯 Why:
The `text/tabwriter` package counts all bytes as visible characters, including ANSI escape sequences used for coloring text. This causes column widths to be calculated incorrectly, breaking the visual alignment of the tables. By enabling `tabwriter.StripEscape` and wrapping escape codes in `\xff`, the tabwriter ignores them during calculation, making the table layout correct.

## ♿ Accessibility/UX:
Fixes terminal layout alignment to be visually organized, which significantly improves readability for users viewing security reports.

author: bokelley
body:
Closes #2755. Part of epic #2693.

## Summary

Slack Addie's tool-call rate is naturally bounded by Slack's API ceiling. The web chat isn't — a logged-in member can script tool invocations at machine speed from the dashboard. The function-level limiter inside `proposeContentForUser` (#2767) bounds the submission path, but other externally-facing tools could still burn Google Docs API quota, bandwidth on attachment fetches, or Gemini credits.

This PR adds per-user + per-tool + global caps at the handler layer.

## What's new

**`server/src/addie/mcp/tool-rate-limiter.ts`** — in-process sliding-window tracker with two helpers:
- `checkToolRateLimit(tool, userId)` — boolean gate you call inline from a handler
- `withToolRateLimit(tool, userId, handler)` — higher-order wrapper that returns a user-facing rate-limit string when the cap trips (LLM surfaces it, no thrown error)

**Caps:**
| Tool | Window | Max |
|---|---|---|
| `read_google_doc` | 10 min | 20 |
| `attach_content_asset` | 10 min | 20 |
| `generate_perspective_illustration` | 10 min | 10 |
| default (unknown tools) | 10 min | 60 |
| **global across all tools per user** | 10 min | 200 |

`system:*` users (newsletter pipeline, digest publisher) are exempt — they legitimately run on a cadence.

## Wiring

- **`createGoogleDocsToolHandlers(userId)`** gained an optional `userId` parameter. Called per-request from `createUserScopedTools` in both `handler.ts` (web) and `bolt-app.ts` (Slack). The per-request handler shadows the boot-time baseline via `claude-client`'s `allHandlers` merge — so when we have a user id, rate limits apply; when we don't (internal jobs, background tasks), they skip.
- **`attach_content_asset`** handler inlines `checkToolRateLimit` before the URL fetch begins.
- **Error path** returns a plain string message ("Rate limit exceeded on read_google_doc. Try again in ~N seconds.") so Sonnet surfaces it to the user instead of throwing and losing context.

## Tests

12 unit cases in `tool-rate-limiter.test.ts` cover:
- Per-tool caps (generate_perspective_illustration at 10 → 11th blocked)
- Global cap (4 tools × 50 = 200 → 201st blocked with scope='global')
- User isolation (Alpha hits wall, Bravo unaffected)
- Tool isolation within user (illustration at cap, read_google_doc still available)
- `system:*` users exempt (100 calls succeed)
- Null/undefined userId skips the limiter
- Default cap applies to unknown tools
- `withToolRateLimit` surfaces user-facing messages and scope ('per_tool' vs 'global')

Typecheck clean; 1711 unit tests pass.

## Related follow-up

**#2783** — `generate_perspective_illustration` is exported but never registered in `handler.ts` or `bolt-app.ts`. Sonnet sees it in the prompt but can't actually call it. Rate-limit cap at 10/10min waits for that wiring. Surfaced while working on this PR.

## Epic #2693 status after this lands

**Shipped:** #2709, #2701 (→#2726), #2703 (→#2744), #2700+#2702 (→#2764), #2699+#2719+#2734 (→#2766), #2712+#2713+#2733 (→#2767), #2752+#2753+#2754+#2756 (→#2772), **#2755 (this PR)**.

**Remaining:**
- #2735 — channel privacy TOCTOU recheck (needs caching design)
- #2736 — interactive Slack approve/reject DMs (Bolt handler refactor)
- #2782 — wrap body in `<untrusted_proposer_input>` tags when replayed to reviewer LLM
- #2783 — register `generate_perspective_illustration` (surfaced in this PR)

body: ## Summary This PR enhances the AI service's Server-Sent Events (SSE) parsing and adds robust sanitization of AI-generated command suggestions to handle various formatting styles and edge cases. ## Key Changes ### SSE Parsing Improvements (`model/ai_service.go`) - Introduced `stripSSEField()` helper function that properly parses SSE field values according to the SSE specification, handling optional leading spaces - Refactored SSE event parsing to use the new helper, improving robustness for both `event:` and `data:` fields - Fixed event error state management: errors are now properly reset on blank lines between events, preventing false error propagation - Improved handling of `[DONE]` markers with or without leading spaces ### Command Sanitization (`commands/query.go`) - Added `sanitizeSuggestedCommand()` function that normalizes raw AI output into executable commands - Handles triple-backtick code fences with optional language tags (bash, sh, shell, zsh, fish, pwsh, powershell) - Strips single backticks for single-line responses - Preserves comment-style refusals (lines starting with `#`) verbatim for user visibility - Trims surrounding whitespace while preserving intentional spacing in multi-line commands - Added validation to reject empty AI responses with user-friendly error messaging ### Test Coverage - Added comprehensive SSE parsing tests (`TestQueryCommandStream_SSEParsing`) covering: - Various `[DONE]` marker formats - Multi-token streams with mixed spacing - Error event handling with and without spaces - Event state reset between messages - Added unit tests for `stripSSEField()` helper function - Added extensive tests for `sanitizeSuggestedCommand()` covering: - Code fence removal with various language tags - Single backtick stripping - Whitespace handling - Comment preservation - Edge cases (empty input, multiline without fences) - Updated existing empty response test to expect error instead of success ## Notable Implementation Details - SSE field parsing now strictly follows the specification for space handling - Error state is properly scoped to individual events (reset on blank lines) - Command sanitization is defensive and handles multiple formatting styles that AI models might produce - body:
## Brief

- **Agent:** Agent 2 — Form Engine Architect
- **Phase:** n/a — post-Phase-2 hardening pass (no phase number per `docs/agent-workflow.md`)
- **Closes:** the `loadCoreFields` hard-blocker added to `KNOWN_GAPS.md` in PR #39

## What this PR ships

Two follow-ups Phase 2 teed up:

1. **`loadCoreFields` registry fix** — closes the kebab/snake latent bug. Every registered module now resolves at runtime, not just the single-word ones.
2. **`requireAdmin` consolidation** — Seam 1 (editor) and Seam 2 (option lists) each shipped a local copy to stay merge-order-independent; collapsed to one source of truth in `lib/admin/require-admin.ts`.

Both were low-dependency work unblocked only by Phase 2 being fully merged. No new features, no DB migrations.

## Files

- **`lib/admin/require-admin.ts`** — adds `requireAdmin` alongside the existing `requireAdminControlCenterAdmin`. Same underlying `has_module_access('admin_control_center', 'admin')` check; different return shape (result union vs. `notFound()` throw) for different callers (server actions vs. route segments).
- **`lib/forms/editor.ts`** — drops 10 lines of local `requireAdmin`; imports from `@/lib/admin/require-admin`.
- **`lib/admin/option-lists.ts`** — drops 13 lines of local `requireAdmin`; imports from `@/lib/admin/require-admin`. Existing `await requireAdmin(supabase)` call sites unchanged — the new signature takes an optional client.
- **`lib/forms/load-core-fields.ts`** — rewrites path resolution. Consumes `getRegistryForm(moduleSlug, formType).coreFieldsPath`, parses into `(moduleDir, formTypeDir?)` segments, dynamic-imports with two distinct template literal shapes so webpack builds the right chunk manifest.
- **`tests/unit/forms/load-core-fields.test.ts`** — 10 new assertions: unknown slug / unknown form_type / mismatched form_type arity errors, plus happy-path resolution for every registered entry including `air_quality` (multi-word) and all four `ice_maintenance` form types (both levels of kebab-snake mismatch).
- **`KNOWN_GAPS.md`** — strikes through the `loadCoreFields` entry with resolution pointer.

## Why the registry approach, and not renaming directories

The alternative would be renaming `app/modules/ice-maintenance/` → `ice_maintenance/` and `air-quality/` → `air_quality/` so slug = directory. That's a larger-surface change affecting import paths in Agent 3/4 modules, E2E tests, route URLs, and the existing `loadCoreFields` template itself. The registry approach is strictly more general: the on-disk directory name is no longer coupled to the DB slug, so future modules can evolve their filesystem layout without DB migrations.

## The Vite warning

Running the new unit tests surfaces two Vite warnings from `vite:dynamic-import-vars`:

```
invalid import "../../app/modules/${moduleDir}/${formTypeDir}/core-fields".
A file extension must be included in the static part of the import.
```

Non-fatal — the imports resolve and the tests pass. The same pattern existed in the pre-hardening `loadCoreFields` (same template-literal shape, just with `moduleSlug` instead of `moduleDir` as the variable). Next.js webpack handles template-literal dynamic imports with implicit `.ts/.tsx` extensions; Vite's plugin is conservative and prefers explicit extensions. Tests are green; production build behavior is unchanged.

## Breaking changes to prior agents

None. All existing call sites work unchanged. `lib/forms/submission-tables.ts` is still the Seam 3 re-export shim — nothing there moved.

- `npm run typecheck` — clean
- `npm run test:unit` — **105/105 pass** (10 new)

- `scripts/check-client-facility-id.sh` — clean

Dylan Guo ([dylanlg3@illinois.edu](mailto:dylanlg3@illinois.edu))

A Case Study Exploring the Current Landscape of Synthetic Medical Record Generation with Commercial LLMs (https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.14657)

New Task Contribution

This PR adds a task as described by Lin, Yu, and Lee in A Case Study Exploring the Current Landscape of Synthetic Medical Record Generation with Commercial LLMs that predicts the mortality of patients based on patient features from the eICU database. body:
Fixes #

## Proposed changes
* **Wrapper visibility** — `state.showLoadMore` now ANDs in `! state.isLoading`, so the load-more block collapses during a first-page fetch (new query, sort change, deep link). Previously the previous query's `pageHandle` flashed a "Load more" button against results that no longer matched until the new response arrived.
* **Button vs. spinner** — `jetpack/load-more`'s button now binds `data-wp-bind--hidden` to `state.isLoadingMore` instead of `data-wp-bind--disabled`. While paginating, the wrapper stays in flow; the button disappears and the adjacent "Loading…" spinner takes its place — matching the UX for a loading-next-page action.

Both paths leave `isLoadingMore` (pagination) orthogonal to `isLoading` (first-page fetch).

This is a pure polish / bug-fix PR against the Phase 1 Interactivity API foundation (#48198). Split out from #48227 so it can land independently of the Phase 2 filter-blocks work.

n/a

## Summary

- New `GET /v1/slack/install/callback` endpoint — receives the OAuth redirect when a workspace admin installs the Aileron Slack app from the App Directory
- Exchanges the authorization code for a bot token (`xoxb-...`) via Slack's `oauth.v2.access`
- Stores the bot token in the system vault (ADR-0020) at `slack-workspaces/{team_id}/bot-token`, encrypted at rest

body:
Local-first create / edit / delete of non-recurring events on the user's primary Google Calendar.

## Backend
- **Schema**: `calendar_events` gains `local_dirty`, `pending_op`, `mutation_id`, `last_push_error`, `last_push_attempt_at`, `conflict_payload` + 2 indexes (migration 0005).
- **Google client**: `insertEvent`/`patchEvent`/`deleteEvent`/`findByMutationId` + `EtagMismatchError`/`GoneError`/`InsufficientScopeError`.
- **Write engine** (`apps/api/src/calendar/write.ts`): local mutations with state-collapse rules (create+delete drops, create+update stays create, existing+delete tombstones). `pushPendingForAccount` pushes queued ops. CREATE retries probe `findByMutationId` first to avoid duplicates after lost responses.
- **Sync** reconciles incoming events by mutationId (provisional `local:*` → real id), skips `localDirty` rows, filters pending-delete tombstones from reads, and pushes before reading each tick.
- **Routes**: scope bumped to `calendar.events`; `canWrite` on accounts; `POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/calendar/events` + `POST /api/calendar/events/:id/discard-conflict`. Returns 409 on etag conflict, 403 on missing scope / non-primary / recurring edit.

## Web
- "+ New event" button in the Calendar header (when user has write scope).
- Click-to-edit on user-owned non-recurring events; read-only links otherwise.
- `syncing`/`conflict` badges on chips; conflict rows highlighted.
- Reconnect-Google banner when stored scope lacks `calendar.events`.

## Out of scope
Recurring edits, attendees, reminders, ACL, free/busy — kept as read-only.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
Under `ExecutionMode.PER_NODE` + `TestStrategy.IMMEDIATE`, any model that received a scheduling-only test-edge from `_augment_immediate_test_edges()` was never persisted to `.execution_state.json` and always re-executed — it never returned `"cached"` on an identical second run.

This PR restores caching for those models by using the canonical executable-node DAG for cache-key construction while preserving the augmented DAG for scheduling and failure propagation.

<details>
<summary>Root cause</summary>

- `_augment_immediate_test_edges()` adds implicit edges from downstream models to upstream tests so test failures can block those models. The augmented `DbtNode` objects flow through `phases` into `_execute_per_node`.
- Test nodes are excluded from caching by default (`CacheConfig.exclude_resource_types` includes `NodeType.Test`), so they never get cache keys recorded in `computed_cache_keys`. They are also not part of `all_executable_nodes`, so they never get entries in `precomputed_cache_keys` either.
- `_build_cache_options_for_node()` iterated the scheduled node's `depends_on` literally. For a model with an injected test edge it saw an upstream with no cache key, logged `"Disabling cache for %s: upstream %s has no cache key"`, and returned `{}`.
- Without a cache policy, `computed_cache_keys[node.unique_id]` was never populated, so `execution_state[node_id]` was never written in `_process_future_result`. The model executed successfully but never surfaced as `"cached"` on a second run.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Fix</summary>

Pass `all_executable_nodes` (already available in `_execute_per_node`) through to `_build_cache_options_for_node`. When a canonical executable-node exists for `node.unique_id`, iterate its `depends_on` (which never contains scheduling-only test edges) instead of the augmented node's `depends_on`. The augmented node is still used everywhere else for scheduling and for failure propagation — no public API change, no change to PER_WAVE behavior.

Preserved unchanged:
- IMMEDIATE test-edge augmentation for scheduling and failure propagation
- Tests excluded from caching by default
- Selective runs and upstream salting for unexecuted dependencies
- Failure clearing from execution state
- Default exclusion of tests/snapshots from caching

</details>

### Regression coverage

`TestImmediateTestStrategyCaching::test_all_models_cached_on_identical_second_run` in `tests/core/test_orchestrator_cache.py`:

- `ExecutionMode.PER_NODE` + `TestStrategy.IMMEDIATE`
- `root -> mid -> leaf` with `test_not_null_root_id` on `root`. Under IMMEDIATE the scheduling DAG places `mid` after the test (injected edge) and `leaf` in a downstream all-model wave.
- Asserts `.execution_state.json` contains an entry for every successful model node after the first `run_build()`.
- Asserts every model node is `"cached"` on the identical second `run_build()`.
- Verified failing on `main` (missing entry for `mid`) and passing with the fix.

### Tests run

From `src/integrations/prefect-dbt/`:

```
uv run pytest tests/core/test_orchestrator_cache.py \
              tests/core/test_orchestrator_test_strategies.py \
              tests/core/test_orchestrator_per_node.py -x -q
```

author: cccoo770668305-gif
body:
💡 What: Replaced manual iterative read/write loops in `Stream::save` and `SeekableStream::toMemoryStream` with the native PHP function `stream_copy_to_stream`. Improved resource management in `Stream::save` and added necessary `rewind()` in `toMemoryStream`.

🎯 Why: Manual byte-by-byte or small-chunk loops are extremely slow in PHP due to high function call overhead. `stream_copy_to_stream` is implemented in C and uses internal 8KB buffering, providing massive speedups.

📊 Impact:
- `Stream::save`: Execution time for a 1MB file reduced from ~1.85s to ~0.015s.
- `SeekableStream::toMemoryStream`: Execution time for 100 iterations of 1MB copies reduced from ~0.21s to ~0.03s (approx. 7x speedup).

🔬 Measurement: Verified with benchmark scripts measuring execution time for both methods before and after the optimization. Correctness confirmed by running the existing PHPUnit test suite (`composer tests`).

author: erfanmnm
body:
### Motivation
- Align CameraSub V2 PLC synchronization with a revised PLC behavior where `CurrentID` represents the currently processed bottle and status changes occur on the same ID rather than after an ID increment.
- Allow separate polling and exit timeout configuration for the V2 polling flow to tune responsiveness independently from the legacy V1 settings.
- Improve application behavior and logging when the PLC advances to a different ID before the expected status change. 

### Description
- Added two new configuration properties `CameraSub_V2_Polling_Exit_Ms` and `CameraSub_V2_Polling_Delay_Ms` to `IniConfigs` with default values wired in `SetDefault` to enable separate V2 polling timeout and delay settings. 
- Changed PLC sync logic in `CameraSubPlcSyncV2Helper.WaitAndResolve` to treat the expected ID as the current snapshot ID (`expectedId = previousId`) and monitor status changes on that ID instead of waiting for an ID increment. 
- Simplified handling for the case when PLC `CurrentId` advances past the expected ID by returning `NoResponse` with a clear message instead of attempting history lookups. 
- Updated `FDashboard` to pick V2-specific polling and exit timeout values when available, and to distinguish `NoResponse` from `Timeout` by treating `NoResponse` as an application `Error` (with specific logging) while `Timeout` still maps to a `Timeout` result. 

### Testing
- Built the solution with `dotnet build` and the build completed successfully. 
- Executed `dotnet test` to run available test suites and no tests were discovered to run in this repository (test command completed without errors).

Revoked X/Y links. Note: already-opened links cannot be revoked.

## Summary
- `better-sqlite3` was being inlined into `apps/dm-tool/out/main/index.js` by Rollup, causing the `bindings` loader to fail at runtime with `the app could not dynamically require better_sqlite3`.
- Root cause: `externalizeDepsPlugin` only externalizes packages in dm-tool's own `dependencies`. `better-sqlite3` lives in `packages/db`'s deps, and `@foundry-toolkit/db` is in `workspaceBundled` — so the native-module require got bundled too.
- Fix: pass `include: ['better-sqlite3']` to the `externalizeDepsPlugin` for the main process so the require survives bundling and Electron can resolve the `.node` binary at runtime.

body:
Image attachments marked as video were opening externally in Safari instead of playing inside `ImageViewer`. Cache entries also had no expiry path, allowing stale disk cache to persist across app restarts/background-return scenarios.

- **Inline video playback in `ImageViewer`**
  - Replaced external URL handoff with embedded `AVKit.VideoPlayer` playback in the viewer.
  - Added player setup/reset lifecycle handling when navigating attachments and dismissing the viewer.
  - Preserved fallback UI (thumbnail + play icon) when a playable URL is unavailable.

- **Cache expiration model in `CacheManager`**
  - Introduced max-age policy (`defaultMaxCacheAge`) and expiration checks on cache reads.
  - Added maintenance API to sweep expired disk entries (`removeExpiredEntries`) and explicit memory eviction (`clearMemoryCache`).
  - Hardened expiry behavior so unreadable file metadata is treated as expired for eventual cleanup.

- **Lifecycle-triggered cache maintenance**
  - Wired app lifecycle hooks to run cache maintenance:
    - on app appearance
    - on return to active after meaningful background inactivity
  - Runs cleanup in utility-priority tasks to avoid blocking foreground UI work.

- **Targeted test coverage updates**
  - Extended `CacheManagerTests` to cover stale-entry invalidation on read and expired-entry pruning during maintenance.

```swift
if attachment.isVideo {
    configureVideoPlayer(for: attachment)   // AVPlayer(url:)
    return
}

// Cleanup on lifecycle transitions
Task(priority: .utility) {
    cacheManager.clearMemoryCache()
    cacheManager.removeExpiredEntries()
}
```

author: jeff-h
body:
## Summary

Adds \`secret::keyfile_hash\`, the missing piece between \"user hands us a \`.key\` file on disk\" and \`CompositeKey::from_password_and_keyfile_hash\`.

The reduction follows KeePass's strictly-length-first, then content-sniffed dispatch:

1. **Exactly 32 bytes** → used verbatim
2. **Exactly 64 ASCII hex digits** → parsed as 32 bytes
3. **XML keyfile (v1 or v2)** → clean \`KeyFileError::XmlKeyFileNotSupported\`
4. **Anything else** → SHA-256 of the whole file

Case 3 returns a typed error rather than silently falling through to case 4. An XML keyfile hashed under the \"unknown bytes\" rule would produce a wrong hash and a misleading \"wrong password\" error downstream. Wiring the XML formats is a follow-up PR.

The XML detection is a small heuristic (UTF-8 BOM strip + leading-whitespace skip, looks for \`<?xml\` or \`<KeyFile\`) — a real XML parser would be overkill purely to reject a format we haven't plumbed yet.

### Tests

**7 new unit tests** cover each case: exact-32, hex decode (lowercase and uppercase), 64 non-hex bytes falling through to SHA-256, arbitrary lengths (0, 1, 31, 33, 63, 65, 128, 4096), XML keyfile rejection, and an XML keyfile preceded by a UTF-8 BOM + whitespace (still detected).

**Integration:** \`tests/kdbx_unlock.rs\` no longer skips fixtures with a keyfile. \`keepassxc/kdbx3-keyfile.kdbx\` (128-byte raw keyfile → case 4) now unlocks end-to-end. All 12 valid fixtures pass; the test function is renamed accordingly.

Also fixes a latent bug in the sidecar JSON reader used by the integration test: a JSON \`null\` value no longer gets read as the string in the NEXT sidecar field.

author: pwelter34
body:
## Summary
This PR adds comprehensive decorator registration support to Injectio, allowing services to be wrapped with decorators without runtime dependencies. The implementation includes a new `RegisterDecorator` attribute, compile-time diagnostics for decorator validation, and code generation for decorator application.

## Key Changes

- **New `RegisterDecorator` Attribute**: Added `RegisterDecoratorAttribute` to mark classes as decorators for existing services, supporting:
  - Generic and non-generic service type specification
  - Keyed service decoration (with specific keys or `AnyKey`)
  - Custom factory methods for decorator instantiation
  - Decorator ordering via `Order` property
  - Tag-based filtering
  - Open generic service decoration

- **Compile-Time Validation**: Extended `ServiceRegistrationAnalyzer` with decorator-specific diagnostics:
  - INJ0010: Decorator does not implement service type
  - INJ0011: Missing service type specification
  - INJ0012: Missing inner service constructor parameter
  - INJ0013: Factory method not found
  - INJ0014: Factory method has invalid signature
  - INJ0015: Open-generic + keyed combination (unsupported)
  - INJ0016: Decorated service not registered (when no dynamic modules present)

- **Code Generation**: 
  - Extended `ServiceRegistrationWriter` to generate decorator registration calls
  - Added `GenerateDecorationHelper()` to emit decoration extension methods (`Decorate<T>`, `DecorateKeyed<T>`, `DecorateOpenGeneric`)
  - Decorators are applied in order and inherit the lifetime of the decorated service
  - Support for both automatic instantiation via `ActivatorUtilities` and custom factory methods

- **Analyzer Enhancement**: Implemented `AnalyzeCompilation` to perform cross-symbol analysis:
  - Collects all decorator registrations and registered service types
  - Validates decorator constraints at compilation end
  - Detects unregistered service targets (when no dynamic modules exist)

- **Test Coverage**: Added comprehensive test suite (`ServiceRegistrationDecoratorTests`) with:
  - Simple decorator registration
  - Generic attribute syntax
  - Chained decorators with ordering
  - Keyed service decoration
  - AnyKey decoration
  - Custom factory methods
  - Open generic decorators
  - Tag-based filtering
  - All diagnostic scenarios

## Notable Implementation Details

- Decorators use a thread-safe collection pattern with locks during compilation analysis
- The decoration helper is only emitted when decorators are present
- Decorator ordering is deterministic (by service type, order value, then decorator type name)
- Open generic + keyed combination is explicitly rejected as unsupported
- Unregistered service detection only applies when no service modules could dynamically register services

body:
## Summary

- **Issue 1 — ML rolling feature noise fix:** Added `min_games_threshold=10` to `MLBDataPipeline` to exclude training games where either team has played fewer than 10 prior games. Games in this window have NaN rolling features (win %, runs scored/allowed) that were silently filled with `0.0` — injecting a false "team with 0% win rate" signal into early-season training data. Setting the threshold equal to the rolling window size ensures all rolling features are fully populated before a game is included. Model v2.1: 54.57% accuracy (vs v2.0: 53.8%, v1.0: 59.1%).

- **Issue 2 — Docker → Homebrew PostgreSQL migration:** Migrated local development database from Docker (postgres:16.2) to native Homebrew postgresql@14 on port 5432. Dumped 5,491-game dataset via `pg_dump` inside the Docker container and restored into the native instance. Updated `api/.env` and `alembic.ini` connection strings. Rewrote `schedule_updates.sh` to check Homebrew PostgreSQL directly — no Docker dependency. `docker-compose.yml` retained for CI and onboarding.

author: mkhomutov
body:
## Summary

RFC 0017 (Persona Memory Injection Token Budget) has merged 7/7 PRs and is closed. The two
behaviours it introduces — the per-event token budget and the empty-context TICK short-circuit —
have full automated coverage but no manual test documents. This PR adds the missing manual tests
so operators have a runbook to verify the behaviour against a live agent.

## Changes

- **`docs/manual-tests/MT-MEMORY-004.md`** — Memory injection token budget: per-event bound holds
  (RFC 0017 [§B](../docs/rfcs/0017-persona-memory-injection-budget.md#b-memory-budget-allocator)).
  Library-level test driving `MemoryBudget` directly. Three steps: greedy admission with overflow
  drop, `min_tokens` floor enforcement, and empty-input handling. No `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` needed.
- **`docs/manual-tests/MT-PERSONA-003.md`** — Empty-context TICK short-circuit suppresses LLM
  calls (RFC 0017 [§F](../docs/rfcs/0017-persona-memory-injection-budget.md#f-empty-context-tick-short-circuit)).
  Live-agent test verifying `empty_context_tick` DEBUG log emission, zero outbound LLM HTTP calls
  during the suppression window, and `TickScheduler` idle-skip engagement after 10
  short-circuited ticks. `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is **not** required for the core flow because the
  short-circuit fires before any LLM call (Step 6, the wake-up check, optionally uses one).
- **`docs/manual-tests/README.md`** — index updated with both new entries under their respective
  feature areas.

## Why these two

RFC 0017's own [Test Strategy](../docs/rfcs/0017-persona-memory-injection-budget.md#test-strategy)
explicitly calls out a manual smoke-test for the token bound but no `MT-` document existed for
it. The TICK short-circuit cost-drain fix (~$0.01 per cold-loaded idle agent at fleet scale) is
not covered by any existing persona MT — `MT-PERSONA-001` only verifies that ticks fire and that
`TickScheduler` reaches its idle state after `idle_after_ticks * interval` seconds, not that the
short-circuit suppresses the cost-drain window inside that interval.

## Validation

- `pre-commit` ran clean: 7/7 checks pass (filemap regenerated, ruff/cargo fmt/doc links/doc
  status/file size all green).
- Both new MT files conform to `docs/templates/MANUAL_TEST_TEMPLATE.md`.
- README index updated; MT IDs `MT-MEMORY-004` and `MT-PERSONA-003` are unused elsewhere in the
  index.

## Out of scope

- Executing the new manual tests. They will be run as part of the v0.2.2 release pass and
  recorded in the upcoming `v0.2.2-execution-report.md`.
- RFC / ROADMAP status changes — RFC 0017 is already closed.
