author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation
The server warmup encounters an error in forward_decode when --disable-cuda-graph is enabled. The root cause is the redundant padding tokens in the input tensor, which leads to a dimension mismatch for the NPU fused attention operator.
```
File "/xxx/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/attention/ascend_backend.py", line 1846, in forward_decode
attn_output, _ = torch.ops.npu.npu_fused_infer_attention_score(
```

## Modification

Fix the padding logic in forward_decode for the NPU attention backend:

- Crop the query tensor to remove redundant padding tokens before calling the NPU fused attention operator
- Run the fused attention operator with the valid tensor
- Pad zeros back to restore the original tensor shape after the operator computation

## Summary
- Add `vercel.json` with `"outputDirectory": "."` so Vercel publishes the repo root, not just `public/`

## Why
Production was 404ing on every page even after flattening the site into the repo root. Build logs on deploy `dpl_DZQ4s633m` show `"Skipping cache upload because no files were prepared"` — meaning nothing was actually published.

Cause: on "Other" (no-framework) projects, Vercel auto-selects `public/` as the output directory when it exists. Our `public/` holds ~100 images but no HTML, so only images shipped and every route hit `/index.html` → 404.

Pinning `outputDirectory: "."` overrides that detection and serves the full repo root, so `index.html`, `captain.html`, `trips.html`, `contact.html`, and `css/style.css` are all published alongside `public/`.

author: ponderingdemocritus
body:
## Summary

- Catalog bump: `@dojoengine/*` 1.7.0-preview.3 → aligned 1.8.x line; `starknet` `^8.5.2` → `^8.9.2`. Drop-in rebuild of every catalog-consuming package and app.
- Adapt to upstream API shifts (Query.world_addresses, onEntityUpdated/onEventMessageUpdated signatures, DojoProvider generic, deltas-only subscriptions, createDojoConfig manifest overwrite).
- Refactor `packages/provider`'s l2_gas headroom logic — drop the accidental +50% double-pad, switch to `ETransactionVersion.V3`, rename the helper to clamp-only.
- Patch `@dojoengine/utils@1.8.4` to drop the `addAddressPadding` wrapper in `getEntityIdFromKeys` — it was breaking every entity-component lookup whose hash had leading zeros (including `WORLD_CONFIG_ID`, which broke `map_center_offset`, `FELT_CENTER`, and all coordinate normalization).

## Notable upstream issues surfaced

1. **`createDojoConfig` ABI overwrite** — `@dojoengine/core@1.8.8` rebuilds `world.abi` as `manifest.abis`. PM manifests only carry `world.abi`, so the overwrite wiped the ABI and `DojoProvider` crashed with *Unable to determine Cairo version*. Worked around in `pm/hooks/dojo/dojo-config.tsx` by pre-populating `abis` so the upstream rebuild is a no-op. Worth filing upstream.

2. **Subscriptions are deltas-only** — `onEntityUpdated` no longer flushes initial state (it did in 1.7). Eternum's readiness gate waited forever for a subscription callback that wouldn't fire on a quiet world. Adjusted `markSubscriptionsReady` to also unblock readiness; initial state still arrives via the explicit `getEntities` calls in `initialSync`.

3. **`getEntityIdFromKeys` over-pads** — `@dojoengine/utils@1.8.4` wraps its hash in `addAddressPadding` (64 hex chars), but Torii 1.8 stores `hashed_keys` without leading-zero padding. Patched in `patches/@dojoengine__utils@1.8.4.patch` to drop the pad. Worth filing upstream.

4. **`getConfigFromTorii` cache short-circuit** — assumed the global subscription would re-deliver config on reload; that assumption broke with deltas-only subscriptions. Removed the short-circuit so RECS is populated before `configManager.setDojo` runs.

## Provider refactor

`packages/provider/src/index.ts`:
- Drop `V3_L2_GAS_OVERHEAD_PERCENT` and `HUNDRED_PERCENT` — `Account.estimateInvokeFee` already applies the global 50% overhead via starknet's transitive `toOverheadResourceBounds` call. The local +50% on top was producing ~2.25× raw, almost certainly accidental.
- Rename `withL2GasHeadroom` → `withL2GasCeiling`; body simplifies to a clamp at `MAX_V3_L2_GAS_MAX_AMOUNT`.
- `{ version: 3 }` → `{ version: ETransactionVersion.V3 }` (typed).

Test file (`execute-and-check-transaction.l2-gas.test.ts`):
- Ceiling test now uses a ceiling-exceeding input (`1_500_000_000n` → `1_200_000_000n`).
- New pass-through regression test: `500_000_000n` → `500_000_000n` (proves no stray multiplication, no stray truncation).
- `version` assertions migrated to `ETransactionVersion.V3`.
- All 40 tests pass (was 39).

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm install` clean; lockfile resolves to `starknet@8.9.2` only (plus deprecated `heavy-load`'s `6.11.0`).
- [x] `pnpm run build:packages` — all 8 packages build (types, amm-sdk, ammv2-sdk, torii, provider, dojo, core, react).
- [x] `pnpm --dir ./client/apps/game typecheck` green.
- [x] `pnpm --dir ./client/apps/eternum-mobile typecheck` green.
- [x] `pnpm --dir ./client/apps/realtime-server typecheck` green.
- [x] `pnpm --filter @bibliothecadao/provider exec vitest run` — 40/40 pass.
- [x] Dev-net smoke against `bltz-clash-571` — game loads, map renders, structures populate, coordinate normalization correct.
- [ ] Mainnet dry-run of one high-l2_gas tx; confirm `resource_bounds.l2_gas.max_amount` is ~1.5× raw estimate (not 2.25×) and never above `1_200_000_000`.

## Known pre-existing issues (not in scope)

- `client/apps/onchain-agent` typecheck fails on `WorldArtifacts.manifest`'s loose `{ contracts: unknown[] }` type. Hidden before because workspace packages weren't built. Not bump-caused; track as separate issue.
- Root `package.json` carries a stale `workspaces.catalog` block (npm-workspaces format, ignored by pnpm 10). Synced in lockstep here for safety; cleanup follow-up to delete it.

## Follow-ups

1. File upstream issue with `dojo.js`: `createDojoConfig` ABI overwrite breaks lean manifests.
2. File upstream issue: `@dojoengine/utils.getEntityIdFromKeys` should not pad to felt252 width (server-side storage is unpadded).
3. Track v9 migration (blocked on `@dojoengine/*` v9-compatible release).
4. Track `Account.fastExecute` integration (blocked on v9 + Cartridge controller `BlockTag.PRE_CONFIRMED` support).
5. Delete the duplicate `workspaces.catalog` block at root `package.json` once confirmed unused.

author: mervinpraison
body:
## Problem (before)

`praisonai onboard` had no non-interactive mode. In several real situations it would hang forever on a blocking prompt:

- **install.sh piped flow** — when the user answered `Y` to "Set up a messaging bot?" and then walked away; the wizard would block on the first `Prompt.ask()`.
- **Daemon post-install reconfig** — no stdin at all → infinite hang.
- **CI / scripted installs** — pytest and CI runners don't give a TTY.
- **Docker / remote bootstrap** — same.

`install.sh` already honoured `PRAISONAI_NO_PROMPT=1`, but once control passed to the Python wizard every `rich.prompt.Prompt.ask` / `Confirm.ask` / `input()` / `getpass.getpass()` call ignored it.

## Fix (after)

Two new entry points, same env-var semantics `install.sh` already documents:

### CLI flag
```bash
praisonai onboard --yes
praisonai onboard -y
praisonai onboard --non-interactive
```

### Env var
```bash
PRAISONAI_NO_PROMPT=1 praisonai onboard
```

Both paths short-circuit every blocking prompt in `@src/praisonai/praisonai/cli/features/onboard.py` to its declared default:

- Platform: defaults to `telegram`
- Token: kept from existing env var (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` etc.) if present; left blank otherwise (wizard prints the usual `⚠ No token` warning)
- Allowlist: kept from existing `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS` etc.
- Overwrite existing `bot.yaml`: declined (safer default — never clobbers a hand-edited config non-interactively)

The wizard also auto-detects and goes non-interactive when `stdin` is not a TTY, so nothing new is needed in `install.sh` (the env var was already forwarded) or in daemon reconfig paths.

### Implementation

1. New `_is_non_interactive()` helper (`onboard.py:28-49`):
   ```python
   def _is_non_interactive() -> bool:
       if os.environ.get("PRAISONAI_NO_PROMPT", "").strip() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on"):
           return True
       try:
           if not sys.stdin.isatty():
               return True
       except (AttributeError, ValueError):
           return True
       return False
   ```

2. Four thin wrappers that every blocking call now routes through:
   - `_prompt_ask(Prompt, …)` → returns `default` instead of calling `Prompt.ask`
   - `_confirm_ask(Confirm, …)` → returns `default` instead of calling `Confirm.ask`
   - `_plain_input(msg, default=…)` → returns `default` instead of calling `input()`
   - `_plain_getpass(msg)` → returns `""` instead of calling `getpass.getpass()`

3. All 11 call sites across `run()` (rich path) and `_run_plain()` (no-rich fallback) were migrated to the wrappers. Zero behavioural change in interactive mode.

4. `praisonai onboard --yes` (`@src/praisonai/praisonai/cli/commands/onboard.py`) sets `PRAISONAI_NO_PROMPT=1` for the process so every nested import and subprocess inherits it.

## Evidence per claim

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|
| 11 blocking prompt sites in the wizard, all now wrapped | `grep -nE "Prompt\\.ask\\\|Confirm\\.ask\\\|input\\(\\\|getpass\\.getpass" src/praisonai/praisonai/cli/features/onboard.py` returns 0 matches outside the wrapper functions themselves |
| Env var detection works for `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`, and variants | `test_is_non_interactive_true_when_env_set` exercises each |
| Does NOT force non-interactive when stdin is a TTY and env is off/empty | `test_is_non_interactive_false_when_env_explicitly_off` |
| End-to-end wizard completes without any blocking call | `test_wizard_run_does_not_block_in_non_interactive` — boobytraps `rich.prompt.Prompt.ask`, `Confirm.ask`, `input`, `getpass.getpass` with `AssertionError` and asserts `OnboardWizard().run()` completes |
| No regression for interactive users | No code path changed when `_is_non_interactive()` returns False — all wrappers delegate unchanged to the original call |
| CLI flag sets the env var cleanly | `onboard_callback(yes=True)` sets `os.environ["PRAISONAI_NO_PROMPT"] = "1"` before invoking the wizard |

## Verification

```
$ PYTHONPATH=src/praisonai pytest tests/unit/cli/test_onboard_non_interactive.py
8 passed in 0.21s
```

Manual:
```bash
# curl|bash flow (no TTY) — no longer hangs
PRAISONAI_NO_PROMPT=1 praisonai onboard

# Explicit opt-in from a user's terminal
praisonai onboard --yes

# Existing interactive behaviour preserved
praisonai onboard                  # → full wizard, unchanged
```

## Diff

```
src/praisonai/praisonai/cli/commands/onboard.py          |  22 ++-
src/praisonai/praisonai/cli/features/onboard.py          |  89 +++++++++--
src/praisonai/tests/unit/cli/test_onboard_non_interactive.py | +187 (new)
3 files changed, 301 insertions(+), 13 deletions(-)
```

## Rollback

Single-commit revert. No schema migration, no yaml change, no env-var semantic change (the variable `install.sh` already forwards just now *works* in the wizard too).

## Related

- Follow-up to the observation in #1493: `install.sh` forwarded `PRAISONAI_NO_PROMPT` but the downstream wizard ignored it.
- Independent of #1496 (bot default tools) — this PR only touches the wizard's prompt gating.

Reachable via a small "Try the v2 preview →" link on the existing `library.html`; old library page is untouched until the D5 cut-over. `mountRecipeBrowser()` builds the filter shell into `#rx-root` via functions returning `HTMLElement` (same pattern as `library-ui.js` / `source-water-ui.js`). Method / Roast segmented rows, flavor chips, My Recipes toggle, and debounced (150ms) search all mirror state to the URL via `history.replaceState`. `applyFilters(filters, recipes, { isSaved })` is a pure predicate (method × roast × tags AND × mine × search), exposed on `window` for direct e2e coverage. ## Summary
- `WsSession.ping()` used `runCatching { ... }.isSuccess`, which catches `Throwable` — including `CancellationException`. A coroutine cancelled mid-ping would see the cancellation swallowed and surfaced as "ping failed" instead of unwinding, leaving callers (e.g. `WsSessionManager.probe`) potentially stuck awaiting a job that won't complete.
- Replace with an explicit try/catch that rethrows `CancellationException` and returns `false` only for other exceptions.

author: squirmywormy275
body:
## Summary
Gets the daily backup workflow actually working end-to-end, plus adds race-weekend hourly coverage.

### Bug fixes (workflow was broken in 4 different ways before)
- **KEY=URL prefix tolerance** — strips leading `DATABASE_PUBLIC_URL=` if someone pastes the full `railway variables --kv` line as the secret value
- **Whitespace strip** — strips all whitespace from the secret (URLs can't contain any), so trailing newlines from copy-paste don't break the connection
- **PG 18 pg_dump PATH** — prepends `/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin` to `$GITHUB_PATH` so the Debian pg_wrapper doesn't dispatch to an older pg_dump preinstalled on ubuntu-latest. Fixes `pg_dump: error: aborting because of server version mismatch` against Railway's PG 18.3 server
- **pipefail off in sanity check** — `gunzip | head -20` fights `set -o pipefail` (head closes the pipe → SIGPIPE on gunzip → step fails). Use `set -eu` only in that step

### New: race-weekend hourly schedule
- Existing daily baseline stays at `0 8 * * *` (02:00 MDT, low-traffic)
- Added `0 * 24-26 4 *` — hourly dumps on April 24-26 UTC, which covers Thursday 6 PM MDT through Sunday 5 PM MDT
- Caps worst-case data loss at **1 hour** during the event (was 24 hours)
- Comment in the cron explains how to update dates annually after each Missoula Pro-Am

### New: concurrency guard
- Added `concurrency: { group: daily-backup, cancel-in-progress: false }` so daily + hourly + manual-dispatch schedules serialize on the public Postgres proxy — queue rather than stampede, and don't kill a backup mid-stream

## Evidence it works
- Branch run [24762982995](https://github.com/SquirmyWormy275/Missoula-Pro-Am-Manager/actions/runs/24762982995) — ✓ success, 30s, artifact `proam-db-backup-24762982995` uploaded

## Race-day safety
- The backup workflow is run-one-off infra; no runtime code changes; no migrations
- The hourly schedule only fires on April 24-26 UTC and can be reverted by deleting one line if it causes problems

## Summary
E2E Playwright test validating the CS42-2 (SW cache bump) + CS42-2b (controllerchange one-shot reload) migration path: a `gwn-v2`-cached browser must purge the old cache and reload into the fresh shell on the next visit.

## Test approach
- Fresh Playwright context with SW enabled (separate spec from `coldstart-real.spec.mjs` to avoid its SW-blocked fixture).
- Installs a minimal old SW (gwn-v2) via context-level route interception, seeds a bogus `gwn-v2` cache with a sentinel `app.js`, switches to the real sw.js (gwn-v3), triggers SW update.
- Asserts all four criteria: cache purged, sentinel not served, gwn-v3 active, controllerchange reload happened exactly once.

## Validation
- `npm run lint` ✓
- `npm test` ✓ (444 tests)
- `npm run test:e2e` ✓ (68 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failures in own test; pre-existing flaky tests unrelated)

### Local Review Log

author: somsubhra-nandi
body:
# fix: replace db.ts stubs with real PKM backend calls

## Description

`lib/db.ts` contained three stub functions that were silently broken in
production:

- `storeUserData()` logged `[STUB]` to the console, waited 500ms, and
  returned `true` — meaning encrypted user preferences were never actually
  persisted to the backend. Any user saving vault preferences believed the
  operation succeeded while data was silently discarded.

- `getAllFoodData()` and `getAllProfessionalData()` permanently returned
  `null` and had no callers. The backend explicitly documents their removal:
  `db_proxy.py` line 224: *"NOTE: /food/get and /professional/get removed;
  domain data is via PKM."*

**Changes:**

1. `storeUserData()` — replaced the fake delay with a real
   `fetch("/api/pkm/store-domain", ...)` call. Sends the encrypted blob
   (`ciphertext`, `iv`, `tag`) to the PKM backend which stores it opaquely
   (BYOK — backend cannot decrypt). Includes a 30s `AbortController` timeout
   and returns `false` on failure instead of silently returning `true`.

2. `getAllFoodData()` and `getAllProfessionalData()` — removed. Zero callers,
   permanently returning `null`, backend endpoints deleted. Dead code.

---

## 📌 Impact Map (Required)

- Routes touched:
  - [x] Listed below:
    - `POST /api/pkm/store-domain` — now actually called by `storeUserData()`
      (was previously bypassed by the stub)
- API / schema / type changes:
  - [x] Listed below:
    - `getAllFoodData()` and `getAllProfessionalData()` removed from `lib/db.ts`
    - No callers exist — confirmed by grep across entire `hushh-webapp`
- Cache keys touched:
  - [x] None
- World-model domain summary effects:
  - [x] None — `summary: {}` passed intentionally; store-preferences stores
    encrypted preference blobs, not queryable PKM domain data
- Mobile parity impacts:
  - [x] None — `storeUserData()` uses relative `/api/pkm/store-domain` path
    which routes correctly on both web and Capacitor via the existing
    Next.js proxy
- Docs updated (exact files):
  - [x] None — removal of dead functions is self-documenting via commit message
- Verification commands executed:
  - [x] `cd hushh-webapp && npm run typecheck` — 0 errors

---

## 🛑 Tri-Flow Architecture Check

- [x] **Web:** `storeUserData()` calls `/api/pkm/store-domain` which is an
  existing Next.js proxy route — no change needed
- [x] **iOS:** N/A — `storeUserData()` is called from a Next.js API route
  (`store-preferences/route.ts`), not from a Capacitor plugin. No native
  change required.
- [x] **Android:** N/A — same as iOS above

---

## 🧪 Testing

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — 0 errors
- [x] Confirmed zero callers of `getAllFoodData()` and
  `getAllProfessionalData()` via grep before removal
- [x] `storeUserData()` call site in `store-preferences/route.ts` unchanged —
  same function signature, same parameters, drop-in replacement
- [x] Commits are signed off (`git commit -s`)

---

## 🛡️ Privacy & Consent

- [x] Does this change access user data? **Yes — encrypted write only**
- [x] Consent is enforced upstream in `store-preferences/route.ts` which
  validates the `consentToken` with the Python backend before calling
  `storeUserData()`. This function is only ever reached after consent
  is confirmed — no change to the consent gate.
- Raw plaintext is never handled — only `ciphertext`, `iv`, and `tag`
  are passed and forwarded. BYOK guarantee preserved.

---

## 📜 Licensing

- [x] First-party changes remain Apache-2.0 compatible
- [x] No new dependencies introduced — uses only browser-native `fetch`
  and `AbortController`

author: wmotte
body:
## Wat

Corrigeert twee problemen op de uitlog-pagina:

1. De in PR #122 toegevoegde knop 'Opnieuw inloggen' navigeerde niet naar login.py.
2. De titel bleef staan op 'Uitloggen' terwijl het uitloggen op dat moment al voltooid was.

## Waarom de knop niet werkte

Op het moment dat de gebruiker op de knop klikte was `api_handler` al uit session_state gepopt. Daardoor viel `logout_page` buiten de actieve navigatielijst (zie `main.py` waar de paginalijst conditioneel is op `api_handler`). Streamlit viel terug op `welcome_page`, en de `st.switch_page(.../login.py)`-callback in `logout.py` werd nooit uitgevoerd.

## Fix

- `main.py`: `logout_page` opgenomen in de unauthenticated paginalijst, zodat `/logout` bereikbaar blijft nadat `api_handler` is gewist.
- `page_navigation/logout.py`: twee-fasen-flow:
  - **Fase 1** (eerste render, `api_handler` aanwezig): HTTP blacklist-call → sessie-cleanup (`api_handler`, `dark_mode`, `is_superuser`) → `st.rerun()`. Die rerun laat `main.py` de nieuwe unauthenticated navigatie opbouwen.
  - **Fase 2** (tweede render, `api_handler` afwezig): titel **'Uitgelogd'** (verleden tijd), succes-melding en de knop die met `st.switch_page(.../login.py)` betrouwbaar naar het inlogscherm navigeert.

## Gedrag

- Klik 'Uitloggen' in sidebar → korte rerun → zie 'Uitgelogd' + succes + knop.
- Klik 'Opnieuw inloggen' → landt op `login.py`.
- HTTP-fout tijdens blacklist → titel 'Uitloggen' + foutmelding (ongewijzigd gedrag).

`gather_defined_operator()` calls `tokens.front()` without checking if the deque is empty first. A malformed `defined` expression, e.g. a bare `defined` at the end of a macro argument list triggers undefined behaviour rather than a clean diagnostic.

## Problem

Google OAuth stores a full HTTPS URL (e.g. `https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/...`) in the `foto_profil` column, but the blade templates unconditionally wrap it with `Storage::url()`, producing an invalid path like `/storage/https://...` that the browser cannot resolve.

Replaced every `Storage::url($x->foto_profil)` call with a ternary that checks `str_starts_with(..., 'http')` — if true the URL is used as-is, otherwise `Storage::url()` is applied for locally-uploaded files. The fix covers the sidebar avatar in `profiluser.blade.php` and `dashboarduser.blade.php`, the profile photo form in `profiluser.blade.php`, and the admin avatar in `profiladmin.blade.php`.

author: maksym-panibrat
body:
## Summary

PR 6 of the [stabilization plan](../../.claude/plans/2026-04-21-stabilize-golden-path.md). \`get_current_user\` in \`app/api/deps.py\` previously caught \`jwt.PyJWTError\` broadly and raised 401 with no log — making auth failures impossible to diagnose without reproducing the client request.

## What lands

\`get_current_user\` now emits a distinct structured \`log.awarning\` per failure mode:

- \`auth.token_expired\` — JWT \`exp\` in the past
- \`auth.token_invalid_signature\` — wrong \`JWT_SECRET\`
- \`auth.token_invalid\` — other \`PyJWTError\` (carries \`error_type\`)
- \`auth.token_missing_sub\` — token decoded but no \`sub\` claim
- \`auth.user_not_found\` — \`sub\` resolves to a nonexistent user (carries \`user_id\`)
- \`auth.user_inactive\` — user exists but \`is_active=False\` (carries \`user_id\`)

The HTTP response is unchanged — 401 with generic \"Invalid token\" or \"User not found or inactive\" — so there's no new timing/info disclosure to clients. Server-side logs become filterable by \`event\` in GCP Logs Explorer.

Level stays at **WARNING**: these are client-side auth failures, not server bugs. Error Reporting (which ingests on ERROR+) stays quiet for these.

- token_expired / invalid_signature / missing_sub / user_not_found / user_inactive (5 failure paths)
- happy_path + no_token_401 (2 boundary cases)
- single_user_mode_bypass + single_user_mode_autocreates (2 \`AUTH_ENABLED=false\` sub-paths)

Uses \`structlog.testing.capture_logs\` to assert log event emission without touching stdlib handlers.

- \`uv run pytest tests/unit/ -q\` — 147 → 156 (+9).

## Summary

`hwaro tool import` bundles three user-visible fixes on the shared CLI + `Base` paths:

- **Classified errors (#443)** — missing `<source-type>`, missing `<path>`, unknown source-type, and empty source directories all become `HwaroError`. The CLI returns `EXIT_USAGE` (2) with an `Error [HWARO_E_USAGE]:` prefix and a source-type-specific hint (e.g. *"Expected a Jekyll site root containing _posts/"*). Importer failures bubble up as `HWARO_E_IO` with the same taxonomy. `--json` / quiet consumers now get the structured payload for these paths.
- **Empty source = failure (#448)** — when the importer returns `imported=0, skipped=0, errors=0`, the CLI now raises `HWARO_E_USAGE` with a hint instead of logging `"0 imported, 0 skipped, 0 errors"` and exiting 0.
- **Collision visibility + `--force` (#449)** — `Base#write_content_file` collisions were previously silent skips with no escape hatch. We now emit a post-run warning `"N file(s) skipped because the destination already exists. Re-run with --force to overwrite."`, and the new `--force` flag overwrites the output. `force` is threaded through all 8 importers.

## Before / After

**Missing source-type**
```
# before: exit 1, ad-hoc "Missing source type..."
# after:
$ hwaro tool import
Error [HWARO_E_USAGE]: missing <source-type> argument
Usage: hwaro tool import <source-type> <path> — supported: wordpress, jekyll, ...
# exit 2
```

**Empty source directory**
```
# before: "Import complete: 0 imported, 0 skipped, 0 errors"  (exit 0)
# after:
Error [HWARO_E_USAGE]: no importable content found at: /tmp/empty
Expected a Jekyll site root containing _posts/ (and optionally _drafts/).
# exit 2
```

**Collision skip**
```
# before: silently skipped, no message, no recovery path
# after (no --force):
Import complete: 0 imported, 1 skipped, 0 errors
[WARN] 1 file(s) skipped because the destination already exists. Re-run with --force to overwrite.

# after (--force): overwrites
Import complete: 1 imported, 0 skipped, 0 errors
```

## Diff footprint

- `src/cli/commands/tool/import_command.cr` — classify all error paths, add `--force`, empty-source check, skipped warning, per-source hint.
- `src/config/options/import_options.cr`, `src/services/importers/base.cr` — add `force` field/param.
- 8 importer files — thread `options.force` through caller → signature → `write_content_file`.
- Specs: base + jekyll `--force` coverage, updated functional CLI specs for new `HWARO_E_USAGE` exit codes + empty-source path.

- [x] `just fix` — 340 inspected, 0 failures
- [x] `just test` — 4584 examples, 0 failures
- [x] Smoke test on `/tmp` fixture: all four classified error paths return exit 2 with `HWARO_E_USAGE`; collision warning fires without `--force`; `--force` overwrites.

Closes #443, closes #448, closes #449

author: roy-oss1
body:
## What does this PR do?

**Problem.** Today the Feishu adapter strips every `<at>` tag and `@_user_N` placeholder out of inbound messages before the agent sees them. A user saying *"@Alice please review this with @Bob"* reaches the agent as *"please review this with"* — the agent has no idea who was mentioned, and therefore cannot do anything about them (summon them, route work, call Feishu OpenAPI with their IDs). Mention semantics, which are a first-class part of how people communicate in group chats, are silently destroyed.

**Goal.** Make @mentions visible and *actionable* to the agent:
1. The agent can see **who** was mentioned (by display name) in the message body.
2. The agent can **act on them** via Feishu OpenAPI (e.g. `im.v1.chat.members.create`, `im.v1.message.create` with a reply target) using stable `open_id`s — no second round trip to resolve names.

**How.** Resolve Feishu's `@_user_N` / `@_all` placeholders through the top-level `mentions` array into a typed map, keep the display names inline in the body, and prepend a structured `[Mentioned: Alice (open_id=ou_aaa), Bob (open_id=ou_bbb)]` hint so the LLM sees both the human-readable name and the stable ID in one place. The same map powers plain-text and rich-post payloads.

The only mentions we strip are the bot's own name, and only at message edges (leading unconditionally, trailing only before whitespace/terminal punctuation) — that strip exists purely to keep `@bot /help` parsing as a command. Mid-text references to the bot (*"ask @bot about it"*) are preserved.

**Also fixes a pre-existing hydration bug:** `Client.request(method=..., ...)` no longer accepts the `method` kwarg on `lark-oapi` 1.5.3, so bot identity was silently failing to hydrate from `/open-apis/bot/v3/info` and the bot could never reliably filter its own mentions. Migrated to the `BaseRequest.builder()` pattern and accepted the `app_name` field the API actually returns.

## Related Issue

Fixes #13846 — the hydration `TypeError` on `lark-oapi` 1.5.5 and the `bot_name` vs `app_name` field mismatch are both addressed here.

Related to #10356 — surfacing `open_id`s to the agent is a prerequisite for the "act on mentioned users" use cases listed there (e.g. "schedule a meeting with everyone who was mentioned").

## Type of Change

- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔒 Security fix
- [ ] 📝 Documentation update
- [ ] ✅ Tests (adding or improving test coverage)
- [ ] ♻️ Refactor (no behavior change)
- [ ] 🎯 New skill (bundled or hub)

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/feishu.py`:
  - Added `FeishuMentionRef` dataclass and `_build_mentions_map` / `_build_mention_hint` helpers that resolve Feishu placeholders (`@_user_N`, `@_all`) via the top-level `mentions` array into `(name, open_id, is_all, is_self)` refs.
  - Added `_strip_edge_self_mentions` — strips bot self-mentions at the leading edge unconditionally and at the trailing edge only when followed by whitespace/terminal punctuation; mid-text mentions are preserved.
  - Rewrote post-type parsing to walk the rich-post tree and resolve `<at user_id="@_user_N">` placeholders through the mentions map (including structural `@_all` detection).
  - Added module-private `_FeishuBotIdentity` with precedence-based `matches()` — open_id > user_id > name; a higher tier is authoritative when both sides carry that identifier, and the next tier only engages as a fallback.
  - Fixed `_hydrate_bot_identity` / `_probe_bot_sdk` to use the `BaseRequest.builder()` pattern required by `lark-oapi` 1.5.3; `_parse_bot_response` now also accepts the `app_name` field the API returns.
  - Threaded the resolved mentions map through `normalize_feishu_message`, `_extract_message_content`, and `_process_inbound_message` so the hint is injected after the empty-body guard (never before, so commands like `@bot /help` still route as commands).
- `tests/gateway/test_feishu.py`: added coverage for mention-map building, hint formatting, edge-strip behavior, post-payload parsing, bot-identity precedence (including user_id-only scenarios), hydration response shape, and end-to-end inbound processing.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/gateway/test_feishu.py -q` — 152 tests pass.
2. In a Feishu group chat with the bot, send each of these and verify the agent prompt receives mention context:
   - `@bot hello` → admits, body becomes `hello`, hint lists only other mentions (bot self-stripped).
   - `hello @bot` → admits, body becomes `hello`, trailing mention stripped.
   - `ask @bot about it` → admits, body preserved as-is (mid-text mention kept), hint lists the bot.
   - `@Alice @Bob please sync` → body preserved, hint is `[Mentioned: Alice (open_id=ou_aaa), Bob (open_id=ou_bbb)]` — agent can now pass those `open_id`s into a Feishu OpenAPI tool call.
   - `@everyone ping` → admits, `[Mentioned: @everyone]` appears in the hint.
   - Rich-post message mentioning multiple users → hint lists each with their `open_id`.
3. Confirm the gateway log shows `_bot_open_id` populated on startup (previously stayed empty due to the SDK regression).

## Checklist

### Code

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated relevant documentation (README, `docs/`, docstrings) — or N/A (N/A — internal platform adapter, behavior documented in tests)

## Screenshots / Logs

```
# Leading mention stripped; hint injected so the agent still knows the bot was addressed
```

body:
## Summary

Adds **`GET /api/admin/users/:userId/credit-transactions.csv`** — admin-side export of one user's full ledger. Support pulls it on a user's behalf. The self-service cousin `/api/users/me/cashback-history.csv` already exists for authenticated users (ADR 017).

### Columns

```
Transaction ID, Created at (UTC), Type, Amount (minor), Currency, Reference type, Reference ID
```

- **Amount** is the raw bigint — precision preserved even for absurd amounts.
- **Null reference fields** emit as empty cells (stable across `'order'` rows and support-adjusted rows).
- **Newest-first** ordering matches how support reads a ledger.
- **Filename includes the userId** so multiple exports stay distinguishable on disk.

### Tier 3 conventions (ADR 019 / 021)

- `text/csv; charset=utf-8`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="loop-user-<id>-credit-transactions.csv"`
- `Cache-Control: private, no-store` — contains the user id + reference ids
- RFC 4180 escape on every cell
- 10 000-row cap + `__TRUNCATED__` sentinel + `log.warn` when hit
- Rate limit 20/min — matches other admin CSV exports
- 400 on missing / non-UUID `userId`

## Test plan

- [x] 6 new unit tests: missing userId, non-UUID userId, happy path + naming + headers, null reference serialisation, empty-ledger header-only, 500 on db throw

- [x] typecheck + lint + docs-lint clean

author: aaronfeledy
body:
Sweep of every finding from the internal gap-hunt review (FINDINGS.md). Each
commit is a single self-contained fix with regression tests. Full test suite
is green across 3 consecutive runs (134 tests, 439 expect() calls).

## What's fixed

### 🔴 Critical
- **C1 — cascade wipe on session/project update.** `INSERT OR REPLACE` was
  deleting child rows (messages, parts, todos, session_share, permission)
  every time a cross-peer session title / summary / time_compacting update
  landed. Replaced with `INSERT … ON CONFLICT(pk) DO UPDATE SET …`.

### 🟠 High
- **H1 + M5 — file sync.** Transient delete failures silently resurrected
  the file next cycle; walkDir followed symlinks (arbitrary path leak).
  `deleteRemoteFile` now returns a tri-state and on transient error retains
  the entry in knownFiles + adds to pendingRemoteDeletes so the download
  branch doesn't resurrect it. walkDir + computeLocalManifest use lstatSync
  and refuse symlinks.
- **H2 / M2 — halt paths didn't clear pendingTombstones.** Fingerprint-halt
  and getHeads-failure defer left pending entries with stale firstSeenAt
  that instant-tombstoned on recovery, bypassing the 30s confirmation
  window. Both now clear the buffer.
- **H3 + M8 — poison-envelope deadlock + time_updated validation.** Pull
  loop broke on any error without advancing; one bad envelope blocked all
  pulls forever. Now per-envelope retry counters in state.json skip past
  after 10 tries and record to `poisonedEnvelopes` for audit. Plugin and
  server both reject `time_updated <= 0`.
- **H4 — no push body/batch caps.** Bun.serve `maxRequestBodySize: 64 MiB`
  + `PUSH_MAX_BATCH: 5000` symmetric with HEADS_MAX_BATCH.
- **H5 — blobs never garbage-collected.** `auth_json` retention: rotated
  tokens stayed fetchable forever. `upsertManifestEntry` now ref-counts by
  sha, unlinks orphaned blobs, and clears tombstone sha256 when the last
  reference drops.

### 🟡 Medium
- **M1 — session-delete halts the plugin.** New `rowParents` secondary
  index (child rowKey → parent session id) lets `markExpectedDeletion`
  cascade-expand messages/parts/todos/shares on a session delete.
- **M3 — state.load() silently eats errors.** Parse failures now back
  up the corrupt file to `state.json.corrupt-${ts}` and log at error
  severity instead of silently resetting.
- **M4 — prototype pollution in applyOverrides.** Rejects `__proto__`,
  `constructor`, `prototype` keys.
- **M6 — wall-clock backjump loses rows.** `pushReadSince` detects a
  backward clock jump and resets the cursor.
- **M7 — parseRowStateKey accepts empty kind.** Rejects `separator <= 0`
  + validates kind against `SYNC_KINDS`.

### 🟢 Low
- **L1** halt marker `schema_version`.
- **L2** `crypto.randomUUID()` for atomic-write temp names.
- **L4** server token `.trim()` + warning.
- **L5** `?exclude=` empty-string short-circuit.
- **L7** `asSessionId` helper replaces 8 unchecked casts in hooks.ts.

### Not fixed (intentional)
- **L6** (log level reactive) is not a bug.
- **L3** (stripJsoncComments marginal) repro passes on all tested edge
  cases — defer until we have a real failure.
- **L8** (log rotation race) is multi-process edge case; documented as
  limitation rather than adding file locking.

## Commits

\`\`\`
$(git log --oneline main..HEAD)
\`\`\`

## Test coverage

134 tests across 14 files. New tests added for C1, H1, H2, H3, H4, H5,
M1, M3, M4, M5, M6, M7, M8, L1. Run 3× consecutively, 0 failures.

## Breaking changes

None in protocol or on-disk formats. state.json gains new optional
fields (pullErrorCounts, poisonedEnvelopes, rowParents); old files load
unchanged and new fields populate on first sync.

Refs: FINDINGS.md

author: marcusquinn
body:
## Summary

Eliminates the 5-8s delay between first-message keystroke and session start in OpenCode sessions that was introduced by the t2724 greeting-toast path.

**Root cause:** `execSync` in `greeting.mjs::runUpdateCheck()` blocked the `session.created` handler because Node waits for all inherited stdout FDs to close, including those held by background children spawned by the update-check script (provenance notify, deploy drift check).

## Changes

### Option A — Node side (`greeting.mjs`)

- Replaced `execSync` / `runUpdateCheck()` with `execAsync` (promisified `exec`) inside new `runGreetingAsync()`.
- All downstream work (cache write, classify, toast emit) runs inside the `.then()` callback — fires when the subprocess eventually finishes, not before.
- Handler calls `runGreetingAsync()` **without `await`** and logs `handler-completed` immediately after, so the `session.created` promise resolves in `<1ms`.
- `AIDEVOPS_PLUGIN_DEBUG=1` log ordering now shows `handler-completed` **before** `emitToast-*` — the reversed ordering confirms async delivery.
- 15s timeout (t2725) is preserved, now governing the fire-and-forget tail.

### Option B — Shell side (`aidevops-update-check.sh`)

Defence-in-depth for any synchronous caller that may exist in the future:

- Provenance notify fork (line ~772): moved `>/dev/null 2>&1` **outside** the subshell: `(curl ... || true) >/dev/null 2>&1 &`
- Deploy drift redeploy fork (line ~612): same pattern: `(bash "$setup_script" --non-interactive) >/dev/null 2>&1 &`

This ensures the parent applies the redirect before the subshell forks, so the background processes never inherit the parent's stdout FD.

## Verification

- `node --check .agents/plugins/opencode-aidevops/greeting.mjs` — PASS
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/aidevops-update-check.sh` — PASS (zero violations)

Resolves #20436

## Summary
- `tenant-auth.ts` / `super-admin.ts` のモジュールトップレベルで `isProductionRuntime() && AUTH_MODE !== "firebase"` を検知して Error を throw し、Cloud Run の起動を fail-fast させる。
- **本番 runtime 判定**: `NODE_ENV` を `.trim().toLowerCase()` で正規化した `"production"` 一致、または Cloud Run 自動注入の `K_SERVICE` 存在、のいずれか（defense-in-depth）。
- **dev モードでは `X-User-Email` が無検証で信頼される**ため、環境変数欠落 / IaC ドリフト / リビジョン切り戻しで AUTH_MODE が "dev" に落ちると allowed_emails 境界 (Issue #286 / #294) がすべてバイパスされる。この事故を起動時に検知する。
- `docs/runbook/auth-mode-production-check.md` 新設 (本番デプロイチェックリスト + 本番 runtime 判定ロジック + 復旧手順)。

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] NODE_ENV=production + AUTH_MODE=dev → モジュール import 時に throw
- [x] NODE_ENV="Production"（大文字） / "production " (末尾空白) でも throw（正規化）
- [x] **NODE_ENV 未設定 + K_SERVICE 設定済み + AUTH_MODE=dev → throw**（Cloud Run 実挙動、codex HIGH 回帰防止）
- [x] K_SERVICE 設定済み + AUTH_MODE=firebase → 起動成功
- [x] NODE_ENV=development / test / 未設定 + AUTH_MODE=dev + K_SERVICE="" → 起動成功（開発/CI 体験保護）
- [x] AUTH_MODE='' (空文字, IaC ミス想定) 本番 runtime → throw
- [x] super-admin.ts にも同等 assertion + `isProductionRuntime()` を適用（モジュール独立のため重複許容）
- [x] 本番デプロイ runbook 整備 + 本番 runtime 判定の明文化

## 設計判断
- **DRY より独立性を優先**: tenant-auth.ts と super-admin.ts で同一 `isProductionRuntime()` + assertion を重複配置。共通モジュール化は循環依存リスク + テスト時の `vi.resetModules()` 対応複雑化のため現状見送り。3 つ目以降が出た時点で共通化を検討。
- **本番 runtime 判定 (codex HIGH 指摘反映)**: 当初は `NODE_ENV === "production"` のみだったが、現行 `.github/workflows/deploy.yml:83` に `NODE_ENV=production` が未設定で assertion が発火しない抜け穴を codex セカンドオピニオンで発見。Cloud Run 自動注入の `K_SERVICE` を併用して本番検知を担保。
- **NODE_ENV の正規化** (silent-failure-hunter M-1): `.trim().toLowerCase()` で IaC の人為ミス（大文字始まり・末尾空白）耐性。
- **deploy.yml 更新は別 PR**: 本コミットで K_SERVICE フォールバックが入ったため HIGH は解消。deploy.yml に `NODE_ENV=production` を明示する変更は defense-in-depth として follow-up Issue で対応予定。

## Test plan
- [x] `npm test --workspace=@lms-279/api` → 536/536 PASS（新規 20 ケース追加）
  - describe.each で tenant-auth.ts / super-admin.ts を並列検証、各 10 シナリオ (計 20)
  - 網羅: NODE_ENV 4 ケース（production/Production/production+trim/dev/test/未設定）× AUTH_MODE 3 ケース（dev/空文字/firebase）+ K_SERVICE 2 ケース（有/無）

## Quality Gate

- [x] silent-failure-hunter: HIGH なし、MEDIUM 1 件反映済み（NODE_ENV 正規化）

body:
<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes core interview session flow by dynamically mutating question lists (probabilistic follow-up chaining, reverse-QA completion) and persisting the mutated JSON, which can affect session progression and reporting. Also modifies voice prompt generation and S3 startup behavior, increasing integration/config risk.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Text interview flow is expanded and becomes persona-aware.** Session creation now accepts `personaType` (STRICT/FRIENDLY), stores it on `InterviewSessionEntity`, and uses `InterviewerPersonaService` to blend skill persona + style in prompts.
> 
> **Follow-ups are now dynamic and probabilistic.** After answering a main question, the service may *skip all follow-ups* or *replace/insert* follow-ups using LLM-generated prompts (`FollowUpGenerationService`), with new config knobs in `application.yml` (`follow-up-probability`, chain continue probability, max depth) and DB persistence via `updateQuestionsJson`.
> 
> **Adds an explicit “反问” (reverse-QA) stage.** The last stage is mapped in `InterviewFlowService`; when reached, submitting the candidate’s question completes the session and returns an `interviewerReply` generated by `InterviewReverseQaService` (new prompt templates), with `SubmitAnswerResponse` extended accordingly.
> 
> **Voice interview prompt/flow is refactored.** Voice sessions now carry `personaType`, prompt building includes phase context, and phase-transition logic is centralized into `InterviewFlowService`.
> 
> **Storage bootstrapping is improved.** Adds `app.storage.auto-create-bucket` (default true) and a startup runner to ensure the S3 bucket exists, handling concurrent creation races and providing clearer failure messaging.
> 
> **Frontend is updated for the new UX/API.** Adds persona selection, displays stage progress and dynamic-follow-up badges, sends `personaType` to text/voice session creation, and shows `interviewerReply` in the reverse-QA step.
> 
> **Resume grading output is hardened.** Switches LLM output for strengths from a JSON array to a semicolon-delimited `strengthsText` to reduce parse failures, with prompt updates and splitting logic.
>

author: fmw666
body:
## Summary
- Add `.gitattributes` to force LF endings for `*.sh` so `bash scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh` (and any future shell script) stops breaking on Windows / WSL with `$'\r': command not found`.
- Keep CRLF for Windows-only `*.bat / *.cmd / *.ps1`.
- Mark `public/assets/webfonts/*` as `binary` — this repo ships font binaries under an `.html` extension, and any future `text=auto` rule would silently corrupt them.
- Deliberately **not** enabling `* text=auto eol=lf` — a trial run of that flagged unrelated legacy assets (CRLF-committed CSS, the webfonts above) as modified and would bury real diffs in line-ending noise. We can tighten per-path later when those files are touched anyway.

## Context
While actually running `scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh` today (to lock down `main` + enable auto-merge), the local working-tree copy of the script had been CRLF-ified, and bash blew up on the `set -o pipefail` line with:

```
scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh: line 23: $'\r': command not found
scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh: line 24: set: pipefail: invalid option name
```

The file in the repo was already LF — the damage was happening on checkout/edit round-trips. `.gitattributes` is the durable fix for that.

Note that this PR contains only `.gitattributes` and no diff for the `.sh` file itself: after the rule is in place, `git add` re-normalizes the working tree to match the LF version already in the index, so no content change is needed. That's the whole point — the rule prevents the drift from reappearing.

## Test plan
- [x] `bash scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh` runs cleanly under WSL (verified locally — branch protection + auto-merge are now live on `main`).
- [ ] CI `build + test` stays green on this PR.
- [ ] After merge, a fresh checkout on Windows shows `scripts/setup-branch-protection.sh` as LF (`file` / `od -c` both confirm).

---
_Queued for `auto-merge` per `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` — should squash-merge on green CI._

author: risu729
body:
## Summary

Fixes the root `@latest` install bug from #9276: if `latest` cannot be resolved to a concrete version, normal versioned backends no longer fall through to installing into `installs/<tool>/latest/` as a real directory. Existing stale real `latest/` directories are also repaired into runtime symlinks after a concrete version is installed.

## Root Cause

`ToolVersion::resolve_version` could leave `tv.version == "latest"` when latest resolution returned no concrete version. The generic install path then created a real `installs/<tool>/latest/` directory. That real directory was later treated as an installed version and could block upgrade/reshim/runtime symlink repair.

## Changes

- Add an e2e regression for unresolved `dummy@latest` proving no real `latest/` directory is created.
- Add a stale-state e2e case proving `mise up` installs `2.0.0`, replaces `latest/` with `latest -> ./2.0.0`, and runs the new binary.
- Make unresolved `@latest` fail unless a concrete latest version resolves or a valid installed runtime symlink exists.
- Ignore stale real `latest/` directories in normal installed-version discovery and `latest_installed_version(None)`.
- Replace stale real `latest/` directories during runtime symlink rebuild when a concrete version exists.
- Preserve the existing UBI direct-URL behavior where `latest` is the artifact identity, while keeping that exception scoped to UBI URL installs.

## CI Flow

- Test-only commit `6bb6d5465` was pushed first and opened as this draft PR.
- GitHub Actions failed on that test-only commit as expected (`e2e-4`).
- Fix commit `54387223f` was pushed after the failing CI signal.
- Follow-up commit `5c9488d3d` keeps UBI direct URL `latest` installs working after CI exposed that compatibility case.

## Local Validation

- `mise run test:e2e e2e/cli/test_latest_real_dir`
- `mise run test:unit`
- `mise run lint`
- Isolated UBI direct URL smoke test for the CI-exposed `ffmpeg` case

## Notes

The only non-versioned literal `latest` exception in this patch is UBI direct URLs, where the URL itself identifies the downloaded artifact. Normal `@latest` requests still need to resolve to a concrete version or an existing valid runtime symlink.

author: yogeshwaran-c
body:
## What kind of change does this PR introduce?
Bug fix (DocumentBuilder).

## What is the current behavior?
`DocumentBuilder.setOpenAPIVersion` validates its argument with:

```ts
if (version.match(/^\d\.\d\.\d$/)) { … }
```

The regex requires **exactly one digit per segment**. OpenAPI Specification versions follow semver — `3.0.x` has already reached `3.0.4`, a future `3.0.10` or `3.10.0` would be entirely valid — but any of those would be silently rejected today with only a warn-level log, and the default version on the document would be kept.

Minimal repro:

```ts
const builder = new DocumentBuilder().setOpenAPIVersion('3.0.10');
// builder.build().openapi is still the default (3.0.0), no error,
// only a WARN-level log: 'The OpenApi version is invalid. Expecting format \"x.x.x\"'
```

## What is the new behavior?
Widened the regex to `/^\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/`, so each segment may contain any non-negative integer. Genuinely malformed inputs (`3.0`, `3.0.0-beta`, …) still fall through to the existing warning.

## Additional context
Added three unit-test cases to `test/document-builder.spec.ts` covering:
- The previously-accepted single-digit case (`3.1.0`) — regression guard.
- Multi-digit segments (`3.0.10`, `3.10.0`, `10.20.30`).
- Malformed inputs, to confirm they still leave the default in place.

author: zvdy
body:
Apply a defence-in-depth middleware chain to /api/v1/*:

- recoverer converts panics into generic 500 responses (stack to logs only).
- requestLogger records method/path/status/duration once per request.
- timeout caps each request at server.request_timeout (default 5s).
- maxBody rejects bodies over server.max_body_bytes (default 1 MiB) with
  413, preventing unbounded memory use on POST /api/v1/analyze.
- rateLimit applies a process-wide token bucket (default 50 rps / burst
  100); configurable, set rate_limit_rps: 0 to disable.
- apiKeyAuth requires Authorization: Bearer <key> or X-API-Key: <key>
  when server.auth.api_key is non-empty. PGAO_API_KEY / API_KEY env vars
  also set it. Disabled by default so existing deployments keep working.

/health, /ready, and /metrics are explicitly excluded from the chain so
Kubernetes probes and Prometheus scrapers keep working without a token.

Also scrubs raw err.Error() from handler responses. A new
respondInternal helper logs full error context while returning a
generic "internal server error" string — stops leaking connection
details and SQL state to callers.

Extends the kind integration test to cover oversized-body rejection
and generic internal-error messaging.

Tests: api coverage 71.2% -> 84.8% (6 new middleware tests, 5 new
handler tests).

## What

Unifies the status indicators shown in the welcome screen and the profile UI so both use the same circle glyph set, and fixes a startup race in profile validation that caused freshly configured profiles to flash as false 'unreachable'.

Specifically:

- **Indicator unification**: Welcome and profile views previously disagreed — one path emitted emoji, the other drew circle glyphs. Both code paths now render from a single shared glyph table, eliminating the visual mismatch reported in #224.

Resolves the emoji-vs-circle mismatch across profile UI and the 'unreachable on first paint' race noted in #224 ('bug(welcome): startup race causes false ''unreachable'' + emoji/circle indicator mismatch across profile UI').

body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive implementation of a Trie-based auto-complete system, including a Java Swing GUI that mimics the Gboard suggestion strip, and adds benchmarking and testing utilities for comparing Trie and brute-force search approaches. It also standardizes package naming conventions and improves dictionary handling in both BruteForce and PrefixTree modules.

**Major additions and improvements:**

### 1. Trie Data Structure and Autocomplete Functionality
- Added a full Trie implementation in `PrefixTree/Trie.java` and supporting node class in `PrefixTree/TrieNode.java`, with methods for inserting words and fetching auto-complete suggestions based on a prefix. The Trie stores the original dictionary line for each word. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-af4a0fa6aa6b5c8a643dfd4cb43607e23a4f31fc04057f540237ea73a3a87b76R1-R73) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-53dc812612eca2c1c018c2e4cd47eab11f94a41a4f601b42170d166b036b7682R1-R14)

### 2. Gboard-style GUI for Autocomplete
- Introduced `PrefixTree/AutocompleteGUI.java`, a Java Swing GUI that displays a live-updating suggestion strip above a text area. It integrates with the Trie to provide top 3 auto-complete suggestions as the user types, and allows users to click a suggestion to auto-complete the current word.

### 3. Scalability and Testing Utilities
- Added `test/ScalabilityDriver.java` and `test/TestAlgorithms.java` to benchmark and compare the performance of Trie-based and brute-force prefix search algorithms across varying input sizes. Both drivers load the dictionary, execute searches, and report timing results. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6068b1a7b738a5b09cff6d318310ebd49439c789fc643337853488f7cb8ad56eR1-R95) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-261483699524a41bd5b3a14d110f6cec4e1a4875bcb14d65fe75685e42c971c0R1-R66)

### 4. Brute Force Improvements and Consistency
- Updated the BruteForce implementation to extract only the first word from dictionary lines when reporting matches, and added a static `countMatches` method for use in benchmarking. Also, standardized package naming to lower-case (`bruteForce`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-493714e1df0420c387f471c68b603dce89bf6e7cd4c6684072bec566237f0e33L40-R40) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-493714e1df0420c387f471c68b603dce89bf6e7cd4c6684072bec566237f0e33R54-R63) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-493714e1df0420c387f471c68b603dce89bf6e7cd4c6684072bec566237f0e33L1-R1) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-cf03b70b72f74e21654fe92fce706aa5d637e6842bf7007bf988385704e97da5L1-R1)

### 5. Documentation
- Added a detailed `INSTRUCTIONS.md` with a step-by-step guide for building the GUI, wiring up the Trie, and handling user interactions in a Gboard-style suggestion strip.

These changes collectively provide a robust, testable, and user-friendly auto-complete solution, with clear separation between algorithmic logic, UI, and benchmarking utilities.

body:
## Summary

- After a successful inventory push, the CLI now opens (or reuses) a pull request from `--inventory-branch` into `--detection-branch` on GitHub HTTPS repos, so the inventory repo's `--mode validate` CI check runs and humans can review per PCI DSS 6.4.3.
- PR creation failure fails the run loudly (log + Slack alert + non-zero exit) rather than silently leaving the inventory update unreviewed — compliance-visible by design.
- No new npm dependencies (uses existing `axios`). No new CLI flags — reuses `--inventory-branch`, `--detection-branch`, `--git-token`, `--repo`.

## Deployment note (read before merging)

The existing `INVENTORY_REPO_PAT` must have `pull_requests: write` in addition to `contents: write`. Classic PATs with `repo` scope already have it; fine-grained PATs need the "Pull requests: Read and write" permission added. Without this, the first run post-deploy will push the inventory commit successfully, then fail the PR step and exit 2.

author: gregpriday
body:
## Summary

- `ProcessDetector` previously emitted on/off state changes on every poll cycle, meaning short-lived processes like `claude --version` or `gemini --help` could trigger agent promotion, icon flicker, and stuck states in the UI
- Added a hysteresis gate requiring `HYSTERESIS_THRESHOLD` (2) consecutive polls agreeing on a state change before committing it — at the 2500ms base poll interval that's roughly 5s of confirmation before any transition fires
- Busy and command state emissions are suppressed while a gated transition is pending, closing the side-channel that would otherwise let a one-poll blip bypass the gate

Resolves #5763

## Changes

- `electron/services/ProcessDetector.ts`: added `onStreak`, `offStreak`, and `pendingDetected` tracking; gated all state commits behind `HYSTERESIS_THRESHOLD`; deferred busy/command mutations during pending transitions; flush pending OFF state on `stop()` so exiting processes inside the hysteresis window don't leave ghost UI state
- `electron/services/__tests__/ProcessDetector.test.ts`: 285 lines of new tests covering hysteresis on/off behaviour, streak resets on candidate swaps, busy/command suppression during pending transitions, and stop-flush edge cases

## Testing

Unit tests cover the full hysteresis matrix. Manually verified that running `claude --version` in a terminal no longer causes the agent icon to flash on and then immediately clear.

author: antonioromero1220
body:
## Summary

Single-PR delivery of CMS SDK v1 Phase 1 (ship `@growthub/api-contract`) **and** Phase 2 (make the CLI load-bear on it). The package is no longer speculative — the CLI itself proves it is the canonical source of truth for the CMS contract.

## Phase 1 — `@growthub/api-contract` (commit 1)

New `packages/api-contract/` — types-only public contract package. Freezes the substrate already present in `cli/src/runtime/cms-capability-registry/` and `cli/src/runtime/hosted-execution-client/`, plus the forward-looking manifest envelope and schema-driven node contracts from the v1 spec.

**Modules**

- `capabilities` — `CapabilityFamily`, `CapabilityExecutionKind`, `CapabilityRecord`, `CapabilityNode`, `CapabilityConnectorNode`, `CapabilityQuery`, `CapabilityRegistryMeta`, `CAPABILITY_FAMILIES`
- `execution` — `ExecuteWorkflowInput`, `ExecuteWorkflowResult`, `ExecuteNodePayload`, `NodeResult`, `ExecutionArtifactRef`, `ExecutionSummary`, `ExecutionMode`, `ExecutionStatus`, `NodeExecutionStatus`
- `providers` — `ProviderAssemblyInput`, `ProviderAssemblyResult`, `ProviderRecord`, `ProviderAssemblyHints`, `ProviderStatus`, `ProviderAssemblyStatus`
- `profile` — `Profile`, `ExecutionDefaults`, `Entitlement`, `GatedCapabilityRef`, `PreferredExecutionMode`
- `events` — `ExecutionEvent` union (`node_start`, `node_complete`, `node_error`, `credit_warning`, `progress`, `complete`, `error`)
- `schemas` — `NodeInputSchema`, `NodeOutputSchema`, `NodeInputField` union (`text`, `long_text`, `number`, `boolean`, `select`, `array`, `json`, `url`, `file`, `url_or_file`)
- `manifests` — `CapabilityManifestEnvelope`, `CapabilityManifest`, `ManifestProvenance`, `ManifestDriftReport`, `ManifestSource`, `ManifestOriginType`, `ExecutionHints`

Marked `"private": true` for now to prevent accidental publish. `publishConfig` is wired so flipping to public is a one-line change.

## Phase 2 — CLI adoption (commit 2)

Two boundary `types.ts` files rewritten as re-export shims onto `@growthub/api-contract`, preserving the existing `Cms*` / `Hosted*` aliases so every downstream consumer (10+ files across runtime modules, commands, and node-contract helpers) continues to work unchanged.

**Changes**

- `cli/src/runtime/cms-capability-registry/types.ts` — shim over `@growthub/api-contract/capabilities`
- `cli/src/runtime/hosted-execution-client/types.ts` — shim over `@growthub/api-contract/{execution,providers,profile,capabilities}`
- `cli/package.json` — adds `"@growthub/api-contract": "workspace:*"` dep
- `cli/src/__tests__/api-contract-equivalence.test.ts` — compile-time identity assertions for `CapabilityNode`, `ExecuteWorkflowInput`, `ExecuteWorkflowResult`, `ProviderAssemblyResult`, `Profile`, `CapabilityRecord`

**Net diff: -287 lines / +94 lines in cli.**

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/api-contract`: exit 0 (build + typecheck)
- `tsc --noEmit` on CLI: **zero new errors**. Pre-existing `@paperclipai/*` workspace-resolution errors are unchanged; confirmed by running tsc on the baseline (with Phase 2 stashed).
- `vitest run` on CLI: failure set **byte-identical to baseline** (same 4 tests in the same 10 files fail with and without Phase 2). The new equivalence test passes; `hosted-execution-client.test.ts` still passes.
- `bash scripts/pr-ready.sh`: passes every contract check (dep pin, version sync, dist artifacts, CLI/create package checks).

## Scope discipline (what this PR is NOT)

Per the v1 spec, deliberately deferred to later phases:

- Manifest registry runtime behavior (envelope loader, drift, local extensions)
- Populating `NodeInputSchema` / `NodeOutputSchema` from hosted metadata
- Adoption of the `ExecutionEvent` union across execution surfaces
- Chat lane, environment management, enterprise dashboard, streaming console UX
- Rewrites of hosted route topology or imperative plugin hooks

## Design notes

- `CapabilityRecord` (slim hosted shape) and `CapabilityNode` (normalized client shape) are distinct, matching the existing CLI normalization split.
- `ProviderAssemblyHints` sits beside `ProviderAssemblyResult`, not inside node execution results — execution stays deterministic, provider resolution stays modular.
- `CapabilityRegistryMeta.source` is widened to `"hosted" | "local-extension" | "derived"` to match the Phase 3 manifest envelope contract. The widening is a supertype of the previous `"hosted"` literal, so existing code is forward-compatible.

## Caveat — branch naming

`pr-ready.sh` flags `claude/cms-sdk-v1-contract-wC0ke` as non-conforming to the `fix|feat|chore|...` prefix convention. Branch was assigned by the task contract; rename before merge if repo policy requires it.

## Test plan

- [ ] Reviewer: `pnpm install` (if the server workspace gap is fixed) or `pnpm --filter @growthub/cli install --ignore-workspace` as a local workaround
- [ ] Reviewer: `pnpm --filter @growthub/cli exec tsc --noEmit` — confirm zero new errors in `cms-capability-registry/`, `hosted-execution-client/`, or `api-contract-equivalence.test.ts`
- [ ] Reviewer: `pnpm --filter @growthub/cli exec vitest run api-contract-equivalence hosted-execution-client` — both pass
- [ ] Reviewer: spot-check that deleting `packages/api-contract/` now breaks the CLI (proof that the package is load-bearing)
- [ ] Reviewer: confirm the preserved `Cms*` / `Hosted*` aliases are acceptable as a soft-migration path (vs. a hard rename across all 10+ consumer files)

body:
## Summary

Closes #347. Implements the locked #342 design for the tool-call and session-summary notifications:

- Per-tool-call title reads `${clientLabel} used ${humanize(toolName)}` (e.g. `Claude used Get Steps`, `Unknown (#1) used Get Steps`). Body is the integration display name only; the shade renders the call timestamp natively via `setWhen(eventTimeMillis)`.
- Session summaries partition by `clientLabel` and post one notification per client: `${clientLabel} used ${count} ${tool|tools}`. Body lists up to 3 unique humanized tool names joined naturally (Oxford comma) with `and N more` past the cap.
- Tap deep-links: per-call taps open the audit-history screen with a `scrollToCallId` extra; summary taps open the audit-history screen filtered to the session time window via `startMillis`/`endMillis` extras. `MainActivity` now resolves the start destination from the notification intent action, and the audit destination reads the extras as nav arguments.
- `Manage` action button on both notifications: routes to the integration manage page when a summary's entries all came from one integration (single integration, always, for per-call); drops the user at home when a summary spans multiple integrations.
- Per-client notification ids derived from `clientLabel.hashCode().mod(10_000)` so multi-client sessions don't collide and repeated sessions for the same client replace their previous notification.

Deprecated copy (`Tool call: {toolName}` / `N tool calls across M integrations`) is removed; the old string resources are dropped from `api/values/strings.xml` in favour of the new templates plus a `joinToolNames` helper that is unit-tested in isolation.

Screenshot catalog regenerated: `./gradlew :notifications:recordRoborazziDebug` re-ran the Roborazzi tests with the new copy and refreshed `docs/notifications/index.html` + the 12 affected PNGs under `notifications/screenshots/`.

- LoRA (`generateMandala`) 는 v14 background fire-and-forget 로 2개월째 가동, prewarm + keep_alive=24h 로 warm, `generation_log` 품질 metrics 축적 중 — 인프라 이미 완비.

## 변경
- `fill-missing-actions.ts`: LoRA primary call (`generateMandala` → `actions` 필드만 추출). 수락 조건:

#### Summary
This PR enables support for standard Go middlewares in the `MuxAdapter`. Consuming applications can now wrap Bouncer's REST endpoints with their own logic (such as Authentication, Logging, or Metrics) without needing to modify the core library.

#### Changes
- **`httpmux/routes.go`**: 
    - Updated `RegisterRoutes` signature to accept `mw ...func(http.Handler) http.Handler`.
    - Added an internal `applyMiddlewares` helper function to handle middleware chaining (outermost to innermost).
    - Updated route registration to use `mux.Handle` with wrapped handlers instead of `mux.HandleFunc`.

#### Usage Example
Developers can now secure the Bouncer endpoints during initialization:
```go
adapter := httpmux.New(authz)
mux := http.NewServeMux()

// Inject custom security logic
adapter.RegisterRoutes(mux, myAuthMiddleware, myLogger)
```
- Closes #16

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/vctb12/Gold-Prices/security/code-scanning/7](https://github.com/vctb12/Gold-Prices/security/code-scanning/7)

Best fix: **validate and normalize status values at write time** and **escape status-derived output at render time** before inclusion in any HTML string assigned to `innerHTML`.

In this file (`admin/orders/index.html`), the single best minimal change is to enforce an allowlist for `newStatus` inside `updateOrderStatus(...)` before storing it. This breaks the taint path and preserves functionality (only legitimate workflow statuses are stored). Since the UI already uses allowed transitions, this should not change normal behavior.

Concretely:
- In `updateOrderStatus(id, newStatus, note)`, before writing `orders[idx].status`, normalize to lowercase and ensure it is one of `ORDER_STATUSES`.
- If invalid, return `null` early (or ignore update), preventing persistence of attacker-injected strings that could later reach `innerHTML`.

No import/dependency is required.

## Summary

- **Full end-to-end WhatsApp automation pipeline** — every lead is auto-greeted, qualified by keyword, routed to the right program, and converted without manual intervention
- **8 API endpoints** on Vercel Serverless: WhatsApp webhook, lead intake, weekly check-in, Exly purchase webhook, program generator (Claude API), rate-limited WhatsApp sender, and 2 cron jobs (Sunday check-in + daily nudge)
- **3 brand-consistent HTML forms** (intake, weekly check-in, reschedule) — mobile-first, DM Sans + Cormorant Garamond, matching existing site design
- **Admin ops dashboard** at `/admin` with auth, live stats (leads, conversion rate, active clients by program, pending check-ins, escalations)
- **Safety layer**: PII masking, opt-out handling, rate limiting (1 msg/2hrs), escalation triggers for medical/injury/refund keywords, Claude output safety flags for risky program content

### Architecture

| Layer | Files |
|-------|-------|
| Shared libs | `lib/supabase.js`, `lib/whatsapp.js`, `lib/market.js`, `lib/escalation.js` |
| API endpoints | `api/whatsapp-webhook.js`, `api/lead-intake.js`, `api/checkin-submit.js`, `api/exly-webhook.js`, `api/send-whatsapp.js`, `api/generate-program.js` |

| Database | `supabase/migration.sql` (leads, clients, checkins, programs, messages) |

### Automation Flows

- **Flow A (New Lead)**: WhatsApp message → webhook → insert lead → auto-reply (Hinglish for IN, English otherwise) → nudge at 2hrs → drop at 24hrs
- **Flow B (Qualification)**: Keyword matching → program recommendation + checkout link + intake form
- **Flow C (Conversion)**: Exly purchase webhook → create client → storage folder → onboarding message → Week 1 program for 12wk clients
- **Flow D (Weekly Check-in)**: Sunday cron → send form links → on submit → trigger program generation → nudge if missed
- **Flow E (Program Generation)**: Client data + check-ins → Claude API → JSON workout/nutrition → branded HTML program → Supabase storage → WhatsApp delivery

author: kunalbehbud
body:
Related to #5915

## Summary

`TestDaprWatchdog_Start` used timing-based synchronization by starting `dw.Start(ctx)` in a goroutine, sleeping for 1 second, and then cancelling the context. That makes the test dependent on scheduler timing and machine load, which can become flaky under CI and especially under race instrumentation.

This change makes the test deterministic and single-iteration based instead of wall-clock based. It sets `dw.interval` below `singleIterationDurationThreshold`, so `DaprWatchdog.Start` returns after the first successful iteration. With that in place, the test can call `dw.Start(ctx)` directly and remove the extra goroutine, `time.Sleep`, and manual cancellation path.

## Verification

Ran:

```bash
go test -race -count=50 -run TestDaprWatchdog_Start ./pkg/operator
```

Result: passed successfully.

author: cremafr
body:
### ✅ Checklist

- [x] `npx changeset` was attached.
- [ ] **Covered by automatic tests.** _The fix replaces a Node.js-only import with a cross-platform alternative. Verified manually on iOS Simulator — the `/swap/accepted` call now returns 200. Unit tests for the hashing function could be added as follow-up._
- [x] **Impact of the changes:**
      - Swap completion notification to backend (`/swap/accepted`) on mobile
      - Swap cancellation notification (`/swap/cancelled`) on mobile (same code path)
      - No impact on desktop (Node.js crypto was already working there)

### 📝 Description

**Problem**: The `/swap/accepted` backend notification was silently failing on Ledger Wallet mobile for all swaps. The `createSwapIntentHashes` function in `postSwapState.ts` used `import crypto from "crypto"` — a Node.js built-in module that resolves to `undefined` in React Native. This caused a `TypeError: Cannot read property 'createHash' of undefined` crash. The crash occurred outside the `try/catch` block, and since `setBroadcastTransaction` calls `postSwapAccepted` without `await`, the rejected promise was silently swallowed.

**Fix**: Replaced `import crypto from "crypto"` with `import { sha256 } from "../../crypto"`, which uses `@noble/hashes/sha256` — a pure JavaScript implementation already present in the `@ledgerhq/live-common` dependency tree and used elsewhere in the codebase. This works identically on Node.js (desktop) and React Native (mobile).

**Before**: `crypto.createHash("sha256").update(data).digest("hex")` → crashes on RN
**After**: `sha256(data).toString("hex")` → works everywhere

### ❓ Context

- **JIRA or GitHub link**: [LIVE-29503](https://ledgerhq.atlassian.net/browse/LIVE-29503)

author: cylae
body:
This submission optimizes the core address overlap detection algorithm and improves the robustness of the command-line interface.

The address overlap detection was previously using a linear search, which led to $O(N^2)$ performance issues when processing large register maps. By switching to a dictionary-based lookup, the complexity is reduced to $O(N)$, significantly speeding up the generation process for devices with thousands of registers. The logic also now correctly handles the common Modbus pattern of having multiple bit-level registers at the same base address.

On the CLI side, the tool now gracefully handles malformed mapping files and invalid page specifications, providing clear feedback instead of crashing. It also informs users when certain parameters (like `--pages`) are not applicable to the current file type.

I created a new kind-like that can support hooks and added it to the kind file. Right now it is private but can still be imported from there.

### Resolution
[//]: # (Does the code work as intended?)

[//]: # (How should the change be tested?)

[//]: # (Were any side-effects caused by the change?)
use() is not the same as useContext(). The React docs are explicit: use() can read a Context or a Promise. When passed a Promise, it suspends — and suspension during SSR with renderToString does not work the same way as in a streaming (renderToPipeableStream) environment.

The risk surfaces like this:
js

// If contextType is accidentally a Promise-like object, or if
// use() is passed something that triggers Suspense...
const ctx = use(contextType); // throws a Promise → breaks renderToString

With useContext(contextType) this can't happen — it only accepts a Context object and never suspends.

The original class branch also used static contextType which is immune to this entirely.
The fix

Replace use with useContext in the rewritten component:
js

// Before
import {createContext, use} from 'react';
// ...
const ctx = use(contextType);

// After
import {createContext, useContext} from 'react';
// ...
const ctx = useContext(contextType);

body:
## 概要

Closes #35 (Parent: #5 Phase 4-4)

`KanaAssembler` が出力するカタカナ文字列から、決定論的に当て字漢字を導出する `KanjiAtejiRules.toAteji(kana: String, seed: Long): String` を実装しました。疾患名・医薬品名の日本語要素表層 Layer (KANJI_ATEJI) で使用します。

## 変更内容

### 新規ファイル
- `src/main/kotlin/io/github/corvus400/fictionaldrugdiseaserefmockserver/fixture/naming/KanjiAtejiRules.kt`
- `src/test/kotlin/io/github/corvus400/fictionaldrugdiseaserefmockserver/fixture/naming/KanjiAtejiRulesTest.kt`

### 実装方針
- **候補辞書**: 50 音 (母音 + カ〜ワ行) + 濁音 + 半濁音 + 撥音 + 拗音 (ャュョ) を網羅。`KanaAssembler` が出力し得る全カナをカバー
- **決定論的選択**: `seed xor ATEJI_SLOT_SALT xor (index × ATEJI_INDEX_STRIDE)` で各位置に対し候補から 1 つを選出。同じ `(kana, seed)` なら常に同一出力
- **フォールバック**: 未登録カナは `无` (U+65E0) で補完し、出力が常に CJK Unified Ideographs (0x4E00..0x9FFF) に収まることを保証
- スタイル: 既存 `KanaAssembler` のハッシュ撹拌パターンを踏襲 (`pickPositive` による正値化)

## TDD サイクル

Issue 仕様通りに Red → Green → Refactor の 1 サイクルを完結:

1. **Red1**: 決定論性 — 同じ `(kana, seed)` に対し同一出力
2. **Red2**: 長さ整合 — 出力漢字列の長さ = 入力カナ列の長さ (1 カナ = 1 漢字)
3. **Red3**: 全て漢字 — 出力文字が全て CJK Unified Ideographs (0x4E00..0x9FFF) に収まる

中間段階で空実装 (`fun toAteji(...) = ""`) を経由し、アサーション失敗の Red を目視確認してから本実装に進みました (Issue #5 R4 遵守)。

## テストプラン

- [x] `./gradlew test --tests "*.fixture.naming.KanjiAtejiRulesTest"` → 3 件全件 green
- [x] `./gradlew spotlessCheck` → 通過
- [x] `./gradlew detektMain` → 通過
- [x] `./gradlew test` (全件) → 既存テストへの影響なし、全件 green

## 不変条件 (t-wada TDD)

**これまで動いていたコードは変わらず動き、かつ、新しいコードも動いている**: 既存の `StableHash` / `FictionLanguage` / `KanaAssembler` テストは変更なしで全件 green のまま、`KanjiAtejiRulesTest` 3 件が追加で green。

- 先行: #37 (Phase 4-1 StableHash) / #33 (Phase 4-2 FictionLanguage) — 共に main にマージ済み

author: siddseethepalli
body: ## Summary - TDZ fix: each plugins/defaults/.ts module now registers itself at module-load via a local side effect. Previously, defaults/index.ts ran `registerDefaultPlugins()` at module-top-level, which TDZ-crashed because `memory-retrieval.ts` → `conversation-runtime-assembly.ts` → … → `agent/loop.ts` → `plugins/pipeline.ts` (which side-effect-imports defaults/index.ts) re-entered defaults/index.ts while memory-retrieval.ts was still mid-load — so the `ALL_DEFAULT_PLUGINS` array hit an uninitialized live binding on `defaultMemoryRetrievalPlugin`. Self-registration attaches each call to the already-initialized per-file plugin identifier, and the former top-level array is now a `getAllDefaultPlugins()` function so its reads are deferred until after the cycle resolves. - conversation-queue.test.ts race fix: two attachment tests were exhibiting a pre-existing race — the test mock invoked `run.onEvent({ type: 'message_complete' })` synchronously (fire-and-forget) and then resolved `agentLoop.run()` immediately, but the async `handleMessageComplete` → persistence pipeline had not yet set `state.lastAssistantMessageId`, so the downstream `resolveAssistantAttachments` received `undefined` and `attachments[0].id` was missing. The real agent loop in `agent/loop.ts` awaits `onEvent(...)` before returning from `run()`; the test now does the same via `await run.onEvent(...)` to preserve production semantics. Part of plan: agent-plugin-system.md (CI fix 2) ---

- **F1 (medium)**: `userId` and other internal entity fields are no longer leaked in the API response. Explicit `toLicenseResponseDto` mapper in the controller.
- **F2 (low)**: `handleAccountDeleted` now uses isolated try/catch blocks with distinctive log tags (`SUBSCRIPTION_CANCELLATION_FAILED` / `LICENSE_REVOCATION_FAILED`) so failures surface for alerting.

## Bug found and fixed during E2E testing
- **wrapError lost HTTP status**: `PaymentController.wrapError` was hardcoding `statusCode: 500` for all non-RpcException errors. The E2E test for "licence belongs to another user" was returning 500 instead of 404. Fixed: `wrapError` now detects `HttpException` instances and preserves `error.getStatus()`. Unit test assertion strengthened to verify `statusCode === 404` on the NotFoundException path (not just "is RpcException"). See commit `fc39dbd`.

## Breaking change
`OrderItemWithProduct.productSnapshot` is now required. No production callers impacted — `LicenseService.generateForOrder` is still not wired to the webhook (see follow-up below).

## Follow-up needed (NOT in this PR)
`LicenseService.generateForOrder()` is never called today. Wire it from `WebhookService.handlePaymentSucceeded()` in a separate PR so the table actually gets populated on purchase. Without this, licenses must be inserted manually for testing.

## Pre-existing issue surfaced
`npm run lint` reports one unused import in `apps/payment-service/src/services/payment.service.ts` (`Subscription`) — **not introduced by this branch**, present on main. Out of scope to fix here.
