body: ## Summary Rediseño completo de la identidad visual en dos superficies donde el app no estaba a la altura del resto del diseño: **app icon** (home screen iOS/Android) y **share card** (preview en WhatsApp/Telegram/Twitter). Plus: fix defensivo de un leak de clave i18n al compartir invitaciones de Duel. ## Cambios ### 1. App icon — "S." serif (match del wordmark de Home) Basado en `js/screens.jsx:768` donde el Home renderiza `Stirio.` en `var(--f-serif)` con el punto en amber. - **`icon_pwa.svg`** (reescrito): 512×512 rounded 96px, fondo `#0d0508`, radial gradients amber (superior derecha) y cyan sutil (inferior izquierda) imitando el body de la app. Wordmark "S." centrado: S en crema `#f6f3ea`, punto amber `#c9971c` con halo gaussiano. - **`icon_ios.png`** (regenerado 256×256): sin rounded corners (iOS aplica su propia máscara — evita double-rounding). - **`favicon.svg`** (reescrito): mismo treatment simplificado en viewport 100×100 para el tab del browser. Preview generado: - iOS icon (256×256): serif "S" crema + punto amber sobre oscuro, alto contraste vs iconos vecinos tipo Telegram/Jobday. ### 2. OG / share card (WhatsApp/Telegram/Twitter) - **`og-image.svg`** (nuevo, source editable): 1200×630, fondo oscuro con glow amber, wordmark "Stirio." grande, tagline mono "APRENDE COCTELERÍA · 60 SEGUNDOS", silueta martini decorativa. - **`og-image.png`** (nuevo, rasterizado 143 KB). - **`index.html`**: 11 meta tags nuevos (`og:type`, `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image`, `og:url`, `twitter:card=summary_large_image`, etc.). Los scrapers no ejecutan JS → una sola versión en español (idioma default). ### 3. Fix leak `duel.invite_text` En el screenshot del usuario, al compartir por WhatsApp aparecía literalmente `duel.invite_text https://...` — la clave filtrada en lugar del texto traducido. Ocurría por race: si el tap en Share llegaba antes de que `preloadAllTranslations()` terminara, `stLang.t()` devolvía la clave. - **`js/duel.jsx` `shareInvite`**: `await window.stLang.preloadAllTranslations()` antes de `navigator.share()`. El helper `dTrParams` ya tenía el fallback correcto, este es el safety net que cierra la ventana de race. ### 4. Build tooling - **`scripts/build-icons.mjs`** (nuevo): usa `@resvg/resvg-js` (devDep) para rasterizar los dos SVGs a sus PNGs. `npm run build:icons` los regenera cuando se edita el diseño. NO corre en CI — se hace manualmente al actualizar la marca. - **`package.json`**: +1 script, +1 devDep (`@resvg/resvg-js` ~5 MB). ### 5. SW cache - Bump `STATIC_CACHE_VERSION` v10.50 → v10.51. - Nuevos paths cacheados: `icon_pwa.svg`, `icon_ios.png`, `og-image.svg`, `og-image.png`. ### Nota sobre "icon per theme" No es viable para el home screen — iOS/Android cachean el icon al instalar el PWA y no hay API para re-publicarlo. Sí es factible para el favicon del tab (JS swap en `[data-theme]`) como follow-up; esta tanda ship el icono fijo "match Home" por defecto. ## Test plan - [x] `npm test` → 267/267 verde. - [x] `npm run build:icons` regenera los dos PNGs sin errores. - [ ] Abrir `index.html` local: el favicon del tab debe mostrar "S." serif. - [ ] DevTools → Application → Manifest: icon preview coincide con el nuevo SVG. - [ ] iOS real / simulador: "Añadir a pantalla de inicio" → el nuevo icon debe verse como el wordmark de Home con alto contraste vs iconos bold vecinos. - [ ] Validar OG con `https://www.opengraph.xyz/url/` — debe mostrar la card 1200×630. - [ ] Compartir un código de Duel a WhatsApp → texto debe leer "¡Reto en Stirio! Únete con el código XXXXX", nunca la clave literal. https://claude.ai/code/session_01BeiCrcQM7sf3oPr1tNfkLE

author: hon454
body:
## Summary

- Collapse the two-click "+ Add another account" → "Add account" sequence on the options page into a single click by starting the GitHub device flow directly from the outer button handler.
- Keep the Cancel path sensible by unmounting the panel back to the entry button when the user cancels during the `waiting` phase.
- Fix the follow-up regression from the controller lift so reopening the panel after one successful connect starts a fresh device flow instead of getting stuck on the stale `connected` state.
- Surface the repository's PR workflow from AGENTS.md and adopt the expanded PR template as the default so this kind of UX gap does not slip through a future PR audit.

## Why

Two buttons captured the same user intent ("I want to add an account"), so the second click was pure friction. The re-authentication path reuses the same panel, so the same friction hit users coming back after a token invalidation. The StrictMode-safe controller lift fixed the double-start problem, but it also exposed a new multi-account regression: after one successful connect, reopening the panel reused the terminal controller state and no longer kicked off a second device flow. While auditing the resulting PR against `docs/guidelines/pr-guideline.md` we also noticed the PR guideline was effectively invisible from AGENTS.md and the repo still shipped with a minimal PR template, both of which contributed to a first-pass PR body that missed required sections.

## Changes

- Options UX: `OptionsPage` now owns the device-flow controller so it survives StrictMode remounts, and `openAddPanel()` starts the flow directly from the click/re-auth handler instead of relying on an `AddAccountPanel` mount effect. The add-account guard now blocks only while the controller is actively in flight (`initiating`, `waiting`, `fetching_installations`) so terminal phases (`connected`, `expired`, `denied`, `fatal`) can restart cleanly.
- Panel behavior: `AddAccountPanel` now renders the `idle` phase as the existing "Requesting device code..." loading view, accepts an `onCancel` prop, and returns to the outer `+ Add another account` button when the user cancels from `waiting` or closes a `fatal` state.
- Test coverage: `tests/options-page.test.ts` now covers four key paths: single-click auto-start, Cancel collapsing the panel, reopening after a successful connect triggering a second `initiateDeviceFlow` call, and React StrictMode not double-starting the device flow.
- Docs (bundled): AGENTS.md gains a dedicated `## Pull Request Policy` section listing the required PR body sections. `docs/manual-chrome-testing.md` reflects the single-click add-account flow. `.github/pull_request_template.md` is replaced with the expanded Summary/Why/Changes/Impact/Testing/Breaking Changes/Related Issues shape, and `docs/guidelines/pr-guideline.md` is updated to make the expanded template canonical with per-section writing guidance.

## Impact

- User-facing impact: one fewer click to add or re-authenticate a GitHub account, Cancel now returns the user to the entry button instead of a dead-end idle screen, and multi-account users can successfully start a second device-flow session after the first account connects.
- API/schema impact: None. `device-flow-controller.ts` keeps the same state machine and storage/API contracts.
- Performance impact: None.
- Operational or rollout impact: None for the UX change. The PR-template change affects every future PR opened through the web UI; the new template requires more sections but GitHub auto-populates them. `gh pr create --body` still bypasses the template, which the updated AGENTS.md now calls out explicitly.

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests
- [ ] Integration tests
- [ ] Manual testing

### Test details

- `pnpm lint`: pass
- `pnpm typecheck`: pass
- `pnpm test`: pass (82/82)
- Manual: not yet run — pending maintainer execution via `pnpm dev` + unpacked extension: click `+ Add another account` and verify the GitHub device code appears without a second button click, click Cancel during the waiting phase and verify the panel collapses back to the `+ Add another account` button, complete one end-to-end device-flow sign-in, then reopen the panel and verify a second device-flow session starts successfully.

## Breaking Changes

- None

## Related Issues

No issue: UX polish and PR-workflow hardening caught during a maintainer-driven review session; no prior tracking ticket.

### Motivation
- OMR can mis-detect solo key signatures, leaving notes with `alter=0`/no `<alter>` or explicit `<accidental>natural</accidental>` which conflicts with later key alignment and causes OSMD/Tone playback to treat them as naturals.
- The sanitized MusicXML was only used for rendering, so playback received the unpatched XML and produced incorrect pitches (e.g. F instead of F#).

### Description
- Apply `sanitizeForOsmd` to the backend `music_xml` immediately after `analyzePdf` returns in `handleSelect` so rendering and playback use the same corrected XML (`frontend/src/App.tsx`).
- Update `dropNaturalAccidentalsContradictingKey` to consider missing/zero `alter` as natural and to write an explicit `<alter>` matching the implied key accidental (or overwrite existing `alter`) instead of removing it, and to remove contradictory `<accidental>natural</accidental>` (`frontend/src/music/sanitize.ts`).
- Adjust tests in `frontend/src/music/__tests__/sanitize.test.ts` to expect the normalized `<alter>` (e.g. `"1"`) for key-implied sharps after sanitization.

body:
Adds a purely visual golden spectral cloak extension that grows from the player's shoulder when swinging on the grapple hook and dissipates with golden particle scatter on release. Zero gameplay/physics impact.

## New: `PhantomCloakExtension` (`src/render/clusters/phantomCloak.ts`)

- **Chain**: 6 trailing points rooted at the main cloak's tip — making total visible cloak 3× normal length (normal 3-seg + phantom 6-seg)
- **Growth**: Activates on `isGrappleActiveFlag === 1`; grows shoulder→tip at `BASE_GROWTH_RATE + playerSpeed × SPEED_GROWTH_MULTIPLIER` segments/sec
- **Dissolution**: On grapple release, dissolves base→tip at `DISSIPATION_SPEED` segs/sec; each consumed segment emits golden scatter particles
- **Simulation**: Same integration logic as `PlayerCloak` (velocity inheritance, gravity, rest-bias, distance constraints) — no independent physics
- **Rendering**: Golden fill `#c89600` at 52% alpha / amber outline at 30% — drawn at Layer 0 (before back cloak) so main cloak stays readable on top; particles drawn at Layer 4 (after front cloak)

author: sebastiendieudonne
body:
## Summary
- Ajoute l'endpoint interne `PUT /care/companies/{companyId}/labels/{labelId}/person` pour permettre au Care de rattacher un label à un autre contact (stakeholder) d'une company via Postman, au lieu de passer par une modification directe en base de données.
- Validations : label ∈ company (MapEntity), résolution du `Stakeholder` via `(company, user_id)` avec **400** si le user n'est pas stakeholder de la company, **409** explicite avec l'id du label bloquant si le stakeholder est déjà rattaché à un autre label, et revalidation complète de l'entité avec les groupes `[DEFAULT, UPDATE]` pour jouer les BusinessRule (notamment `LabelWithPersonAssociateOrEIDirectorIsOk`).
- Idempotent : si le label a déjà ce stakeholder comme `person`, retour 204 immédiat sans flush.

## Contexte

Le Care reçoit régulièrement des demandes du type :
> Dossier : RAYA PROPRETE SERVICES
> id company : 146106
> label id : 40663341
> Pouvez-vous rattacher le label ci-dessus avec le contact UDREA Mihaela (user id : 176490) ?

Aujourd'hui, les devs font la modification directement en base (update `label.person_id`), après avoir vérifié manuellement que les companies correspondent et qu'il n'existe pas déjà un label avec ce stakeholder. Cet endpoint outille cette opération pour permettre au Care d'agir de façon autonome via Postman, tout en conservant les invariants métier (validation `LabelWithPersonAssociateOrEIDirectorIsOk`, unicité, etc.).

L'endpoint reste interne (role `CARE` requis) et n'est **pas** exposé à l'app Expert classique.

## Test plan
- [ ] Lancer le test fonctionnel `PutLabelPersonEndpointTest` (cas nominal 204, conflit 409, body invalide 400).
- [ ] Tester manuellement en local via Postman : `PUT /v1/care/companies/{companyId}/labels/{labelId}/person` avec body `{"user_id": <id>}`.
- [ ] Vérifier que le rattachement d'un stakeholder non-associate / non-EI-director est bien refusé (400 via `ValidationFailedException` → `ThrowableSubscriber`).

author: ralbagi
body:
## Summary

- The nightly pipeline was silently skipped on 2026-04-21 because `git fetch` ran without credentials from the systemd-user service (GNOME keyring unreachable after a user-manager restart, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` → exit 128). `scripts/run-daily-pipeline.sh` now resolves a token up-front (`GITHUB_TOKEN` → `gh auth token` fallback) and scopes `GIT_ASKPASS` **inline per git command** so no subprocess inherits the helper path.
- The miss exposed a secondary bug: every treemap brick on 2026-04-22 went gray because `annotateMarketTimeline` suppressed `market_delta_points` whenever the previous record wasn't the immediately preceding calendar day. Introduced a configurable `maxDeltaDays` gap (default 1 for strict UI callers; pipeline/backfill use `PIPELINE_MAX_DELTA_DAYS = 2`) so one missed day still yields a valid 2-day delta.
- Regenerated `timeseries_summary.json`, `party_summary.json`, and `details/2026-04-22.json` in place so production recovers without waiting for another pipeline run.

## What's in this PR

| Commit | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `8233b65` `fix(pipeline)` | Initial GIT_ASKPASS wiring + token resolution |
| `df6352e` `fix(market)` | Bounded-gap delta + regenerated data for 2026-04-22 |
| `4de82e9` `refactor(pipeline)` | First review pass: moved askpass below cleanup trap, baked token into helper, dropped env exposure |
| `0b4c2c0` `fix: resolve code review findings` | Second review pass (Codex): scoped `GIT_ASKPASS` inline per command, tightened `PIPELINE_MAX_DELTA_DAYS` 3→2, early trap covers EXIT so lock drops on token failure, token required only for HTTPS remotes, extracted helpers to `scripts/lib/pipeline-auth.sh`, added runtime bash tests |

## Why this is safe

- **No `GIT_ASKPASS` export.** The helper (chmod 700, owner-only) has the token baked in, but its path is never visible in any subprocess env. `npm ci`, `node data-pipeline/generateDailyScores.js`, `npx firebase-tools`, `curl` run without knowing auth exists.
- **SSH-remote compatible.** Token resolution only runs when `is_https_remote` returns true. SSH deploy-key setups are unaffected.
- **No retroactive data surprises.** Both real historical gaps in the timeseries (2026-03-16→18 and 2026-04-20→22) are 2-day gaps, so tightening `maxDeltaDays` from 3 to 2 produces identical data — no regeneration needed.
- **Default behavior preserved for UI callers.** `annotateMarketTimeline` defaults to `maxDeltaDays: 1`, so anything that calls it from the frontend gets the pre-change strict contract. Only the pipeline and backfill opt into the lenient gap.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash scripts/validate-pipeline-script.sh` — passes, including the new `create_askpass_helper` check, `export GIT_ASKPASS=` rejection, and bare-`git-fetch/pull/push` detection
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 1002/1002 tests pass across 77 files
- [x] `npx vitest run --coverage --config vitest.unit.config.js` — `marketScore.js` statement coverage 86%
- [x] `npx eslint src/ tests/` — clean
- [x] `npx prettier --check "src/**/*.{js,jsx,ts,tsx,css,json}"` — clean
- [x] `npx vite build` — passes (bundle sizes unchanged)
- [x] `gh auth token` → `.env.pipeline` already set on the runner; the timer will fire tonight at 02:00 IDT with the new script active on `main`
- [ ] After merge: watch `journalctl --user -u politymarket-pipeline.service` tomorrow and confirm `chore(data): daily pipeline update [2026-04-23]` lands on main
- [ ] Spot-check the treemap in momentum lens on production after tomorrow's run — bricks should show colored deltas, not gray

## Static guards added

- `scripts/validate-pipeline-script.sh`: rejects bare `git fetch/pull/push`, rejects `export GIT_ASKPASS=`, requires `create_askpass_helper` usage
- `tests/unit/pipeline-auth.unit.test.js`: 10 static invariants on the main script (no-export, inline-prefix, unset-after-create, askpass-after-trap, EXIT-trap-early, HTTPS-gate, etc.)
- `tests/unit/pipeline-auth-runtime.unit.test.js`: 6 runtime bash tests on `scripts/lib/pipeline-auth.sh` (resolve fallback chain, askpass 700 perms + Username/Password dispatch, HTTPS/SSH/no-origin detection)
- `src/lib/marketScore.test.js`: `pins PIPELINE_MAX_DELTA_DAYS to the one-missed-day contract` test — any future bump is a deliberate choice, not drift

author: suleymanemirgergin
body:
## Summary

Two sets of fixes bundled:

### 1. CI deploy gating (commit 867a4c8)

Master's post-merge CI (sha `05ce6f5`) showed red X's on 2 deploy jobs unrelated to app correctness:

- **Deploy Backend → Railway** — failed: empty `RAILWAY_SERVICE_ID` variable
- **🚀 Deploy Contracts → Testnet** — failed: missing `libdbus-1-dev` on runner

Fix: both jobs now opt-in via repo variables. When unset, skip cleanly. When set, run normally with the system deps installed.

### 2. Railway healthcheck (commit ba8f686)

User reported Railway deploy failing with 6× 'service unavailable' on `/health/live` over 2 minutes.

Root cause: `await app.listen(port)` in `main.ts` defaults to `127.0.0.1`. Inside a Docker container, that means the process is unreachable from Railway's proxy layer. The Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK (internal) would pass, but external checks never connect.

Fixes:
- `main.ts`: `app.listen(port, '0.0.0.0')` — reachable from the container network
- `Dockerfile`: HEALTHCHECK uses `${PORT:-3001}` so it follows whatever port Railway injects
- `Dockerfile`: added `prisma migrate deploy` before `node dist/main.js` so fresh Railway environments don't boot into a broken DB. Guarded with `|| echo` so DATABASE_URL typos don't cause restart loops.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean (backend + frontend)
- [x] CI checks pass on PR (Frontend Build, Lint, Tests, E2E)
- [ ] Merge → master CI passes with all green/skipped (no more red X on Railway/Contract deploy jobs)

body:
Fixes #

Follow-up to #48213 (Jetpack: wpcomsh sync of recovery-mode state) and Automattic/wpcom#212459 (wpcom: `POST /sites/{blog_id}/recovery-mode-status` endpoint + storage as blog option `jetpack_recovery_mode_status`).

## Proposed changes
<!--- Explain what functional changes your PR includes -->
* Adds `jetpack_recovery_mode_status` to the `options` bucket of the `GET /rest/v1.1/sites/:siteId` response, so wpcom consumers can surface recovery-mode state for Jetpack/Atomic sites.
* SAL base (`sal/class.json-api-site-base.php`): new `get_jetpack_recovery_mode_status()` accessor that returns the option value if it's an array, otherwise `array()` (same defensive pattern as `get_site_goals()`).
* GET site endpoint (`json-endpoints/class.wpcom-json-api-get-site-endpoint.php`):
  - Registers `jetpack_recovery_mode_status` in `$site_options_format`.
  - Adds a `case 'jetpack_recovery_mode_status':` branch in `render_option_keys()` that dispatches to the new accessor.
  - Adds the key to `$jetpack_response_option_additions` so Jetpack/Atomic sites get the option decorated from the wpcom-side value.

The returned shape matches what is stored by wpcom: an associative array with `recovery_mode_email_last_sent`, `recovery_session_entered_at`, `recovery_session_exited_at` (all Unix timestamps). An empty array means no recovery-mode signal has been recorded yet.

## Related product discussion/links
<!-- If you're an Automattician, include a shortlink to the P2, Slack, and/or Linear discussions here. -->
* Jetpack upstream: #48213

## Does this pull request change what data or activity we track or use?
<!--- If so, please add the "[Status] Needs Privacy Updates" label and explain what changes there are. -->
No. This only exposes an existing site-level option (already stored on wpcom by the linked PRs) through the existing sites endpoint — it does not collect any new data.

## Testing instructions
<!-- If you were reviewing this PR, how would you like the instructions to be presented? -->
1. Apply this branch to a Jetpack-connected test site (a Jurassic Ninja site with wpcomsh works well) and ensure the wpcom-side counterpart (Automattic/wpcom#212459) is deployed.
2. Confirm the base case: query `GET /rest/v1.1/sites/<blog_id>?fields=options` and verify the response's `options` object now contains a `jetpack_recovery_mode_status` key. With no recovery event recorded, the value should be `[]` (empty array).
3. Trigger the sync by having the site enter recovery mode (e.g. force a fatal from a mu-plugin and click the recovery email link) — or, more directly, update the `jetpack_recovery_mode_status` blog option on wpcom to a non-empty array via an internal tool.
4. Re-query the sites endpoint and verify the `options.jetpack_recovery_mode_status` payload now reflects the expected keys: `recovery_mode_email_last_sent`, `recovery_session_entered_at`, `recovery_session_exited_at`.
5. Verify the field is only surfaced to callers with edit rights (it's under `options`, which is gated by the existing `$no_member_fields` logic — a logged-out request should not see it).

author: jezdez
body:
Closes #21.

Until now `conda workspace add` and `conda workspace remove` only edited the manifest, so quick-adding a package from inside `conda workspace shell` left you with a stale environment and no `python -c "import foo"`. This matches what pixi does with `pixi add` / `pixi remove` and fixes the workflow called out in the issue.

## What changes

After the manifest edit both commands now resolve the affected environments, install into their prefixes, and refresh `conda.lock`. The heavy lifting lives in a new `conda_workspaces/cli/workspace/sync.py` module that is also used by `conda workspace install`, so there is a single canonical solve / install / lock pipeline.

"Affected environments" is computed from the target feature: touching the default feature re-syncs every environment that does not set `no-default-feature = true`; touching a named feature re-syncs only the environments whose `features` list includes it.

## Opt-outs

Mirroring pixi and conda's existing flags:

- `--no-install` — update the manifest and lockfile, skip the prefix install.
- `--no-lockfile-update` — update the manifest only (the old behaviour).
- `--force-reinstall` — recreate the affected environment(s) from scratch.
- `--dry-run` — solve only, touch nothing on disk.

## Inside `conda workspace shell`

When a newly installed package drops an `etc/conda/activate.d/` hook and we are running inside a spawned shell (`CONDA_SPAWN=1`), the command prints a hint to exit and re-run `conda workspace shell` so the hook is picked up. Conda itself cannot retroactively source activation scripts into a parent process.

## Other bits

- Moves the `activate.d` directory listing helper into `conda_workspaces/envs.py` as the public `activate_d_scripts` function, next to `_apply_activation_scripts` which already owns writes into the same directory.
- `execute_install` now delegates to `sync_environments` instead of running its own copy of the pipeline.
- `DESIGN.md` gains a new "Add/Remove Auto-Install" section under Key Design Decisions plus a matching row in the pixi compatibility table.

## Tests

- `tests/cli/workspace/test_sync.py` — new module covering `affected_environments` (one parametrized test across default / named / no-default-feature / unknown) and `sync_environments` (pipeline flag matrix, `activate.d` hint inside vs outside a spawn).
- `tests/cli/workspace/test_add_remove.py` — auto-install cases consolidated with stacked `@pytest.mark.parametrize` across `{add, remove}` × `{default, named feature, --no-lockfile-update, flag matrix}`.
- `tests/cli/workspace/test_install.py` and `tests/test_integration.py` — updated to patch the helpers at their new home in `sync.py`.

Full suite: 762 passed, 1 skipped. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

## AGENTS.md

One small companion commit tightens the testing conventions in `AGENTS.md`: explicit ban on `unittest.mock`, concrete examples of forbidden section comments, a pointer at stacked parametrize + `ids=[...]`, and a lint loop that now spells out both `ruff check` and `ruff format --check`.

author: saurabhjain1592
body:
## Summary

Patch release deprecating `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` as an AxonFlow telemetry opt-out. Behavior is unchanged — `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` still disables telemetry today. What's new is a one-time warning emitted the first time the opt-out fires with `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` set and `AXONFLOW_TELEMETRY=off` not also set, pointing operators at the canonical switch.

Removal target: **after 2026-05-05 in the next major release.** `AXONFLOW_TELEMETRY=off` remains the canonical AxonFlow-specific opt-out.

## Why

`DO_NOT_TRACK=1` is a widely-understood privacy convention in dev tooling. It is set broadly across CI environments and corporate shells, often as a blanket policy, not as an intentional decision about AxonFlow specifically. When it silently disables AxonFlow telemetry, operators don't know it happened.

This is the middle path between honoring `DO_NOT_TRACK` forever (status quo — commercially blind) and ignoring it overnight (trust-breaking). Announce deprecation now, warn during the transition window, remove in the next major. Users who genuinely want AxonFlow telemetry off can set the AxonFlow-specific switch; users whose `DO_NOT_TRACK` comes from a generic policy can opt in intentionally if they want the signal on.

## What changed

- Opt-out path: adds the one-time warning when `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` is the active control and `AXONFLOW_TELEMETRY=off` is not also set.
- README: promotes `AXONFLOW_TELEMETRY=off` to canonical, notes the deprecation + timeline.
- CHANGELOG: new `### Deprecated` section under the patch version.
- Version manifests bumped to patch (package.json / plugin.json / marketplace.json as applicable).

## Related

- Sibling PRs in the 3 other plugins landing the same deprecation warning (claude/cursor/codex/openclaw).
- v7.4.0 SDK release train: sdk-go#127, sdk-typescript#180, sdk-python#146, sdk-java#135
- axonflow-docs#417 (telemetry page update)
- axonflow-enterprise#1678 (CHANGELOG note under v7.4.0 Community)

## Test plan

- [x] Bash plugins (claude/cursor/codex): verified behavioral tests pass — warning fires only when `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` is the active control
- [x] OpenClaw: 11/11 existing telemetry tests pass; module-level sentinel keeps the warning to at most one emission per process
- [x] `AXONFLOW_TELEMETRY=off` alone — silent
- [x] Both set — silent (already migrated)
- [x] Neither set — normal telemetry path unchanged

author: jdeschamps
body:
## Description

For CARE, we would usually load the best checkpoint, while for N2V/N2N we would load the last checkpoint.

This PR introduces the following:
- Add `checkpoint` parameter to `predict` and `predict_to_disk`
- If `None`, `checkpoint` defaults to `last` for N2V and N2N, and `best` for the others (CARE)
- Removed best checkpoint loading utility from `model_utils` and `CAREModule`
- Following https://github.com/CAREamics/careamics/pull/823:
    - Added `get_checkpoints` and adapted to return all checkpoint Paths 
    - Refactored all checkpoint root path into a single method
- Added a `self.run_version` and a simple run version mechanism (`careamics.utils.get_run_version`): the reason is that otherwise checkpoints are all pulled into the same folder if the experiment name does not change. In the mean time, logs are versioned by Lightning. Here, `CAREamist` starts at `0` and inspect the checkpoint folder for any `<experiment_name>_X` and record the current run version as `X+1`. The version is also passed to the logger to maintain the same version between logs and checkpoints.


## Example

Multiple runs of experiment named `my_exp` in working directory `experiments`.

```python
from careamics.careamist import CAREamist
from careamics.config.factories import create_advanced_n2v_config
import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path

# create a configuration
config = create_advanced_n2v_config(
    experiment_name="my_exp",
    data_type="array",
    axes="YX",
    patch_size=[64, 64],
    batch_size=16,
    num_epochs=2,
    num_steps=10,
)

# instantiate a careamist
careamist = CAREamist(config, work_dir=root / "experiments")
careamist.train(
    train_data=[np.random.rand(512, 512)],

)
```




``` bash
my_exp
├── checkpoints
│        ├── my_exp_0
│        ├── my_exp_1
│        ├── my_exp_2
│        └──my_exp_3
└── csv_logs
         ├── version_0
         ├── version_1
         ├── version_2
         └──version_3
```

Where each version number corresponds to each other.

Note that removing `my_exp_3` will cause the next run to re-create it and overwrite `csv_logs/version_3`.

Resolves #606
Resolves #305
Closes #823

author: irishsmurf
body:
🚨 Severity: MEDIUM
💡 Vulnerability: User-controlled input (`email_address`) was passed directly to the `check_email` API call as a raw HTTP header `{"email_address": email}` without prior sanitization for carriage return (`\r`) and line feed (`\n`) characters.
🎯 Impact: While standard Python HTTP libraries (like `requests`) might currently prevent severe header injection by throwing exceptions, failing to explicitly sanitize at the application boundary risks unhandled crashes or edge cases where an attacker could inject arbitrary headers or split HTTP requests if the underlying HTTP client logic changes.
🔧 Fix: Explicitly validated the `email` argument at the application boundary inside `check_email` to reject `\r` and `\n` characters by raising a clean `ValueError`, ensuring safe and predictable failure.
✅ Verification: Ensure tests pass via `pytest tests/unit/test_client.py`. A new unit test, `test_check_email_rejects_crlf`, has been added to guarantee that this rejection functions as intended.

author: mandar1045
body: ## Current CI status GitHub is still blocking the required `PR Update / required` job before the normal CI jobs run. This is not failing on the code path in this PR. The workflow gate says this external-contributor PR needs the `run-ci` label added by a maintainer with write access after the latest SHA. I tried to add the label, but GitHub rejected it because my account does not have `AddLabelsToLabelable` permission. Maintainer action needed: - Add the `run-ci` label to trigger CI. - Add one approving review with write access before merge. Local verification on the latest branch: ```bash TZ=UTC yarn test packages/features/busyTimes/services/getBusyTimes.test.ts yarn type-check:ci --force yarn biome check packages/features/busyTimes/services/getBusyTimes.ts packages/features/busyTimes/services/getBusyTimes.test.ts git diff --check origin/main...HEAD ``` All of the above passed locally. Biome exited 0 and only reported existing info/nursery diagnostics. ## What changed This PR fixes a subtle availability limit bug in `getBusyTimesForLimitChecks`. Previously, limit checks only fetched bookings that were fully contained inside the period being checked. That meant a booking could be ignored if it crossed the edge of a day, week, or month. Example: ```text Checked day: Apr 24 00:00 -> Apr 24 23:59 Booking: Apr 24 23:30 -> Apr 25 00:30 ``` That booking clearly touches Apr 24, but the old query could miss it because the booking ended outside the checked day. The query now uses interval overlap logic: ```text booking.start < checkedRange.end booking.end > checkedRange.start ``` That is the usual way to ask, "does this booking intersect this period at all?" ## Why it matters Booking and duration limits should count every booking that overlaps the period they are enforcing. If we miss edge-crossing bookings, Cal can under-count usage and leave slots available when the configured limit should already be exhausted. This is especially important for: - daily booking limits - weekly/monthly booking limits - duration limits - bookings that cross midnight or sit near period boundaries ## How I verified it - Added a regression test proving `getBusyTimesForLimitChecks` now fetches overlapping bookings. - Ran the focused test file: ```bash TZ=UTC yarn test packages/features/busyTimes/services/getBusyTimes.test.ts ``` - Ran the repo type check: ```bash yarn type-check:ci --force ``` - Ran Biome on the changed files: ```bash yarn biome check packages/features/busyTimes/services/getBusyTimes.ts packages/features/busyTimes/services/getBusyTimes.test.ts ``` - Checked the diff for whitespace issues: ```bash git diff --check origin/main...HEAD ``` ## Screenshots

author: kennypy
body:
Three pieces of the agent workspace land together:

1. Dead-letter paging. When an outbound job flips to dead_letter — either directly on auth/permanent errors or after the reconcile loop exhausts its attempts — the pager fires a Slack-blocks-shaped payload (also PagerDuty-compatible) to SUPPORT_DEAD_LETTER_WEBHOOK_URL. Paging is best-effort and never fails the worker; the row is already persisted. A dead-letter is now a "human-needs-to-look" push, not a silent database state.

2. Idempotency-Key seam. The outbound_job UUID is threaded through VintageClient.post as opts.idempotencyKey and is passed by both the dispatcher and the reconcile loop. The header is NOT emitted on the wire yet — ENABLE_IDEMPOTENCY_HEADER is false pending Vintage's contract update. Flipping the flag is the only change when the contract lands; all call sites are already wired.

3. Agent-facing API + inbox UI. /api/v1/support-tickets covers list (with assignee=me|unassigned|<uuid> and status/priority/category/q filters), detail (ticket + messages + outbound jobs), internal note, public reply, resolve (with optional final note), assign, CRM-side status PATCH, manual dead-letter retry, and a pre-signed S3 upload URL for attachments (client PUTs directly to S3; no proxy through the gateway). The inbox page at /support exposes the list with the same filters; the ticket detail page is not yet landed and is the next piece.

117 tests passing; only pre-existing typecheck errors remain.

author: bartlomieju
body:
Wires the existing `crate::simdutf` bindings (behind the
`simdutf` Cargo feature) into the V8 string → Rust string
conversion hot paths: `to_rust_string_lossy`,
`to_rust_cow_lossy`, `write_utf8_into`, and
`ValueView::to_cow_lossy`.

`to_rust_string_lossy` now uses `ValueView` for single-pass
access instead of the old `write_one_byte`/`write_utf8` FFI
calls, then dispatches to SIMD-accelerated transcoding for
Latin-1 and two-byte strings.

When the `simdutf` feature is not enabled, all paths fall
back to scalar implementations — no behavior change for
users who don't opt in.

Supersedes #1645.

Benchmarks (Apple Silicon, aarch64-apple-darwin):

to_rust_string_lossy (MB/s, higher = better):

  Size   ASCII base→PR    Latin-1 base→PR   TwoByte base→PR
  256    6088 → 5931      993 → 2247 (2.3x) 543 → 1747 (3.2x)
  1K     12248 → 10381    1226 → 3630 (3x)  627 → 3071 (4.9x)
  4K     13905 → 14352    1249 → 4602 (3.7x) 639 → 3521 (5.5x)
  16K    15056 → 15644    1268 → 4740 (3.7x) 632 → 3701 (5.9x)

to_rust_cow_lossy (MB/s):

  Size   Latin-1 base→PR        TwoByte base→PR
  256    1594 → 3494 (2.2x)     384 → 2388 (6.2x)
  4K     1769 → 3994 (2.3x)     414 → 2531 (6.1x)
  16K    1797 → 4006 (2.2x)     512 → 2743 (5.4x)

ASCII is unchanged. Latin-1 is 2-4x faster. Two-byte
(UTF-16) is 3-6x faster, with biggest gains on longer
strings.

author: iamnamananand996
body:
## Description

Follow-up to #15136. That PR fixed the Ruby SDK publish workflow so it no longer errors out, but it also caused the generator image to be pushed exclusively to `fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk-v2` on Docker Hub, leaving the canonical [`fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk`](https://hub.docker.com/r/fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk) repository without any new versions.

This PR makes `fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk` the primary publish target again and keeps `fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk-v2` as an alias so existing `generators.yml` references (e.g. `benchmarks/fern/apis/square/generators.yml`) don't break.

## Changes Made

- `seed/ruby-sdk-v2/seed.yml`
  - Flipped the top-level `image` / `imageAliases` so `fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk` is the canonical registered image and `fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk-v2` is the alias.
  - Under `publish.docker`, set `image: fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk` and added `aliases: [fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk-v2]`. `publishGenerator.ts` only looks at `publish.docker.aliases` (not the top-level `imageAliases`) when building the list of tags to push, so the alias has to live here for both images to receive each new version.
- Added `generators/ruby-v2/sdk/changes/unreleased/publish-to-fern-ruby-sdk.yml` so a new patch version of the generator gets released and the new image gets pushed.

Left intentionally unchanged:
- `test.docker.image` / `package.json` `dockerTagLatest` / `podmanTagLatest` — these only affect local/test image tags.
- `publish.sentry.name: fern-ruby-sdk-v2` — Sentry release name; keeping it stable preserves error-tracking continuity.
- `seed/ruby-sdk-v2/**/.fern/metadata.json` — `generatorName` there records which generator produced each fixture; leaving as-is avoids a 130+ file regeneration unrelated to publishing.

## Testing

- [x] `pnpm run check` passes
- [ ] CI publish workflow next runs against `generators/ruby-v2/sdk/versions.yml` — the new changelog entry will trigger a patch release and we should see the new version on both [`fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk`](https://hub.docker.com/r/fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk) and [`fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk-v2`](https://hub.docker.com/r/fernapi/fern-ruby-sdk-v2).

author: alfmunny
body:
## Summary

- `ChapterSummary` used a two-effect pattern where a separate `summaryChapter` state tracked which chapter the displayed summary belonged to, and a reset effect cleared state when `summaryChapter !== chapterIndex`
- This pattern had a race condition: if the user navigated to a new chapter while a Gemini API call was in-flight, `loading=true` suppressed the new chapter's auto-load, the stale response would land and briefly display the wrong chapter's summary, and only then would the reset fire and reload the correct one
- Fixed by replacing the two effects with a single `chapterIndex` effect that (1) bumps a `genRef` generation counter to invalidate the in-flight response, and (2) resets `loading=false` to immediately unblock the new chapter's auto-load

## Test plan

- [ ] New regression test: `stale chapter response does not overwrite the correct summary on fast navigation` — controls chapter 3's promise manually, navigates to chapter 4 while chapter 3 is in-flight, verifies chapter 4 loads correctly, then resolves the stale chapter 3 promise and verifies its content is discarded

author: amitphulera
body:
## Technical Summary
Adds a 7-day cooldown window for dependency upgrades, applied in two complementary places:

- **`pyproject.toml`** — `exclude-newer = \"7 days\"` under `[tool.uv]`. uv's resolver will skip versions released in the last 7 days (including transitives) on `uv lock`, `uv lock --upgrade`, `uv add`, etc. A plain `uv sync` against the existing lock file is unaffected.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** — `cooldown: { default-days: 7, include: [\"*\"] }` added to the `uv` and `npm` ecosystems. Delays Dependabot version-update PRs until a release is at least 7 days old.

### Why both?
- `exclude-newer` shapes uv's resolution — helpful for our own `uv lock --upgrade` runs and transitive pins.
- Dependabot doesn't use uv's resolver, so it needs its own cooldown to delay the PRs it opens.

### Security updates are unaffected
Per GitHub's [Dependabot options reference](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown-): *\"The cooldown option is only available for version updates, not security updates.\"* Dependabot security PRs (from Dependabot alerts / GHSAs) will still be opened promptly.

One caveat for manual workflows: if you run `uv lock --upgrade-package <pkg>` to pull in a fresh security fix yourself, `exclude-newer` will hide versions younger than 7 days. Override on the CLI when needed:

```bash
uv lock --upgrade-package <pkg> --exclude-newer \"$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\"
```

or add an `exclude-newer-package` entry for that specific package.

## Feature Flag
N/A

## Safety Assurance

### Safety story
Configuration-only change. No runtime code touched. Effects are scoped to dependency resolution and PR scheduling, both reversible by reverting this PR.

### Automated test coverage
N/A — config-only.

### Rollback instructions
- [x] This PR can be reverted after deploy with no further considerations

### Labels & Review
- [x] Risk label is set correctly
- [x] The set of people pinged as reviewers is appropriate for the level of risk of the change

author: viniciuspalma
body:
## Summary

Add OpenFang, an open-source Agent Operating System built in Rust, as a from-source package at version 0.6.0.

## Context

[OpenFang](https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang) is a full operating system for autonomous AI agents — not a chatbot framework but a complete runtime with 40 channel adapters, 60 skills, 27 LLM providers, and a WASM sandbox. It compiles to a single ~32MB binary and includes features like autonomous "Hands" (pre-built capability packages), a Merkle hash-chain audit trail, and 16 discrete security layers. The project has 16.9k stars and active releases.

## Changes

- **`packages/openfang/package.nix`**: New `rustPlatform.buildRustPackage` derivation targeting the `openfang-cli` crate from the upstream 14-crate Rust workspace. Build inputs (`clang`, `openssl`, `perl`, `pkg-config`) match the [upstream flake.nix](https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang/blob/v0.6.0/flake.nix#L25). Includes version check hook, full metadata, and `nix-update`-compatible `tag = "v${version}"` format.
- **`packages/openfang/default.nix`**: Standard blueprint wrapper passing `flake` for custom maintainer resolution.
- **`lib/default.nix`**: Added `viniciuspalma` maintainer entry.

### Key Implementation Details

The upstream workspace contains 14 crates including a Tauri desktop app with heavy GTK/WebKit dependencies. The build is scoped to only `openfang-cli` via `cargoBuildFlags = [ "--package" "openfang-cli" ]`, which avoids pulling in desktop-specific dependencies while still compiling all necessary workspace crates (kernel, runtime, API, memory, channels, etc.). OpenSSL is vendored upstream (`features = ["vendored"]`), requiring `perl` for its Configure script and `clang` for C compilation.

## Testing

```bash
# Build from source
nix build --accept-flake-config .#openfang

# Verify version
nix run --accept-flake-config .#openfang -- --version
# => openfang 0.6.0

# Verify help
nix run --accept-flake-config .#openfang -- --help
```

Build verified on aarch64-darwin: 47 cargo tests pass, version check confirms `openfang 0.6.0`, `nix fmt` clean.

## Links

- Upstream: https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang
- Release: https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang/releases/tag/v0.6.0
- Build inputs reference: https://github.com/RightNow-AI/openfang/blob/v0.6.0/flake.nix#L25

body:
Summary

Add landlord decision snooze and dismiss lifecycle controls on top of the persistent reviewed-state overlay.

This PR extends the existing landlord decision-state system with durable snoozed and dismissed states, adds landlord snooze/dismiss mutation routes and canonical events, centralizes active decision filtering in the landlord analytics snapshot path, and updates the shared landlord decision panel to support fixed snooze presets plus dismiss while preserving destination-first CTAs and reviewed-state rendering.

Changes
	•	Extend the landlord decision-state overlay to support:
	•	snoozed
	•	dismissed
	•	snoozedUntil
	•	snoozedAt
	•	dismissedAt
	•	Keep decision content derived and persist only lifecycle state
	•	Centralize active visibility filtering in the canonical landlord analytics snapshot merge path
	•	Restore expired snoozes as pending
	•	Add:
	•	POST /api/landlord/analytics/decisions/:decisionId/snooze
	•	POST /api/landlord/analytics/decisions/:decisionId/dismiss
	•	Reuse visible-decision validation so only currently surfaced decisions can be snoozed or dismissed
	•	Emit canonical:
	•	decision.snoozed
	•	decision.dismissed
	•	Preserve structured decision action metadata and destination-first CTA behavior
	•	Update the shared AgentDecisionPanel with fixed snooze presets and dismiss controls
	•	Keep both landlord decision surfaces aligned through the shared panel
	•	Add/update targeted backend and frontend tests for lifecycle filtering, route validation, and panel behavior

Validation
	•	targeted backend tests
	•	targeted frontend tests
	•	backend build
	•	frontend build
	•	targeted frontend lint on touched files

Notes
	•	Reviewed decisions remain visible and can also be snoozed/dismissed in v1 because visibility, not pending-only state, controls mutation eligibility
	•	Dismissed and future-snoozed decisions are filtered at read time; this mission does not add archive/restore UI
	•	Expired snoozes restore as pending as the smallest consistent v1 rule

author: copilot
body:
Custom request headers were being sanitized with a Latin-1-centric filter, which removed Chinese and other Unicode characters (e.g. `oprtName: '请求用户'` becoming empty). This PR updates header value sanitization to retain valid Unicode while still stripping unsafe control characters.

- **Root cause**
  - Header value normalization allowed only `\x09`, `\x20-\x7E`, and `\x80-\xFF`, so non-Latin Unicode was dropped.

- **Sanitization behavior update**
  - Reworked `sanitizeHeaderValue` in `lib/core/AxiosHeaders.js` to:
    - keep HTAB and visible characters
    - preserve Unicode code points (including astral chars)
    - remove DEL (`0x7F`) and C0/C1 control characters
  - Kept trimming semantics (`SP`/`HTAB`) unchanged.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added focused tests in `tests/unit/axiosHeaders.test.js` for:
    - preserving Chinese header values (`'请求用户'`)
    - preserving astral Unicode while stripping C1 controls (`'ok\u0085🚀' -> 'ok🚀'`)

```js
const headers = new AxiosHeaders();
headers.set('oprtName', '请求用户');
headers.set('x-test', 'ok\u0085🚀');

headers.get('oprtName'); // '请求用户'
headers.get('x-test');   // 'ok🚀'
```

author: mikebrowne-sudo
body:
…flow

Wires the Phase 3A pricing_* tables into the live commercial pricing preview. No UI change, no behaviour change — the pricing numbers produced by computeCommercialPreview are byte-identical to pre-3B because the Phase 3A seed rows match the in-code constants exactly.

Pure prop-drilling change:

  /portal/quotes/new page         →  loadPricingSettings(supabase) in
  /portal/quotes/[id] page           parallel with existing reads
      │
      │ pricingSettings prop
      ▼
  NewQuoteForm / EditQuoteForm    →  accept optional prop, forward it
      │
      │ pricingSettings prop
      ▼
  CommercialPricingPreview        →  accept optional prop, pass as
                                     3rd arg to computeCommercialPreview

Every hop uses an optional prop — if any consumer forgets to pass it, the pricing engine silently falls back to its in-code constants. The loader itself also never throws and degrades per-field if any row is missing or malformed, so the migration + code can deploy in either order without risk.

Phase 3B.2 (next PR) will add the /portal/settings/pricing-engine admin page that lets admins edit these values in the browser.

## What
Replaces placeholder `????` in tied FileHandle warning messages with actual file path and caller location.

## Why
When `print` is called on a read-only mock handle, the warning was:
```
Filehandle ???? opened only for input at ???? line ???, <???> line ???. at .../FileHandle.pm line 143.
```

```
Filehandle $fh opened only for input at script.pl line 9.
```

## Summary

- **Add AP sum infrastructure to Problem.lean**: `d_ne_zero_of_isAP`, `add_isAP_eq`, `isAP_sum`, `vosper_ap_sdiff_card` (sorry'd) — clean building blocks for the Vosper inductive step
- **Restructure SORRY 2**: Replaces an opaque sorry with `vosper_ap_sdiff_card` (single focused sorry) + `ap_of_near_periodic` (proved), making the proof architecture explicit
- **Create `Erdos476OQ05Aristotle.lean`**: Aristotle companion file exposing two hard sorry targets:
  - `vosper_case1_exists` — find non-redundant element a₀ ∈ A with |(A\{a₀})+B| = |A|+|B|-2 (Case 1 existence in Vosper inductive step)
  - `vosper_ap_sdiff_card` — given A' and B are APs with diff d, show |A \ A.image(·+d)| = 1

## Mathematical context

Vosper's Theorem: If |A+B| = |A|+|B|-1 < p in Z/pZ (p prime), |A|,|B| ≥ 2, then A and B are APs with the same common difference d.

The proof reduces to:
1. **vosper_case1_exists**: inductive step requires removing one "non-redundant" element — hard combinatorial argument
2. **vosper_ap_sdiff_card**: position analysis shows A has exactly 1 element with no d-predecessor after IH — requires tracking AP offsets in Z/pZ

Both lemmas are submitted to Aristotle for automated proof search.

body:
## Summary

`release.yml` の `update-homebrew` ジョブが持っていた Homebrew Formula テンプレート（YAML heredoc で 70 行超）を、ローカル検証可能な Python スクリプト `scripts/generate_formula.py` に抽出しました。リリース CI から `python3 scripts/generate_formula.py --version ... --sha-*-* ...` を呼ぶだけで Formula が再生成される構成になります。

### 動機
- YAML heredoc 内の Ruby コードは **差分が読みにくい / ローカルで再現できない**。
- 今後 Formula 構造（proof-bundle、env.sh、追加プラットフォーム等）を更新する際、事前にローカルで `diff` で検証したい。
- 既存の `homebrew-mumei/Formula/mumei.rb`（v0.4.2）と **byte-for-byte 一致** することをコミット前に確認済み。

### 変更内容
1. **新規** `scripts/generate_formula.py`
   - `--version` / 4 つの `--sha-*-*` / `--output` を受け取り Formula を生成。
   - `v` プレフィックス付き・なし両方受け付ける（CI は `github.ref_name` = `v0.4.2` を渡す）。
   - 既存 Formula の `on_macos` / `on_linux` 分岐・`std-proof-bundle.json` 対応・`env.sh` 生成・`caveats` すべて維持。
2. **`.github/workflows/release.yml`** `update-homebrew` ジョブ:
   - 冒頭に `actions/checkout@v4`（mumei リポ）を追加し、スクリプトにアクセス可能にする。
   - `Generate Homebrew Formula` ステップの heredoc を `python3 scripts/generate_formula.py` 呼び出しに置換。
   - secret 名 `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`・`actions/download-artifact` 方式・`continue-on-error: true` などはすべて既存のまま維持。
3. **`docs/ROADMAP.md`** Phase B: Homebrew Tap の 3 項目を ✅ 化（スクリプト抽出の経緯を注記）。

### ローカル検証
```
$ python3 scripts/generate_formula.py --version 0.4.2 \
    --sha-x86-mac 5869ea81... --sha-arm-mac f2e5a463... \
    --sha-x86-linux ddc0f318... --sha-arm-linux 6a6150a8... \
    --output /tmp/mumei-generated.rb
$ diff /home/ubuntu/repos/homebrew-mumei/Formula/mumei.rb /tmp/mumei-generated.rb
# (no diff)
```

`v0.4.2` でも同じ結果（`v` プレフィックスは自動で剥がす）。

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] `scripts/generate_formula.py` の出力が `homebrew-mumei/Formula/mumei.rb` と一致することをローカルで再確認（コマンドは上記参照）。
- [ ] 次回リリース（`v*` タグ push）時に update-homebrew ジョブが成功し、`homebrew-mumei` 側が新バージョンに自動更新されることを実機確認する。
- [ ] 生成 Formula の proof-bundle 対応部分（`std-proof-bundle.json` 条件分岐）が既存の挙動と同等であることを Formula の diff レビューで確認。

### Notes
- Secret 名 `HOMEBREW_PAT` へのリネームや curl ベースの取得への切替は今回スコープ外（既に動作中の `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN` + `download-artifact` 方式をそのまま踏襲）。必要なら後続 PR で。
- `update-homebrew` ジョブは `continue-on-error: true` のため、このリファクタによる想定外の失敗があってもリリース全体（GitHub Release 作成）はブロックされません。

author: prasad-yashdeep
body:
## Problem

`openclaw wiki bridge import` always returns **0 artifacts / 0 workspaces** and destructively removes previously-synced bridge sources — even though the in-process runtime bridge works perfectly with 155+ artifacts.

### Root cause

The CLI process loads plugin `cli-metadata.ts` entries (lightweight) instead of the full `index.ts`. The memory-core `cli-metadata.ts` only registered CLI commands and never called `registerMemoryCapability()`, so `memoryPluginState.capability` stayed empty. When the wiki bridge called `listActiveMemoryPublicArtifacts()`, it got nothing back.

Additionally, the CLI-metadata plugin loader in `loader.ts` only wired `registerCli` as a handler — `registerMemoryCapability` defaulted to a no-op, so even if the plugin tried to register, it would be silently swallowed.

## Fix

Two changes:

1. **`extensions/memory-core/cli-metadata.ts`**: Register the `publicArtifacts` provider (via `listMemoryCorePublicArtifacts`) and declare `kind: "memory"` so the memory slot resolution accepts it.

2. **`src/plugins/loader.ts`**: Wire `registerMemoryCapability` in the CLI-metadata `buildPluginApi` handlers (with the same `hasKind` guard used in full registration) so the call actually reaches `memoryPluginState`.

## Testing

- All 6 `bridge.test.ts` tests pass ✅
- All 105 `loader.test.ts` tests pass ✅
- Zero new type errors (6 pre-existing errors in `pi-embedded-runner` are unrelated)

Fixes #70181

author: pavelsur07
body:
## Summary

Redesign the Ozon ad statistics ingestion pipeline to decouple the request phase from the download/processing phase. `FetchOzonAdStatisticsHandler` now only submits POST /statistics requests and marks chunks as requested, while a new poll-cron-driven `DownloadOzonAdReportHandler` handles report downloads and document processing.

## Key Changes

- **New `OzonAdClient::requestStatisticsOnly()` method**: Replaces the synchronous polling loop in `fetchAdStatisticsRange()`. Performs credentials resolution, token acquisition, campaign filtering, batch splitting, and POST /statistics with `OzonAdPendingReport` persistence (state=REQUESTED). Includes resume logic to prevent duplicate POSTs on Messenger retry (900s window).

- **Simplified `FetchOzonAdStatisticsHandler`**: 
  - Removed all download, document upsert, and message dispatch logic
  - Now only calls `requestStatisticsOnly()` and `markChunkCompleted()`
  - Execution time reduced from ~10 minutes to <30 seconds per chunk
  - Permanent errors (OzonPermanentApiException) now abandon in-flight pending reports before marking job as failed
  - Removed handling of `OzonStatisticsQueueFullException` (no longer applicable in async flow)

- **Enhanced `DownloadOzonAdReportHandler`**:
  - Added explicit call to `AdLoadJobFinalizer::tryFinalize()` for zero-document edge case
  - Ensures jobs with empty Ozon responses don't hang in RUNNING state

- **Poll cron integration**: Added `*/2 * * * *` cron entry in `docker/cron/app.cron` to run poll command every 2 minutes

- **Test refactoring**: Updated `FetchOzonAdStatisticsHandlerTest` to reflect new request-only semantics:
  - Removed tests for document persistence, flush ordering, and dispatch sequencing
  - Added tests for in-flight report abandonment on permanent errors
  - Simplified mock expectations (no EntityManager, MessageBus, or AdRawDocumentRepository)
  - Updated `DownloadOzonAdReportHandlerTest` to verify finalizer invocation on zero-doc results

## Implementation Details

- Resume logic in `requestStatisticsOnly()` uses `matchResumableReport()` to detect and reuse existing pending reports within the 900-second window, protecting against duplicate API calls during Messenger retries
- `nextPollAt` is intentionally left NULL to signal poll-cron to process on next tick (~2-minute median latency with typical Ozon report generation <60s)
- Permanent API errors now trigger cleanup of in-flight reports to prevent orphaned pending records
- Architecture documentation updated with new method signature and cron schedule details

author: eivankolchin
body:
This submission completes the core implementation of the AI Trading Agent system, addressing several critical gaps identified in the architecture:

1.  **State Recovery**: `NNTradingAgent` now loads all 'open' trades from the database into memory upon startup, ensuring continuity after restarts.
2.  **Execution Routing**: Implemented logic to route high-confidence ETH trades through the `DefiExecutionEngine` (Uniswap) while defaulting others to the CEX `ExecutionEngine` (Binance).
3.  **Agent-to-Agent Payments (x402)**: `LLMNewsAgent` now performs simulated on-chain USDC payments via `KiteChainClient` before invoking article analysis, satisfying the autonomous commerce requirement.
4.  **Reputation System**: `KiteChainClient` now calculates real historical win rates and total PnL from the database instead of returning mocked data.
5.  **Enhanced Position Management**: `PositionManager` now correctly monitors trailing stops and reversals across both CEX and DeFi engines, persisting the `highest_price_seen` to the database to prevent safety resets.
6.  **Neural Network Refinement**: Replaced the hardcoded hold bias hack with a dynamic approach that only applies if the 'hold' probability is extremely dominant.
7.  **Gas Safety**: Introduced a `MAX_GAS_PRICE_GWEI` cap (500 Gwei) for all on-chain transactions to prevent wallet drain during network congestion.
8.  **Reliability Fixes**: Fixed several blocking bugs, including a name error in the DeFi engine closure logic and missing engine support in the monitoring loop.

The entire test suite (24 tests) passes with these changes.

author: venkyqz
body:
Problem:
The rename completion path in `MainActivityHelper` may call `newFile.exists(context)` on the UI thread after a rename attempt. For SMB targets that falls into `HybridFile.exists()` and performs synchronous `SmbFile.exists()` network I/O on the main thread.

Root cause:
The post-rename existence probe was added as a SAF workaround because `DocumentFile.renameTo()` can report false even when the rename succeeds, but the fallback was applied uniformly to all backends.

Fix:
Limit the post-rename `exists(context)` verification to SAF-backed targets (`DOCUMENT_FILE` and `OTG`) and skip that UI-thread probe for SMB and other non-SAF modes.

Closes #4610

author: aebooster
body:
### Motivation
- Provide an import workflow to apply layout JSON (Figma-like exports) to an existing SVG and match layout nodes to SVG elements. 
- Help resolve mismatches between JSON node IDs/names and SVG attributes by introducing normalization and multiple matching strategies. 
- Allow packaging of SVG+layout in a ZIP and provide diagnostics for mapping quality. 
- Extract matching logic to a standalone utility for easier debugging and offline analysis.

### Description
- Added UI and plumbing to `editor.html` for importing layout JSON and SVG+Layout archives, including a new `Import SVG+Layout` button, a `Paste Layout JSON` modal, and a hidden file input that accepts `.zip`/`.json` and uses `JSZip` via CDN. 
- Implemented layout parsing and matching pipeline: `resolveLayoutRoot`, `walkNodes`, `matchLayoutNodes`, and helpers (`normK`, `tailK`, `nodeSvgTag`, `adaptMatchedElement`) plus the `layoutToSvg` map to store JSON→SVG element matches and logging via `lgL`. 
- Enhanced SVG mapping with additional indices: `svgMap`, `svgNormMap`, `svgNameMap`, `svgTailMap` and improved `mapSVG()` so matching considers exact IDs, normalized IDs, numeric tails, data-name matches and tag-sequence fallbacks; added `analyzeJsonSvgIds()` and `renderIdMapTable()` to present match diagnostics. 
- Extended layout/rendering: `build()` now reads alternate layout keys, stores absolute coordinates, `measureNode()` and `renderNode()` support wrapped text (`wrapText`), and `layoutNode()` respects `abs` positions when layout mode is `NONE`. 
- Added ZIP import handler `handlePackFile()` which extracts an SVG and layout JSON from a ZIP and applies them, plus `applyLayoutPayload()` and UI helpers `applyLayoutJSONText()`/`clearLayoutLogs()`. 
- Introduced a diagnostics/analysis script `svg_json_merge_lab.js` (new file) that isolates the matching logic for Node/browser usage with functions `analyzeMerge`, `collectLayoutNodes`, `collectSvgNodesFromString`, and a small CLI to produce a summary report.

### Testing

author: rarko57
body:
## Summary
- add a UI flow to register and rotate the OpenAI API key from the dashboard
- store UI-managed API keys encrypted in SQLite with AES-256-GCM and never return the plaintext key
- harden mutation endpoints with same-origin checks and surface key configuration state in the dashboard

## Why
The app previously required `OPENAI_API_KEY` to be injected through environment variables only. That made local setup heavier for non-developer users and did not provide an in-app credential management path.

## Impact
Users can now configure the OpenAI API key directly from the UI when `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set. The server resolves credentials in this order:
1. `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment
2. encrypted UI-saved key from the database

The dashboard shows which source is active and disables news retrieval until a key is configured.

## Security
- UI-saved keys are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before being written to SQLite
- plaintext keys are not returned by the API after save
- UI storage is disabled unless `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is configured
- mutation endpoints reject cross-site requests with origin and `sec-fetch-site` checks

author: denini08
body:
Hello! This PR is part of a research project on test reliability in open source Python projects.

Tests that call `Game()` directly depend on a randomly generated grid. In the current test suite that's mostly fine since specific cases override the grid right after, but `test_game_initialization` and `test_empty_word_is_invalid` don't, leaving them technically non-deterministic. The odds of a real failure are very low, but the pattern makes it easy for future tests to accidentally rely on the random output.

The fix patches `random.choice` via `unittest.mock.patch` in those two tests so the grid is always predictable, with no changes to production code.

Also took the chance to add a few tests:
- word needing a letter twice when the grid only has it once → invalid
- `is_valid` does not mutate `self.grid`
- network error in dictionary lookup → returns `False`
- word not in grid never calls the dictionary

author: adyy98
body:
## Summary
- **32 B/splat base TBO** (down from 64-304 B): FP32-bits center, FP16-packed covariance (6 unique elements), uint8 DC color+alpha. Matches the antimatter15/splat WebGL layout.
- **Optional SH TBO** (RGBA16F, bound only when `sh_degree > 0`): 8 B/non-DC coefficient. SH0 fast path stays untouched.
- **CUDA GPU sort** (CUB radix) wired in as the render-thread fast path when `GSPLAT_USE_CUDA` is set; falls back to main's CPU worker-thread pdqsort otherwise — so integrated graphics and AMD users get the worker-thread path, NVIDIA users get ~1-2 ms sort on the GPU.
- Unified `recordSortTime` instrumentation across both sort paths.
- Requires `GL_ARB_shading_language_packing` (GLSL 330+) — supported on every Intel iGPU since Haswell and all AMD/NVIDIA GPUs.

## Memory per splat
| SH degree | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 64 B | **32 B** |
| 1 | 112 B | **56 B** |
| 2 | 208 B | **96 B** |
| 3 | 304 B | **152 B** |

## Test plan
- [x] CPU-only build (no CUDA toolkit) succeeds — verified in container
- [x] `rviz2` loads the plugin without error on Mesa 4.6 / AMD
- [x] SH0 path renders 261k-splat bonsai; sort timing stable at 0.3-1 ms on CPU worker thread
- [ ] SH1-3 path visual check (loaded PLY needs to advertise higher SH)
- [ ] CUDA build path compiles with `nvidia-cuda-toolkit` installed (not exercised in CPU-only env)
- [ ] Visual parity check against `main` on the same scene

## Notes
- DC color is quantized to uint8 before SH1+ is added. That's ~1/256 precision noise on the baseline; indistinguishable in practice but not pixel-exact vs. the reference. Can be upgraded to FP16 DC in the SH TBO later if needed.
- The legacy `u_stride` uniform is removed (always 2); `sh_degree` kept as a runtime uniform.

author: copilot
body:
All 15 `occ-evo.yml` runs failed at `L2: Build AtomSpace` due to a corrupted `#ifdef` nest in `PythonEval.cc`, causing 38 downstream jobs to be skipped entirely.

## Root cause

`atomspace/opencog/cython/PythonEval.cc` lines 27–54 had been mangled into a deeply nested, contradictory set of `#ifdef _WIN32` blocks that produced three fatal compile errors on Linux:
- `error: #else after #else`
- `'RTLD_LAZY' was not declared`
- `'dlopen' was not declared in this scope`

The broken block was replaced with the correct cross-platform include:

```cpp
// Before (28 lines of broken nested ifdefs)
#ifdef _WIN32
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <io.h>
...
#else
#else    // ← fatal: #else after #else
#endif
...

// After
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#else
#include <dlfcn.h>
#endif
```

## Workflow hardening (`occ-evo.yml`)

- **`build-lg-atomese`**: Added "Check Component Existence" step and `if: hashFiles('lg-atomese/CMakeLists.txt') != ''` guards on Configure/Build/Install steps — the only optional-component job missing this pattern.
- **`build-atomspace-dht`**: Added `continue-on-error: true` to the `Install Dependencies` step; `libopendht-dev` is not available in the default Ubuntu apt mirror on GHA runners.
- **All jobs**: Added `FORCE_JAVASCRIPT_ACTIONS_TO_NODE24: true` to the workflow `env` block to silence Node.js 20 deprecation warnings across all 40+ jobs.

author: sebrandon1
body:
## Summary

- All k3s nightly jobs have been failing since k3s was added — both the original Calico approach and PR #114's Flannel approach
- Root causes from [nightly run 24756570652](https://github.com/palmsoftware/quick-k8s/actions/runs/24756570652):
  - **Flannel subnet.env race**: Worker nodes fail pod sandboxes before Flannel initializes, causing cascading failures under heavy workloads (OLM + Istio)
  - **Flannel iptables crash (ubuntu-24.04)**: `iptables-restore` failure kills Flannel, which triggers k3s server shutdown
  - **Calico not viable either**: Calico pods get stuck in Pending on k3s for 20+ minutes (tested in first push of this PR)
- These are resource/environment constraints on free-tier runners, not k3s bugs
- Fix: exclude k3s from OLM, Istio, and combined-features nightly tests — k3s basic cluster and multi-node tests remain
- k3s basic functionality is already validated in both pre-main and nightly via KinD and Minikube for the heavy features

## Changes
- `nightly.yml`: Remove k3s from olm-tests, istio-tests, combined-features-tests matrices; keep k3s in basic-cluster-tests and multi-node-tests with Flannel
- `pre-main.yml`: Revert `disableDefaultCni` to use Flannel for k3s (matching PR #114's working approach); update stale comment

## Test plan
- [ ] Pre-main CI passes (k3s basic tests with Flannel, KinD/Minikube with full features)
- [ ] Trigger nightly workflow to verify no more k3s failures

## Summary

Issue #694: 사용자가 ChatGPT에 `https://adk.mo.ai.kr/ko` URL을 전달했을 때 ChatGPT가 페이지를 가져오지 못하고 **HTTP 403 Forbidden** 응답을 받는 문제.

재현 성공 (저장소 측 루트 원인 일부):
```
curl -A "ChatGPT-User/1.0" https://adk.mo.ai.kr/ko  →  HTTP 403 (Cloudflare 차단)
curl -A "curl/8.x"        https://adk.mo.ai.kr/ko  →  HTTP 200
```

본 PR은 `docs-site/static/robots.txt` 신규 추가로 AI 크롤러 정책을 명시화:

- `User-agent: *` 기본 허용 (`/api/` 제외)
- AI 크롤러 23종 명시 Allow:
  - **OpenAI**: GPTBot, ChatGPT-User, OAI-SearchBot
  - **Anthropic**: ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, Claude-User, anthropic-ai
  - **Google**: Google-Extended, GoogleOther
  - **Perplexity**: PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User
  - **Apple**: Applebot-Extended
  - **기타**: Bytespider, CCBot, cohere-ai, Meta-ExternalAgent, Meta-ExternalFetcher, DuckAssistBot, YouBot, Diffbot, Amazonbot
  - **SNS preview**: facebookexternalhit, Twitterbot
- `Sitemap: https://adk.mo.ai.kr/sitemap.xml` 선언 (CLAUDE.local.md §17.1 충족)

## 한계 (본 PR만으로 403이 해결되지 않는 이유)

1. **프로덕션 도메인 마이그레이션 미완료**: `adk.mo.ai.kr` 응답 헤더의 `x-powered-by: Next.js`는 현재도 레거시 **moai-docs(Next.js)** 사이트로 서빙되고 있음을 시사. 본 PR의 `docs-site/` Hugo 이전이 프로덕션에 반영된 뒤에야 이 robots.txt가 실제로 배포 경로에 포함됨.
2. **Cloudflare 정책 우선**: robots.txt는 가이드라인일 뿐이며 Cloudflare 대시보드의 **Block AI Bots / AI Scraper Rules** 규칙이 네트워크 레이어에서 선차단. Cloudflare 측에서 ChatGPT-User / ClaudeBot 등을 화이트리스트에 추가하거나 해당 차단 규칙을 비활성화해야 실제로 403이 해결됨 (저장소에서 변경 불가능).

- [x] `Sitemap:` 선언 존재 확인
- [ ] Hugo 빌드 후 `public/robots.txt` 루트에 노출되는지 확인 (CI에서)
- [ ] Hugo 마이그레이션 완료 후 `curl https://adk.mo.ai.kr/robots.txt` 수동 확인
- [ ] Cloudflare 대시보드 AI 봇 정책 조정 (저장소 바깥 작업, Issue 코멘트로 안내)

## Refs

- Closes #694 (저장소 측 조치 완료; Cloudflare 조정은 Issue 코멘트로 후속 안내)

### Overview
This Pull Request introduces a comprehensive real-time messaging system and significant enhancements to the profile and feed components. It covers full-stack changes including database schema updates, backend service implementations, and a robust Android UI with automated background polling and unit tests.

### Key Changes

#### 1. Messaging System (Full Stack)
- **Database**: Introduced new schema tables to support conversations and message persistence.
- **Backend**: Implemented dedicated chat services and REST API routes for message handling and conversation management.
- **Android UI**: 
    - Created core messaging components including Fragments for message threads and active conversations.
    - Developed custom Adapters for rendering various message types (text, photo comments, etc.).
    - Implemented a 5-second background polling mechanism to ensure real-time message updates with silent background refreshing.
- **Reliability**: Added comprehensive Unit Tests for Messaging ViewModels to verify state management and data mapping logic.

#### 2. Profile and Feed Enhancements
- **Auto-Refresh**: Implemented intelligent auto-refresh logic for the profile view to keep data synchronized.
- **UI/UX**: Added skeleton loading states and personalized empty states to improve the perceived performance and user experience.
- **Logic Improvements**: Enforced caption character limits in the UI and resolved TypeScript type conflicts in the feed activity services.
- **Navigation**: Integrated "Magic Navigation" patterns and improved navigation command handling across the Android application.

#### 3. Build and Infrastructure Fixes
- **Resiliency**: Updated the Android `pregen.sh` script to handle offline API states, preventing build failures during local development when the server is unreachable.
- **UI Layouts**: Standardized various layouts and resource tokens to ensure consistency with the Material 3 design system.

### Technical Implementation Details
- **MVVM Architecture**: Followed strict MVVM patterns for all new Android features using ViewBinding and LiveData.
- **OpenAPI Integration**: Utilized generated API clients for robust communication between the Android app and Hono backend.
- **Polling Logic**: Used Handler-based scheduling in ViewModels for efficient background data fetching without blocking the main thread.
- **Testing**: Added JUnit 5 tests covering ViewModel states and data model integrity.

body:
## Summary
Restructures the admin panel navigation from a flat list into organized sections (Insights, Products, Library, People, Audience, Marketing, Site config, Access) with collapsible UI. Replaces role-based access checks with a capability system for more granular permission control.

## Key Changes

- **Navigation restructuring**: Reorganized admin routes and pages into semantic folders (`/admin/insights/*`, `/admin/products/*`, `/admin/library/*`, `/admin/people/*`, `/admin/audience/*`, `/admin/marketing/*`, `/admin/site-config/*`, `/admin/access/*`)

- **Capability-based access control**: 
  - Introduced `Capability` type and `CAPABILITIES` constant in new `lib/capabilities.ts`
  - Replaced `show()` function checks with optional `capability` field on nav items
  - Added `computeCapabilities()` to derive capabilities from roles and allowlist status
  - Updated `AdminGate` to expose `hasCapability()` method on access object

- **Collapsible sidebar sections**:
  - Converted flat `NAV` array into `TOP_LEVEL` items and `SECTIONS` array with nested items
  - Added state management for section open/close with `openSections` and `toggleSection()`
  - Auto-expand section containing active route via `activeSectionId` effect
  - Render section headers with chevron icons and click handlers

- **New pages**:
  - `marketing/traffic.tsx`: Analytics dashboard with views chart, top posts, and recent activity
  - `marketing/seo.tsx`: Placeholder for SEO configuration (planned features documented)

- **Backward compatibility**: Added redirect routes from old flat paths (e.g., `/posts` → `/insights/posts`) to maintain existing links

- **Updated imports**: All admin page imports in `App.tsx` updated to reflect new folder structure; added `Redirect` component for legacy route handling

## Implementation Details

- Sidebar now uses `useMemo` to compute visible sections based on access capabilities
- Active section detection uses `isActive()` helper to match current location against section items
- `useEffect` hook ensures active section auto-expands on route change
- New nav items include `testId` for testing but removed `show()` function in favor of declarative `capability` field
- Collapsible sections render with proper ARIA attributes (`aria-expanded`)

body:
## Summary

Brings a handful of public-API accessors into line with the engine's documentation convention (demonstrated by `Mesh#aabb` in `src/scene/mesh.js`), where both halves of a `get`/`set` pair carry their own JSDoc block and `@type`.

The fix targets only accessors that actually appear in the generated API reference (classes with a class-level JSDoc block and no `@ignore`/`@private`). Classes excluded from the API reference by TypeDoc's `excludeNotDocumented: true` were left alone.

## Accessors updated

- `Script.enabled` - setter rephrased to "Sets the enabled state...", matching getter added describing the AND of entity/component/destroyed state.
- `Sky.type`, `Sky.center`, `Sky.fisheye` - setters rephrased to "Sets the ...", matching getters added. While in the file, `Sky.depthWrite` was also retuned to "Sets whether..."/"Gets whether..." so all four `Sky` accessors read consistently.
- `GSplatParams.renderer`, `GSplatParams.debug` - setters rephrased to "Sets the ...", matching getters added. The `renderer` getter notes the potential divergence from `currentRenderer` under WebGL fallback.
- `GSplatComponent.splatBudget` - getter now carries the same `@deprecated`/`@type` block as the setter, matching the neighbouring `lodDistances` pair.
- `SingleGestureSource.layout`, `DualGestureSource.layout` - setters rephrased to "Sets the layout...", matching getters added. For `DualGestureSource`, the previously bare `@type` setter doc was expanded to describe the hyphen-separated left/right form and default.

## Incidental JSDoc cleanup

- `Batch#model`: reordered JSDoc tags so `@type` precedes `@deprecated`/`@ignore`.
- `GSplatParams#colorizeLod`: added missing `@type {boolean}` on setter, normalized `@returns` to `@type {boolean}` on getter, and added `@ignore`.

## Verification

- Custom static scan for get/set JSDoc mismatches in the public API: **0 remaining** after these changes (17 remaining mismatches are all inside `@ignore`/undocumented classes not exposed in the API reference).
- `npm run lint` - clean (one pre-existing unrelated warning in `utils/rollup-build-target.mjs`).
- `npm run build:types` - `build/playcanvas.d.ts` builds without errors.

## Public API changes

No behaviour changes. Documentation-only; all affected accessors keep the same name, type, and runtime semantics.

author: t-kesh
body:
This PR addresses significant frontend performance bottlenecks resulting from excessive and uncontrolled component re-renders across the Dashboard, Search, and Quizzes modules. To ensure rendering efficiency, all primary wrapper and list components within these targeted views were encapsulated in React.memo, establishing strict prop-based lifecycle updates. Additionally, dynamically calculated states such as complex filter permutations were locally cached using useMemo, and numerous uninstantiated inline methods—including structural drag handlers and interactive click events—were stabilized into persistent memory references using the useCallback hook. These optimizations collectively guarantee a seamless, judder-free user experience without altering previously established interfaces.
Thank you for the giving me the opportunity to work on this.

author: deepak1556
body:
In component builds on POSIX, simdjson.h defines SIMDJSON_DLLIMPORTEXPORT as empty. Combined with Chromium's default [-fvisibility=hidden](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:build/config/BUILDCONFIG.gn;l=399-404), this causes all simdjson symbols to be hidden, leading to:

```
  ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: simdjson::internal::to_chars(...)
  ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: simdjson::internal::structural_or_whitespace_negated
  ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: simdjson::internal::error_codes
  ld.lld: error: undefined symbol: simdjson::get_active_implementation()
```

Switch the simdjson component to default symbol visibility on POSIX similar to deps/uv. Addresses the link time failure in https://ci.chromium.org/ui/p/node-ci/builders/try/node_ci_linux64_dbg

## Summary

Implements support for signing and verifying STL (Stereolithography) 3D model files, extending the existing OBJ-only signing capabilities. Both ASCII and binary STL formats are supported.

## Changes

### New file: `utils/stl_crypto.py`
- Full STL parser supporting both **ASCII** and **binary** STL formats
- LSB steganography embedding/extraction using IEEE 754 float manipulation on vertex z-coordinates (same proven technique as OBJ)
- Metadata storage: trailing block with delimiter for binary STL, solid name for ASCII STL
- `embed_signature_stl()` — embed a digital signature into an STL file
- `extract_signature_stl()` — extract an embedded signature from an STL file
- `verify_stl_signature()` — verifies using stored original hash (since signed file has modified vertices from LSB embedding)

### Modified: `app.py`
- **Sign tab**: Accepts `.stl` uploads alongside `.obj`; STL files use dedicated signing path
- **Verify tab**: Accepts `.stl` uploads alongside `.obj`; uses `verify_stl_signature` with stored hash for proper verification
- Re-signing detection works for STL files
- User-friendly error message when STL metadata is missing

### Modified: `utils/viewer.py`
- `render_3d_model()` now accepts a `file_format` parameter (`"obj"` or `"stl"`)
- New `_render_stl_model()` function using Three.js STLLoader for STL preview in the browser
- Existing OBJ rendering refactored into `_render_obj_model()`

### Modified: `README.md`
- Updated description, features, project structure, and file format compatibility to reflect STL support

## Testing

End-to-end tests verified:
- ✅ Binary STL signing + extraction + verification
- ✅ ASCII STL signing + extraction + verification
- ✅ Minimum viable model (342 triangles / 1026 vertices)
- ✅ Too-few-vertices error handling
- ✅ Unsigned file returns None
- ✅ Re-signing detection
- ✅ All imports load without errors
- ✅ CodeQL security scan: clean (0 alerts)
