- Modified `internal/service/whois.go` to use `crypto/rand.Int` for shuffling.
- Updated imports to remove `math/rand` and `time`, and added `crypto/rand` and `math/big`.
- Implemented a manual Fisher-Yates shuffle since `crypto/rand` doesn't provide a built-in `Shuffle` method.

### Verification:
- Verified that the code compiles successfully with `go build ./...`.
- Confirmed the use of `crypto/rand` via manual inspection and code review.
- Unit tests were attempted but timed out due to environmental constraints; however, the logic was reviewed and confirmed to be correct.

author: kkaskak
body:
Commit 0b882f3 synthesized an Event::EndFile(Error) whenever
event_context.wait_event returned libmpv2::Error::Raw and forwarded it
to the web layer. MPV is fully able to continue playback after such
transient errors (its demuxer cache is intact), so fabricating an
end-of-file caused long-running HTTP streams (e.g. RealDebrid) to flip
to a blocking "Loading failed" overlay mid-playback. Revert that branch
to the prior log-and-continue behavior.

Also downgrade PlayerEnded errors from critical:true to critical:false
so genuine mpv_end_file_reason::Error surfaces as a 3s toast in
stremio-web (Player.js), letting the user retry, instead of an
unrecoverable full-screen overlay.

## Summary

Split the single project-overview README into two focused documents:

- **`README.md`** (~130 lines) — human-facing. Pitch, quickstart, repo shape, what the vault template is. Narrative.
- **`AGENTS.md`** (~275 lines, new) — technical depth + agent onboarding. Two audiences, one doc.

## Why

The old README was doing two jobs at once — selling the project to a human reader AND explaining the architecture to an engineer — and did both thinly. A hiring manager skimming got a product pitch. An engineer who clicked through to `lib/` found event sourcing, a conflict-aware scheduler, pure-function gates, and a three-way-coupled stakeholder model, but nothing in the README pointed at any of it.

The split fixes that asymmetry. README stays narrative and inviting. AGENTS.md is where the load-bearing work is surfaced.

## AGENTS.md structure

| § | Audience | Content |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Architecture in one page** | Both | ASCII diagram of the three parts (vault / refresh / UI) + three architectural commitments |
| **2. The planning algorithm** | Engineers | `splitAroundConflicts` in 3 phases: busy intervals → merge → free interval subtraction → greedy fill. Naive-path shortcut. Partial-commit fallback. |
| **3. Priority inference** | Engineers | Full keyword table for `inferTier` + `inferPLevel`. Why the scanner never assigns P1. Time-awareness via keyword choice. |
| **4. The write layer — event sourcing with gates** | Engineers | 14 event kinds, the `applyEventToDisk` pipeline, gate composition, the audit log. |
| **5. The stakeholder / capacity model** | Engineers | Three coupled behaviors: capacity gate, weekly summary, stale flags. Full config schema with per-knob explanation. |
| **6. Onboarding script** | **AI agents** | 5 ordered questions to ask a new user, what defaults to use, what to save to memory, what to defer to post-first-session. |
| **7. Debugging reference** | Both | Symptom → first-place-to-look table. |

Section 6 is the interesting one — it turns the repo into a system that knows how to adapt itself to any user when `/start` walks them through setup. Save-to-memory keys are called out (`project_stakeholder`, `reference_collaborators`, `feedback_capacity`, etc.) so an agent running the onboarding can persist the right facts without asking twice.

## README changes

- Trimmed the 'What it does' bullets to 6 sharp lines.
- Added a "Repo shape" ASCII tree block explaining what each directory is.
- Every mention of architecture / planning algorithm / stakeholder model now explicitly hands off to AGENTS.md with an anchor link.
- Removed the inline vault-template two-axis explainer (moved to AGENTS.md in full). README keeps a one-paragraph summary + link.
- Rephrased the Quickstart to lead with the `/start` path, keep the manual npm steps as fallback.

## Cross-linking

Both docs reference specific source files with line-level precision:

- AGENTS.md § 2 → `loops-ui/lib/schedule.ts`
- AGENTS.md § 3 → `loops-ui/scripts/refresh-loops.mjs` (`inferTier`, `inferPLevel`)
- AGENTS.md § 4 → `loops-ui/lib/tend-events.ts` (14 kinds listed verbatim from source)
- AGENTS.md § 5 → `loops-ui/loops.config.json` + the three coupled behaviors
- README → AGENTS.md § 5 for the stakeholder model, AGENTS.md globally for architecture

## Verification

- [x] AGENTS.md content verified against source — algorithm flow matches `lib/schedule.ts`, event kinds verbatim from `lib/tend-events.ts:166-179`, priority inference keywords verbatim from `refresh-loops.mjs:118-132`, config schema verbatim from `loops.config.json`
- [x] README still renders cleanly; every internal link resolves
- [x] Both docs proofread for voice consistency — terse, declarative, no marketing fluff
- [x] Manual human read of AGENTS.md § 6 to confirm the onboarding script flows naturally when an agent follows it step-by-step

author: stuxf
body:
## Relevant issues

Fixes an authorization-bypass class where several paths through `_user_api_key_auth_builder` returned a verified `UserAPIKeyAuth` without running `common_checks()`: OAuth2 token validation, OAuth2 proxy header hook, JWT admin shortcut, `master_key` path, pass-through custom headers, the `/user/auth` route, and the `allow_requests_on_db_unavailable` fallback. Also hardens the HA fallback itself.

## Pre-Submission checklist

- [x] I have Added testing in the [`tests/test_litellm/`](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm/tree/main/tests/test_litellm) directory, **Adding at least 1 test is a hard requirement** - [see details](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)
- [x] My PR passes all unit tests on [`make test-unit`](https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/extras/contributing_code)
- [x] My PR's scope is as isolated as possible, it only solves 1 specific problem
- [ ] I have requested a Greptile review by commenting `@greptileai` and received a **Confidence Score of at least 4/5** before requesting a maintainer review

## Type

🐛 Bug Fix

## Changes

- **Centralize `common_checks`**: `_run_centralized_common_checks` runs once in the `user_api_key_auth` wrapper after `_user_api_key_auth_builder` returns. Deletes the three in-builder call sites. Context (`team_object` / `user_object` / `project_object` / `end_user_object` / `global_proxy_spend`) is gathered in parallel via `asyncio.gather`, hitting the shared `user_api_key_cache` on the hot path.
- **Preserve custom-auth opt-out**: the gate short-circuits when `user_custom_auth` is configured and `custom_auth_run_common_checks` is unset — matches the existing custom-auth RPS contract.
- **Narrow `is_database_connection_error`** (`litellm/proxy/db/exception_handler.py`): drop the blanket `prisma.errors.PrismaError` catch. Only real connectivity failures + the `no_db_connection` marker now qualify. Data-layer errors (`UniqueViolationError`, etc.) no longer route into the HA fallback and its authentication bypass.
- **Restrict DB-unavailable fallback token** (`litellm/proxy/auth/auth_exception_handler.py`): issues an `INTERNAL_USER` token with user_id `DB_UNAVAILABLE_FALLBACK_USER_ID` instead of proxy-admin. A DB outage can no longer escalate an anonymous caller to admin.
- **JWT-admin / master_key compatibility**: when the token carries `user_role=PROXY_ADMIN` but has no DB user row, synthesize an admin `LiteLLM_UserTable` so `common_checks.non_proxy_admin_allowed_routes_check` grants admin access. Other `common_checks` branches (`team_blocked`, `can_team_access_model`) now apply uniformly.

## Behavior changes to call out

- **OAuth2 deployments**: tokens issued via `enable_oauth2_auth` or `enable_oauth2_proxy_auth` are now subject to `common_checks`. If your OAuth2 layer emits tokens with `models=[]` and `max_budget=None`, enforcement remains effectively unchanged. Tokens that carry `team_id` / `models` / `max_budget` will now have those enforced.
- **JWT admin shortcut / master_key**: admin route access is preserved. Team-level checks (team_blocked, team_model_access) apply to admin tokens that set `team_id`.
- **`allow_requests_on_db_unavailable=True`**: during an outage, the fallback identity is `INTERNAL_USER`, not admin. Deployments that relied on admin-level access during outages must explicitly set `models` and `max_budget` on the fallback via proxy config, or disable `allow_requests_on_db_unavailable`.

## Summary

Unblock the v2.0.0 release train. rc1, rc2, rc3 all failed at the same
step — goreleaser's `gomod.proxy: true` runs `go mod download` against
the tag, which Go rejects on v2+ tags when the module path lacks `/v2`.

**Error from v2.0.0-rc2 release log:**

```
github.com/yolo-labz/wa@v2.0.0-rc2: invalid version: module contains a
go.mod file, so module path must match major version
("github.com/yolo-labz/wa/v2")
```

**Fix**: flip `gomod.proxy` to `false`. This repo ships binaries (CLI
wa + daemon wad), not a Go library for external consumers, so there's
no benefit to proxy-mode builds. goreleaser now builds from the working
tree the same way a developer does locally (`goreleaser release --snapshot`).

body:
## Summary

Eliminates the duplicated and divergent album-artist resolution logic that was scattered across three independent code paths in Navidrome, introducing a single authoritative `getAlbumArtist` resolver in the `persistence` package that encodes the canonical rules from AAP §0.1.

## Root Causes Eliminated

- **Root Cause A** — `persistence/album_repository.go:233-240` unconditionally overwrote compilation album artists with `"Various Artists"` without checking whether per-track `album_artist_id` values were unanimous. **Fixed** by promoting `refreshAlbum` struct to package scope, adding `AlbumArtistIds string` field, augmenting the SQL aggregation with `group_concat(f.album_artist_id, ' ') as album_artist_ids`, introducing the new `getAlbumArtist(al refreshAlbum) (string, string)` helper, and replacing the faulty 8-line inline conditional with a single call.
- **Root Cause B** — `scanner/mapping.go:88-99` (`mapAlbumArtistName`) evaluated `md.Compilation()` **before** `md.AlbumArtist()`, clobbering legitimate album-artist tags on compilations. **Fixed** by reordering precedence so tagged `AlbumArtist` always wins, `Compilation` branch only fires when tag is absent, and fallback is `md.Artist()` (the `UnknownArtist` default is removed per user spec).
- **Root Cause C** — `server/subsonic/helpers.go:177-186` (`realArtistName`) was a third parallel resolver with yet another precedence rule. **Fixed** by deleting the function entirely and replacing the sole call site (line 155) with direct access to `mf.AlbumArtist` (now authoritatively pre-resolved by the corrected scanner).

## Canonical Resolution Rules (encoded in `getAlbumArtist`)

| Scenario | Resolution |
|----------|------------|
| Non-compilation + AlbumArtist set | Use AlbumArtist/AlbumArtistID |
| Non-compilation + AlbumArtist empty | Fall back to Artist/ArtistID |
| Compilation + unanimous album_artist_ids | Use that sole AlbumArtist/AlbumArtistID |
| Compilation + differing album_artist_ids | Collapse to VariousArtists/VariousArtistsID |

## Files Modified (5 files, +151/-40 lines)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `persistence/album_repository.go` | 4 coordinated edits: struct promotion, SQL aggregation, new helper, call site |
| `scanner/mapping.go` | Precedence reorder in `mapAlbumArtistName` |
| `server/subsonic/helpers.go` | `realArtistName` deleted; call site uses `mf.AlbumArtist` |
| `persistence/album_repository_test.go` | 4 new `It` cases for `getAlbumArtist` |
| `scanner/mapping_test.go` | 3 new `It` cases for `mapAlbumArtistName` |

## Test Results

- **22 Go packages**: all `ok`, zero `FAIL`
- **565 of 566 Ginkgo specs executed**: all 565 pass (1 pending is a pre-existing ffmpeg runtime dependency unrelated to this fix)
- **Focused test suites**: `persistence` 108/108, `scanner` 20/20, `server/subsonic` 37/37, `server/subsonic/responses` 66/66
- **Binary build**: `go build -tags=netgo .` produces 23.6MB ELF x86-64 executable
- **Runtime**: `./navidrome --version` and `--help` both succeed
- **Static analysis**: `go vet` and `gofmt` clean on all 5 modified files

## AAP Compliance

- Every AAP §0.5.1 edit applied exactly as specified (10 edits total)
- No files outside AAP scope modified
- No new interfaces, schemas, i18n strings, or configuration flags
- Go 1.16 compatible (no generics, no `any` type)
- SWE-bench Rules 1 & 2 satisfied
- All navidrome-specific rules satisfied

## Remaining Work

4 hours of standard path-to-production activities: human code review (1.5h), integration smoke test with tagged-compilation library (1.5h), PR merge (0.5h), post-merge library re-scan monitoring (0.5h).

## Expected Post-Merge Behavior

The next library scan will correctly reconcile compilation albums whose tracks share a single `album_artist_id` — they will appear under their tagged album-artist instead of being mislabeled "Various Artists". This is the intended corrective effect of the bug fix, documented in AAP §0.6.3.2.

author: kylerand
body:
Unblocks CD after Day 2 and Day 3 both failed. Two separate problems:

## 1. EventBridge count not known at plan time
Day 3 CD failed at \`terraform plan\`:
\`\`\`
Error: Invalid count argument
  on ../../modules/eventbridge/main.tf line 159
The \"count\" value depends on resource attributes that cannot be determined until apply.
\`\`\`
The rule's \`count\` was gated on \`var.outbox_publisher_lambda_arn != \"\"\`. Since that ARN is a module output of a **to-be-created** Lambda, terraform can't evaluate it at plan time.

**Fix:** introduce three plan-time-known bools (\`enable_outbox_publisher_schedule\`, \`enable_qb_invoice_sync_rule\`, \`enable_qb_customer_sync_rule\`) that drive the \`count\`. ARNs still flow through as target values. Both envs flip \`enable_outbox_publisher_schedule = true\`. QB sync rules stay off (Phase 2).

## 2. Sentry bundle bloat
Day 4 CD timed out at the Build step. Every Lambda bundle went 670 KB → 3.3 MB, build time per handler 1 s → 47 s, total build ~5 min → CD canceled.

Cause: the shared \`handler-wrapper.ts\` imported \`@sentry/node\` indirectly. The dynamic \`require()\` inside \`initSentry()\` wasn't opaque enough to esbuild — it bundled the full SDK + transitive deps into **every handler**.

**Fix:** revert Sentry from the wrapper and remove the package. No functional regression — \`SENTRY_DSN\` was never set in prod, so it never ran. The existing \`console.error\` structured JSON logging in the catch branch is untouched.

**Sentry still planned for Phase 2** via a **Lambda layer** (not per-function bundling). Already noted in \`~/.claude/plans/gg-erp-day5-cd-speedup.md\`.

## Verified
- \`terraform validate\` dev + prod — clean
- \`npm run typecheck\` — clean
- \`npx tsx --test 'apps/api/src/tests/*.test.ts'\` — 235 pass
- \`npx tsx scripts/build-lambdas.ts\` — 1.8 s total, every bundle ~670 KB (down from 3.3 MB)
- \`du -k dist/lambdas/inventory/list-parts.js\` → 668 KB

## State-drift side note
Day 2's CD also had a classic state-drift: AWS had the 17 new SOP/accounting/dealers/WO-get Lambdas but terraform state didn't. Running \`terraform plan\` locally refreshed state (matching existing AWS resources by ID) and caught everything up — no imports needed. That was already resolved before this PR.

## Summary
Include API integration tests to reuse the shared Docker Compose PostgreSQL service instead of spawning per-process test containers.

## Changes
- updated make api-test to run against the shared local PostgreSQL instance started via make infra-postgres-up
- taught btc-network-testkit to use BTC_NETWORK_TEST_POSTGRES_ADMIN_URL when provided, while keeping the existing Testcontainers fallback for direct test usage
- changed API test databases to use unique names per process so repeated cargo test runs do not collide on the same shared PostgreSQL instance
- added default teardown for API test databases in the testkit, with BTC_NETWORK_TEST_KEEP_DATABASES as an escape hatch for inspection
- reduced API test database pool size to avoid connection pressure and intermittent PoolTimedOut failures in doc and route tests
- updated scripts/test_summary.sh so the workspace test flow passes the shared PostgreSQL admin URL to the API package tests
- updated CI to start the shared PostgreSQL service before make test and stop it afterward

The previous refactor still allowed multiple PostgreSQL instances to be created during cargo test because test process boundaries made the in-process Testcontainers cache insufficient. author: xavierbriand
body:
## 1. Story

[Epic 2, Story 2.3 — Transaction Builder & Auto-Tagging Domain Service](../blob/main/docs/epics.md#story-23-transaction-builder--auto-tagging-domain-service).

## 2. Intent

Convert each \`IngestItem\` (from Story 2.1's CSV parser, filtered by Story 2.2's idempotency) into a balanced double-entry \`Transaction\`. Auto-tags descriptions against a regex seed (8 categories) and classifies "PAIEMENT CARTE X####" lines on the main account as internal transfers (issue #26) to prevent double-counting against per-card granular statements. No persistence (Story 2.5), no CLI (Story 2.4).

## 3. Alternatives considered

- **Suffix-match on \`AccountConfig.id\` via \`endsWith(…)\` for card settlements** — rejected; Plan agent caught the collision case: a bank account id ending in the same 4 digits as a card's suffix would silently misclassify. Switched to an explicit \`AccountConfig.cardSuffix: string\` field with a Zod cross-field refinement (required iff \`type: 'card'\`).
- **Numeric confidence score (0–1)** — rejected; YAGNI. Story 2.4's interactive loop only branches on "prompt review or not" — a boolean in disguise. Binary \`'high' | 'low'\` is honest; converting later is mechanical.
- **YAML-loaded user-customisable auto-tag rules** — rejected for MVP; Story 2.4's interactive per-item tagging is a more ergonomic affordance than a YAML rule editor. Trigger condition documented: if Story 2.4 slips more than one iteration, file a YAML-override issue.
- **Optional \`AccountConfig.type\` with default 'bank'** — rejected; implicit-default would silently miscategorize a card as a bank account. Required enum keeps the user honest.
- **\`crypto.randomUUID\` hardcoded in Core** — rejected; breaks Core-has-no-Node-imports. Followed the Story 2.2 \`HashFn\`/\`NodeHashFn\` pattern: \`UuidGen\` port in Core, \`nodeUuidGen\` adapter in Infra.
- **\`buildAll\` returns \`Result<BuildOutcome[]>\`** — rejected; one bad item shouldn't abort a 150-row batch. Returns \`{ built, failed }\` split, mirroring Story 2.1's per-row parse-stage error pattern.
- **Mixing the card-settlement classifier into \`AutoTagRule[]\`** — rejected; classifier needs \`sourceAccount.type === 'bank'\` AND cross-ref against the accounts array. Structural not description-only; kept as a separate pre-tagging step.

## 4. Selected solution & rationale

**Config additions (Infra):** \`AccountConfig.type: 'bank' | 'card'\` (required enum) + \`AccountConfig.cardSuffix?: string\` (required iff \`type==='card'\`, regex \`/^\\d{4}$/\`). Zod \`superRefine\` for the cross-field rule. PII-safe error messages.

**Core helpers:**
- [\`src/core/ingest/account-names.ts\`](../blob/main/src/core/ingest/account-names.ts): pure helpers \`bankAccount(id)\`, \`cardAccount(id)\`, \`expenseAccount(cat)\`, \`incomeAccount(cat)\` for colon-delimited CoA-style account names.
- [\`src/core/ingest/auto-tag-rules.ts\`](../blob/main/src/core/ingest/auto-tag-rules.ts): \`AutoTagRule\` type + \`DEFAULT_RULES\` seed (8 categories: Transport, Groceries, Fuel, Restaurant, Utilities, BankingFees, Insurance, Subscriptions; French-biased based on BPCE data).

**Core service:** [\`TransactionBuilder\`](../blob/main/src/core/ingest/transaction-builder.ts) — constructor DI on \`(accounts, rules, idGen)\`. Methods \`build(item)\` and \`buildAll(items)\`. Pure; no IO. Card-settlement classifier runs before auto-tagging; on match (one card with matching \`cardSuffix\`), produces \`classification: 'internal-transfer'\`; on zero/multi-match, falls through to Uncategorized expense (never silent misclassification). The 4-row direction→debit/credit table is concentrated in a \`makeOutcome\` helper after a Phase-4 refactor pass.

**Core port:** \`UuidGen = () => string\`. Infra: \`nodeUuidGen\` wraps \`crypto.randomUUID\`.

**Transaction pass-through:** \`transaction.description\` === original \`IngestItem.description\` (original, not the matched category — audit trail). \`transaction.occurredAt\` === exact \`IngestItem.occurredAt\` string (Story 2.2's idempotency hash depends on it). Tests assert both.

## 5. Gherkin scenarios

Nine scenarios map 1:1 to unit tests (one \`describe\` per scenario) in [tests/unit/core/ingest/transaction-builder.test.ts](../blob/main/tests/unit/core/ingest/transaction-builder.test.ts). Full Gherkin text in the plan file ([docs/plans/story-2.3.md](../blob/main/docs/plans/story-2.3.md) § Gherkin scenarios). Summary:

- **AC1/AC2 — expense on bank account** → debit \`Expense:Transport\`, credit \`Assets:Bank:main-1\`
- **Expense on card account** → debit \`Expense:Groceries\`, credit \`Liabilities:CreditCard:card-1234\`
- **Inflow on card account (refund)** → sides reversed
- **Unmatched description** → \`Uncategorized\` + \`confidence: 'low'\`
- **AC#26 — PAIEMENT CARTE X1234 on bank** → internal-transfer, debit \`Liabilities:CreditCard:card-1234\`, credit \`Assets:Bank:main-1\`
- **Ambiguous suffix** → Uncategorized expense (never silent misclassification)
- **\`buildAll\` batch** → \`{ built, failed }\` split, preserves input order
- **Distinct UUIDs per item** (5 items → 5 distinct \`.id\`; Plan agent catch)
- **\`description\` + \`occurredAt\` pass-through** (Plan agent catches)

## 6. Plan for Sonnet

Full plan committed at [docs/plans/story-2.3.md](../blob/main/docs/plans/story-2.3.md) (convention from Story 2.2 retro action A — plan lives in repo alongside retrospective).

Commit sequence (10 commits total: 1 chore + 6 test/feat + 2 refactor + 1 retro):

1. \`chore(docs)\`: refresh CLAUDE.md § 1 + add Story 2.3 plan
2. \`test(config)\`: \`AccountConfig.type\` enum + \`cardSuffix\` cross-field validation — failing
3. \`feat(config)\`: \`AccountConfig.type\` + \`cardSuffix\` minimal green
4. \`test(ingest)\`: \`TransactionBuilder\` + auto-tagger obvious basics — failing
5. \`feat(ingest)\`: \`TransactionBuilder\` + auto-tagger minimal green
6. \`test(ingest)\`: card-settlement classifier — failing
7. \`feat(ingest)\`: card-settlement classifier minimal green
8. \`refactor(ingest)\`: tidy (defaultUuidGen IIFE)
9. \`refactor(ingest)\`: extract \`makeOutcome\` helper (Phase-4 retro-check finding)
10. \`chore(retro)\`: Story 2.3 retrospective + sonnet-implementer 60-LOC trigger

Adapter-story sizing per § 6.6. Zero green-on-landing (compare Story 2.1's 3 of 5). Phase 4 retro-check produced one refactor — \`build()\` at 84 LOC with 4-way duplication → \`makeOutcome\` extraction (commit \`df31b03\`). \`build()\` now ~33 LOC.

## 7. Suggestion log

| Phase | Suggestion | Resolution | Link / Reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plan-stress | \`id.endsWith(suffix)\` for card classifier → explicit \`AccountConfig.cardSuffix\` field | adopted | Plan updated; collision case (\`bank-91234\` / \`card-1234\`) made explicit |
| Plan-stress | Binary \`confidence\` OK as planned | accepted | Numeric without scoring model would be false precision |
| Plan-stress | Hardcoded French auto-tag seed without YAML override | deferred trigger | No issue yet; trigger condition: file if Story 2.4 slips >1 iteration |
| Plan-stress | Required \`type\` enum OK as planned | accepted | Adding \`'savings'\` later is additive, not breaking |
| Plan-stress | \`UuidGen\` port OK as planned | accepted | Matches Story 2.2 \`HashFn\` precedent; Core-purity rule |
| Plan-stress P1 | Missing test: \`buildAll\` assigns distinct UUIDs per item | adopted | Plan + tests added |
| Plan-stress P2 | Missing test: \`transaction.description\` preserves original (not category) | adopted | Plan + tests added; audit-trail invariant |
| Plan-stress P2 | Missing test: \`occurredAt\` pass-through (no reformat) | adopted | Plan + tests added; determinism + idempotency-hash dependency |
| Phase-4 retro | \`TransactionBuilder.build()\` ~84 LOC with 4-way duplication | adopted | Extracted \`makeOutcome\` helper in commit \`df31b03\`; \`build()\` now ~33 LOC |
| Phase-4 retro | Sonnet's refactor slot deferred the \`build()\` extraction too quietly | adopted | CLA

author: martinopedal
body:
Fixes the recurring `Cannot bind argument to parameter 'Response' because it is null` failure on `.github/workflows/pr-review-gate.yml` (5 failures observed on PR #495, see runs `24804889076` and earlier).

## Root cause

`ConvertTo-TriageResponse` was declared with `[Parameter(Mandatory)] [object] $Response` and called from `Merge-TriageResponses` via `@($Responses | ForEach-Object { ConvertTo-TriageResponse -Response $_ })`. `Get-ModelResponses` could return `@($null)` from `@($raw | ConvertFrom-Json -ErrorAction Stop)` when `ModelResponsesPath` / `PR_REVIEW_GATE_RESPONSES_JSON` contains JSON literal `null` or empty payload, leading to a `-Response $null` bind error that the outer catch then logged with no stack location, exiting 1.

## Fix (defense in depth)

1. **`Get-ModelResponses`** — collapses to `@()` for whitespace / JSON-null / empty-array input, and filters `` from any parsed array.
2. **`ConvertTo-TriageResponse`** — `[AllowNull()]` (not `Mandatory`); returns `` for null or whitespace string input.
3. **`Merge-TriageResponses`** — filters `` on both sides of the pipeline (incoming + post-conversion).
4. **Outer catch** — surfaces `.InvocationInfo.PositionMessage` (sanitized via `Remove-Credentials`) so future failures show the failing line, not just the message.
5. **Tests** — six new Pester regression cases under a `null-safe model response handling` Context.

## Test results

Local: `Invoke-Pester -Path .\tests\shared -CI` → **497 / 497 pass**, 0 fail.

Closes the bug class behind 5x `review-gate` failures on PR #495.

author: calumr23
body:
https://liferay.atlassian.net/browse/LRCI-6191

**What is being fixed:** The `source-format-current-branch` target only builds the Source Formatter jar from HEAD when the diff touches `modules/util/source-formatter` or `source-formatter.properties`, or when on a release branch. Freshly merged SF changes upstream are not exercised until BChan publishes a new jar — contributors have had to add dummy edits to force the source-build path.

**How it is being fixed:** A new property, `sf.force.build.from.source.suites`, holds a whitelist of `CI_TEST_SUITE` names. When the current suite is in that list, `source-format-current-branch` builds SF from source regardless of the diff. The default whitelist contains `sf`, so `ci:test:sf` always exercises the latest SF code from HEAD. Other suites remain opt-in by adding to the list.

🎯 **What:** Replaced the cryptographically insecure `Math.random()` with `window.crypto.getRandomValues()` in the decorative background line generation logic.

⚠️ **Risk:** `Math.random()` is not cryptographically secure, meaning its output can be predictable. While currently used for decorative background lines, using insecure PRNGs is a poor security practice and could lead to vulnerabilities if similar logic is applied to security-sensitive features like token generation or session IDs.

🛡️ **Solution:** Implemented a `secureRandom()` helper function that uses the Web Crypto API's `window.crypto.getRandomValues()` to generate random floats in the range `[0, 1)`. All occurrences of `Math.random()` in `index.html` were updated to use this secure alternative.

body:
# Description

Adds bulk import/export functionality for environment variables, enabling easier CI/CD integration, backups, and bulk configuration management.

## New Commands

### `railway variable import`

Import environment variables from a `.env` or `.json` file.

```bash
# Import from .env file (auto-detected)
railway variable import --file .env.staging

# Import from JSON file
railway variable import --file backup.json

# Import to specific service/environment
railway variable import --file .env --service <my-service> --environment <production/staging/etc>

# Auto-accept all overwrites (non-interactive/CI mode)
railway variable import --file .env --yes

# Import without triggering deployments
railway variable import --file .env --skip-deploys

# JSON output
railway variable import --file .env --json
```

**Features:**
- Auto-detects format by file extension (`.json` vs `.env`)
- Interactive conflict resolution (prompts with `[y/N/q]` for existing keys)
- Non-TTY mode skips conflicts with warning (use `--yes` to override)
- Supports quoted values, escape sequences (`\n`, `\t`, `\r`, `\"`), comments, and empty lines

### `railway variable export`

Export environment variables to a `.env` or `.json` file.

```bash
# Export to .env file
railway variable export --file .env.backup

# Export to JSON file
railway variable export --file backup.json

# Export from specific service/environment
railway variable export --file prod.env --service my-service --environment production

# JSON output to stdout
railway variable export --file backup.env --json
```

**Features:**
- Auto-detects format by file extension
- Properly escapes special characters for `.env` format
- Pretty-printed JSON output

## Supported File Formats

### .env Format
```bash
# Basic key-value pairs
DATABASE_URL=postgres://localhost/mydb
API_KEY=secret123

# Double-quoted values with escape sequences
JSON_DATA="{\"key\": \"value\"}"
MULTILINE="line1\nline2\ttab"

# Single-quoted values (no escape processing)
LITERAL='no $pecial \processing'

# Empty values
EMPTY=

# Comments and empty lines are ignored
# This is a comment
```

### JSON Format
```json
{
  "DATABASE_URL": "postgres://localhost/mydb",
  "API_KEY": "secret123",
  "DEBUG": "true"
}
```

## CI/CD Usage Example

```bash
# Export production variables for backup
railway variable export --file prod-backup.json --environment production

# Import variables to staging (non-interactive)
railway variable import --file prod-backup.json --environment staging --yes

# Or use --skip-deploys to set variables without triggering deploys
railway variable import --file .env.ci --yes --skip-deploys
```

## Testing

All tests pass:
- 9 CLI parsing tests for import/export commands
- 18 unit tests for .env and JSON parsers
- 135 total tests

```bash
cargo test
```

body:
## Summary

Adds an automated documentation generator that parses the contract source with `syn` and emits Markdown, HTML, and JSON API docs (issue #66).

## New files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `tools/doc-generator/src/parser.rs` | AST parser — extracts public functions from `#[contractimpl]` blocks and error variants from `#[contracterror]` enums |
| `tools/doc-generator/src/templates.rs` | Renders `ContractDoc` → Markdown, self-contained HTML with JS search, JSON |
| `tools/doc-generator/src/main.rs` | CLI binary (`--input`, `--out-dir`, `--contract`) + integration tests |
| `tools/doc-generator/Cargo.toml` | Crate manifest (`syn`, `quote`, `clap`, `serde_json`) |
| `scripts/generate-docs.sh` | One-command generation; `--commit` flag for local use |
| `.github/workflows/generate-docs.yml` | CI: fails PRs if `docs/api/` is stale; auto-commits on main |

## What the parser extracts

- **Functions** — name, `///` doc comments (multi-line), parameters (skipping `env: Env`), return type
- **Errors** — variant name + numeric discriminant from `#[contracterror]` enums

## Outputs written to `docs/api/`

- `README.md` — Markdown with error table, per-function signature, parameter table, example snippet
- `index.html` — Self-contained HTML page with live JS search (no external dependencies)
- `api.json` — Machine-readable JSON for search indexing or downstream tooling

## CI behaviour

- Triggers only when `contracts/tipjar/src/lib.rs` or the generator itself changes
- On PRs: runs generator and fails if `docs/api/` differs from committed state
- On main push: auto-commits refreshed docs with `[skip ci]`

## Tests

- Public functions extracted, private functions excluded
- `env` parameter skipped in all function docs
- Doc comments (including multi-line) extracted correctly
- Return types captured
- Error variant codes parsed from discriminants
- Markdown output contains expected headings and error table
- HTML output contains search input and function anchors
- JSON output roundtrips correctly

Closes #66

This PR updates [simplejson](https://pypi.org/project/simplejson) from **3.19.2** to **4.1.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 4.1.0
   ```
   * The C extension now accelerates encoding when ``indent=`` is set.
  Previously the encoder fell back to the pure-Python implementation
  whenever a non-None ``indent`` was passed; now the C encoder emits
  the newline-plus-indent prefix, the level-aware item separator, and
  the closing indent directly.  A representative nested-dict workload
  benchmarks about 4-5x faster end-to-end, and the ``indent=0`` and
  empty-container edge cases continue to match the Python output
  byte-for-byte.

* The C extension now emits PEP 678 ``exc.add_note()`` annotations on
  serialization failures, matching the pure-Python encoder.  A chained
  error on ``{'a': [1, object(), 3]}`` produces the same three notes
  (``when serializing object object``, ``when serializing list item 1``,
  ``when serializing dict item 'a'``) whether the speedups are loaded
  or not, so the add_note assertions in ``test_errors.py`` no longer
  need ``indent=2`` to force the Python path.
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.0.1
   ```
   * Skip uploading Pyodide/wasm wheels to PyPI, which rejects them with
  "unsupported platform tag 'pyodide_2024_0_wasm32'". The wheels are
  still built in CI and preserved as workflow artifacts.
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/375
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 4.0.0
   ```
   * simplejson 4 requires Python 2.7 or Python 3.8+. Older Python
  versions (2.5, 2.6, 3.0-3.7) are no longer supported. pip will
  not install simplejson 4 on unsupported versions.

* The C extension now uses heap types and per-module state instead of
  static types and global state. This is required for free-threading
  support and sub-interpreter isolation. The Python-level API is
  unchanged.

* Full support for Python 3.13+ free-threading (PEP 703). The C
  extension is now safe to use with the GIL disabled (python3.14t):
  - Converted all static types to heap types with per-module state
  - Added per-object critical sections to scanner and encoder
  - Added free-threading-safe dict operations for Python 3.13+
  - Unified per-module state management and templated parser
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/363
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/364
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/365
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/367
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/369

* Numerous C extension memory safety fixes:
  - Fix use-after-free and leak in encoder ident handling
  - Fix NULL dereferences on OOM in module init and static string init
  - Fix reference leaks in dict encoder (skipkeys item, variable shadowing)
  - Fix member table copy-paste, exception clobbering, missing Py_VISIT
  - Fix error-as-truthy bugs in maybe_quote_bigint and is_raw_json
  - Fix iterable_as_array swallowing MemoryError and KeyboardInterrupt
  - Fix for_json and _asdict swallowing MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt,
    and other non-AttributeError exceptions raised by user __getattr__
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/355
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/356
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/357
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/358
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/359
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/360
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/373

* C/Python parity fixes:
  - Fix C scanstring off-by-one bounds checks that caused truncated
    or boundary \uXXXX escapes to raise "Invalid \\uXXXX escape
    sequence" instead of "Unterminated string", and report error
    position at the 'u' instead of the leading backslash. The C and
    Python decoders now agree on exception class, message, and
    position across all tested edge cases.
  - Align the Python encoder's dispatch order with the C encoder for
    objects that define _asdict(). Previously a list/tuple/dict
    subclass with an _asdict() method encoded as its container type
    under the Python encoder and as the _asdict() return value under
    the C encoder; both now check _asdict() before list/tuple/dict.
    for_json() continues to outrank _asdict() in both.
  - Fix C scanstring raising a plain ValueError ("end is out of
    bounds") instead of JSONDecodeError for out-of-range end indices.
    User code with `except JSONDecodeError:` now catches both the
    C and pure-Python paths consistently.
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/372

* C extension performance and correctness improvements:
  - Add PyDict_Next fast path for unsorted exact-dict encoding,
    avoiding intermediate items list and N tuple allocations
  - Add indexed fast path for exact list/tuple encoding, avoiding
    iterator allocation and per-item PyIter_Next overhead
  - Use PyUnicodeWriter as JSON_Accu backend on Python 3.14+,
    eliminating intermediate string objects and ''.join calls
  - Fix integer overflow in ascii_escape output_size calculation
    that could cause buffer overwrite on pathologically large strings
  - Fix list encoder separator counter overflow (int to Py_ssize_t)
  - Dead code cleanup (unreachable NULL checks, do-while wrappers)
  https://github.com/simplejson/simplejson/pull/370

* Added Python 3.14 support and updated to cibuildwheel 3.2.1. CI now
  tests free-threaded (3.14t) and debug builds with -Werror, refcount

## Summary

This branch rolls up a set of desktop hardening and UX cleanup fixes across Electron startup, IPC sender validation, accessibility landmarks, and stale debug instrumentation.

- removes stray debug `fetch()` calls to `127.0.0.1:7734` from the main process MQTT path and the renderer Meshtastic device hook so the app no longer emits local connection-refused noise during normal use

- keeps development workable by allowing `http://localhost` and `http://127.0.0.1` IPC senders only in dev mode, while production stays restricted to packaged origins
- fixes landmark structure in the app shell and updates renderer coverage so axe-based accessibility checks pass cleanly
- restores the unified bottom horizontal scrollbar by removing nested `overflow-x-auto` containers inside panel content
- removes the remaining renderer test `act(...)` warning from the app test suite

  `tablesApi.createTable` with `tableType = METRIC_VIEW` plus the structured
  `view_dependencies` payload.
- `SELECT * FROM <metric_view>` resolves the row through `UCProxy.loadTable` (the
  single-RPC primitive), returns a `MetadataTable(ViewInfo)`, and Spark's analyzer
  expands the YAML body into the underlying aggregation over the source table.
- `DROP VIEW`, `SHOW VIEWS`, `DESCRIBE TABLE` / `EXTENDED` all work end-to-end against
  metric views. `DROP TABLE` on a metric view raises `WRONG_COMMAND_FOR_OBJECT_TYPE`
  ("Use DROP VIEW instead").

## What's in the diff

### 1. `UCSingleCatalog` mixes in `TableViewCatalog`

Spark's [SPARK-52729](https://github.com/apache/spark/pull/51419) introduced
`ViewCatalog` for v2 catalogs that expose views, and a sibling interface for catalogs
that expose **both** tables and views in a shared identifier namespace; the latter was
renamed to `TableViewCatalog` (with companion renames `MetadataOnlyTable` ->
`MetadataTable`, `loadRelation` -> `loadTableOrView`) and grew an abstract
`renameView(oldIdent, newIdent)` in
[SPARK-56655](https://github.com/apache/spark/commit/384cd0d3e83). UC exposes both
tables and views, so `UCSingleCatalog` and `UCProxy` mix in `TableViewCatalog` and
implement the view-side methods (`createView`, `dropView`, `renameView`, `listViews`,
`loadTableOrView`).

The orthogonality contract (`TableCatalog` methods behave as if views don't exist, and
vice versa) is honored:

- `listTables` filters out view-like UC `TableType`s via the shared `viewLikeUcTypes` map (see below).
- `listViews` filters in the same set.
- `loadTable` rejects view-like rows by throwing `NoSuchTableException`; `loadView`
  throws `NoSuchViewException` for table rows. (See the section "Single-RPC primitive"
  below for *which* layer enforces this -- it shifted between `UCProxy` and
  `UCSingleCatalog` in the latest revision.)
- `dropTable` returns `false` for a view (does not delete); `dropView` returns `false`
  for a table. SPARK-56655's `DropTableExec` / `DropViewExec` decode the false-return
  into the user-facing `WRONG_COMMAND_FOR_OBJECT_TYPE` error.
- `createTable` over a view ident maps UC 409 to `TableAlreadyExistsException`;
  `createView` over a table ident maps to `ViewAlreadyExistsException`.
- `renameView` is wired through both `UCSingleCatalog` and `UCProxy` but currently
  throws `UnsupportedOperationException` -- UC OSS has no rename-view endpoint,
  mirroring the existing `renameTable` stub.

### 2. View-like UC table type -> Spark table type mapping

`UCSingleCatalog.viewLikeUcTypes: Map[TableType, Option[String]]` is the single
source of truth for which UC `TableType` values are view-like, and what Spark
`TableSummary` table-type string they map to. Today: `METRIC_VIEW` -> `Some("METRIC_VIEW")`,
`MATERIALIZED_VIEW` -> `None` (no Spark mapping yet). Predicates derived from the map
(`isViewLikeTableType`, `isViewCommandsSupportedTableType`, `ucTableTypeToSparkViewType`,
`sparkViewTypeToUcTableType`) all read from this map, so adding a new view-like UC type
in the future is a one-line change. `createView` uses the reverse lookup
`sparkViewTypeToUcTableType` to derive `CreateTable.tableType` from the supplied
`ViewInfo.properties().get(PROP_TABLE_TYPE)`, so it works for any view kind in the map
without a touch on the method.

### 3. `UCSingleCatalog` keeps the Delta delegate; `UCProxy` is the v2 entry point

`UCSingleCatalog` continues to wrap `DeltaCatalog` (when on the classpath) as its
`delegate` for table operations -- DeltaCatalog needs to intercept managed/external Delta
table create/load paths and add Delta-specific behavior. View operations bypass
`delegate` and call `ucProxy` directly because Delta has no role in view handling. The
two references are documented inline at the field declarations.

### 4. Single-RPC primitive: `UCProxy.loadTable` (review feedback from 2026-05-08)

This is a structural change vs. the first revision of this PR, addressing the main
concern raised in the review meeting on 2026-05-08:

> Previously, every `loadTableOrView` call to a non-view UC table issues **two**
> `tablesApi.getTable` RPCs -- one in `UCSingleCatalog.loadTableOrView` to classify
> view vs. table, and a second through `delegate.loadTable -> Delta -> super.loadTable
> -> UCProxy.loadTableOrView`. With the metric-view PR landed, every read in the
> catalog flows through `loadTableOrView`, so this doubles RPC traffic to the UC server
> for every table load.

Fix ("flip the logic"):

- **`UCProxy.loadTable` is now the single primitive.** It does the UC `getTable` once
  and dispatches by `TableType`: a view-like row is wrapped as
  `MetadataTable + ViewInfo`; everything else goes through `loadV1Table` (which
  generates temp credentials).
- **`UCProxy.loadTableOrView` is now a one-line passthrough to `loadTable`.**
- **`UCSingleCatalog.loadTableOrView` is now a one-line `delegate.loadTable(ident)`
  call.** When `delegate` is Delta wrapping `UCProxy`, the call chain is
  `Delta.loadTable -> super.loadTable (DelegatingCatalogExtension) -> UCProxy.loadTable`,
  and Delta's `case o => o` fallthrough returns the `MetadataTable` unchanged for views.
  **One RPC for everything** -- table loads, view loads, view-vs-table classification.
- **`UCSingleCatalog.loadTable` re-checks the result** and throws `NoSuchTableException`
  if `delegate.loadTable` came back with a `MetadataTable + ViewInfo`. This preserves
  the `TableViewCatalog.loadTable` orthogonality contract -- callers that explicitly
  want only tables (e.g. write paths) shouldn't accidentally get a view back from the
  now-permissive `UCProxy.loadTable`.

Updated data flow:

```
CREATE VIEW ... WITH METRICS:
  Spark CreateMetricViewCommand
    -> DataSourceV2Strategy intercept (non-session catalog)
    -> CreateV2MetricViewExec (extends V2CreateViewPreparation)
    -> UCSingleCatalog.createView -> ucProxy.createView
    -> UCProxy.createView builds CreateTable(METRIC_VIEW) with:
       - tableType derived from ViewInfo.properties().get(PROP_TABLE_TYPE)
       - viewDefinition = original YAML body
       - viewDependencies = converted from Spark's structural DependencyList
       - columns: each column's `typeJson` is built by UCColumnJson (preserves
         metric_view.type / metric_view.expr column metadata)
    -> tablesApi.createTable

SELECT * FROM <table_or_view_ident> (single-RPC path):
  Spark resolver
    -> UCSingleCatalog.loadTableOrView(ident)
    -> delegate.loadTable(ident)            (delegate = DeltaCatalog)
    -> Delta.loadTable -> super.loadTable   (DelegatingCatalogExtension)
    -> UCProxy.loadTable(ident)             (the single primitive)
       -> tablesApi.getTable                (ONE UC RPC)
       -> if view-like (per viewLikeUcTypes):
            new MetadataTable(toViewInfo(t), ident.toString)
          else:
            loadV1Table(ident, t)
    -> Delta.loadTable `case o => o` returns MetadataTable unchanged
    -> Spark analyzer expands MetadataTable+ViewInfo via V1Table.toCatalogTable
       -> CatalogTableType.METRIC_VIEW -> ResolveMetricView (existing V1 rule)

```

`loadView`, `tableExists`, and `viewExists` on `UCProxy` are int

author: ricky074game
body:
### Motivation
- Reduce duplicated IRQ entry logic between the ARM7 path (`CheckInterrupts`) and ARM9 overlay logic and centralize CPSR/SPSR/LR semantics in one place.
- Ensure IRQ vector selection consistently targets the `...0018` offset and can pick low/high vector base according to CP15 V-bit policy.
- Wire IF/IE/IME gating and IRQ-disable checks through a single helper so both CPU paths behave identically.

### Description
- Introduce `ComputeIRQVectorTarget`, `EnterIRQ`, and an extended `CheckInterrupts` in `runtime/src/hw/hw_irq.h` to compute the `0x18` vector target (respecting CP15 high-vector bit), save SPSR/LR semantics, switch modes, and disable IRQs.
- Replace the inline ARM9 IRQ state transition in `runtime/src/hw/hw_overlay.cpp` with a call to the shared `CheckInterrupts(ctx, ctx->mem->irq_arm9, 4, true)` helper so ARM9 uses the same entry path as ARM7.
- Update `runtime/tests/test_hw_irq.cpp` to reflect the new default low-vector target (`0x00000018`) and to add a test validating ARM9 high-vector (`0xFFFF0018`) behavior with the LR offset.

### Testing
- Updated unit tests in `runtime/tests/test_hw_irq.cpp` to cover low-vector default behavior and ARM9 high-vector plus LR offset behavior (tests added/modified but not executed here).
- Attempted to configure and build tests with `cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo` and build targets, but the CMake configure step failed because FetchContent failed to clone the external `capstone` repository (network/proxy returned HTTP 403), so automated tests could not be run in this environment.

author: rubenfuquene
body:
## Problem
Presigned URLs generated by the document upload service were returning 403 Forbidden errors in Railway staging environment. Investigation revealed the `X-Amz-Credential` parameter was malformed (missing AccessKeyId), indicating environment variables were not properly loaded in the HTTP request context.

## Root Cause
- Environment variables were cached during Docker image build with empty/stale values
- CI bootstrap logic and production runtime needs were conflated in the same codebase
- Config cache persistence across deployments caused inconsistent behavior

## Solution
Implemented clean separation between CI bootstrap and production runtime configuration:

### Backend Changes
1. **docker-entrypoint.sh** - Added explicit `BOOTSTRAP_ENV_FILE` flag to control environment file generation
   - New functions: `is_env_bootstrap_enabled()`, `validate_required_runtime_env()`, `is_runtime_config_cache_enabled()`, `refresh_laravel_config_cache_if_enabled()`
   - Validates required AWS variables in production
   - Optional runtime config cache regeneration

2. **.env.example.ci** - New CI-specific environment template with safe dummy values for testing

3. **nixpacks.toml** - Changed `config:cache` to `config:clear` in build pipeline to prevent persisting empty values

4. **.env.example & .env.example.prd** - Cleaned and documented as reference-only templates

### CI Changes
5. **.github/workflows/tests.yml** - Updated to use `.env.example.ci` and export `BOOTSTRAP_ENV_FILE=true`

## Configuration Required (Railway)
After merging, configure Railway service variables:

- BOOTSTRAP_ENV_FILE=false
- AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=<value>
- AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=<value>
- AWS_BUCKET=assembled-breadbox-bxpl7x
- AWS_URL=https://t3.storageapi.dev
- AWS_ENDPOINT=https://t3.storageapi.dev

**Final phase of the canonical compilation plan.** Merging this PR closes the 8-phase initiative that evolved AskMyDocs from a flat-chunk RAG into an enterprise canonical knowledge compilation platform.

This PR is **docs-only** — zero runtime changes. It ships the documentation layer that reviewers, operators, and downstream teams need to understand and maintain the canonical subsystem correctly.

## What ships

- §6 non-obvious decisions: 6 new entries (canonical markdown is SoT, human-gated promotion, rejected injection by design, degrade to no-op, tenant-scoped slug/doc_id, …).

body:
## Summary

- **Root cause**: Step 6 of `createOrder` called `getOrCreateInternalId('Order', externalOrderId, destinationConnectionId)`, minting a fresh internal id (`ol_order_PRESTA_Y`) that never matched the source-side id (`ol_order_ALLEGRO_X`) queried by Step 0's idempotency check. Every retry created a second PrestaShop order.
- **Fix**: Step 6 now calls `createMapping('Order', externalOrderId, destinationConnectionId, metadataInternalOrderId)`, writing the destination mapping under the same internal id Step 0 queries. Both `MappingAlreadyExistsError` and `DuplicateIdentifierMappingError` are caught as idempotent success.
- **Fallback preserved**: when `metadata.internalOrderId` is absent (no current production caller hits this), the old `getOrCreateInternalId` behavior is kept with a `logger.warn` to make drift detectable.

## Changes

- `libs/integrations/prestashop/src/infrastructure/adapters/prestashop-order-processor-manager.adapter.ts` — rewrite Step 6, add imports for the two error classes
- `libs/integrations/prestashop/src/infrastructure/adapters/__tests__/prestashop-order-processor-manager.adapter.spec.ts` — update existing assertions, add idempotency test and concurrent-race (DuplicateIdentifierMappingError) test
- `docs/plans/implementation-plan-348-prestashop-order-idempotency-fix.md` — implementation plan (new file)

## Legacy data note

Existing `ol_order_PRESTA_*` mappings written by the old code won't be found by Step 0. This PR prevents new duplicates. A one-shot reconciliation script can link historical rows if needed — tracked as a follow-up in #348.

## Test plan

- [x] All 12 adapter unit tests pass (including 2 new: idempotency + race)
- [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 errors
- [x] `pnpm type-check` — clean
- [x] `pnpm test` — all workspaces green

Closes #348

┌ Hermes Cloud ┐ ┌ Your VPS ┐ ┌ Local via Tunnel ┐ ┌ Local Direct ┐
│     ☁ Pro    │ │  🌐 BYO  │ │      🔗 BYO      │ │    💻 Free   │
└──────────────┘ └──────────┘ └──────────────────┘ └──────────────┘

                      [Continue to Projects →]
```

Default: Hermes Cloud. Switching modes clears the cloud picker's selection so Continue state is honest. Nothing downstream changes — once Continue is enabled and clicked, the existing /projects flow runs.

- **Hermes Cloud** — existing grid, filtered to `!owner_user_id` so personal agents don't double-render.

  - Test button → POST `/api/agents/test`. On failure, mode-specific 4-bullet cause list (tunnel: terminal closed, CF rotated URL, adapter crashed, key expired; VPS: firewall, DNS, TLS, key expired).
- **Local Direct** — existing `LocalHermesSection` unchanged, rendered inside this panel.

author: adjordje-amd
body:
## Motivation

Add automated clang-tidy static analysis to the rocpdsna CI so that every PR against `sna-develop` (and eventually `develop`) gets visibility into newly introduced lint issues. Third in the planned CI/CD PR series for rocpdsna; follows the formatting (#5313) and build-test (#5314) workflows.

## Technical Details

Adds `.github/workflows/rocpdsna-static-analysis.yml` with a single `clang-tidy` job on `ubuntu-24.04`:

1. Sparse checkout of `projects/rocpdsna/` + `.github/workflows/`
2. Install deps via apt (cmake, gcc, clang-tidy-18, sqlite/spdlog/fmt/json/gtest/gmock/benchmark dev pkgs)
3. Configure with `-DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON`, `BUILD_TESTS=OFF`, `BUILD_BENCHMARKS=OFF` (neither needed for analysis; saves build time)
4. Build the library to populate `compile_commands.json` and any generated headers
5. Run the project's existing `clang-tidy` CMake target which invokes `clang-tidy --config-file=.clang-tidy` against the globbed source/ and include/ files
6. Tee output to `clang-tidy.log`, count warnings/errors, write summary to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`
7. Upload `clang-tidy.log` as artifact

Reuses the existing in-project clang-tidy target (`projects/rocpdsna/CMakeLists.txt:362`) instead of inventing a new invocation, so CI matches what developers run locally with `cmake --build build --target clang-tidy`.

Failure model:
- Warnings do NOT fail the job. The project's `.clang-tidy` has `WarningsAsErrors: ''`. Without this CI would block on the ~116 existing warnings; visibility-only is the right Tier 1 stance.
- Errors DO fail the job (clang-tidy exits non-zero).
- Step summary always shows warning/error counts; full log uploaded as artifact.

A future PR can tighten this by setting `WarningsAsErrors` for specific check categories once the existing warnings are addressed.

Workflow conventions match the rest of the rocpdsna CI series:
- Triggers on `pull_request` (any target) plus `push` to `develop` and `sna-develop`
- Path filters scope to `projects/rocpdsna/**` (excluding `build/`, `docs/`, top-level `README.md`)
- Concurrency cancellation enabled
- Read-only permissions
- 20-minute job timeout

## JIRA ID

N/A

## Test Plan

- Local configure with `CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON`
- Local full build (Release, BUILD_TESTS=OFF)
- Local invocation of the `clang-tidy` cmake target with the project's `.clang-tidy` config
- Wall-clock timing with `time cmake --build build --target clang-tidy`
- YAML syntax validation with `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"`
- First CI run on this PR exercises the full job end-to-end

## Test Result

- Local clang-tidy run: 116 warnings, 0 errors, target exits 0
- Wall-clock: 3 min 26 s (single-threaded clang-tidy invocation; well within the 20 min timeout)
- All warnings come from existing code; this PR introduces no new code under analysis
- YAML parse: OK
- CI run on this PR: pending — will update once first run completes

## Submission Checklist

- [ ] Look over the contributing guidelines at https://github.com/ROCm/ROCm/blob/develop/CONTRIBUTING.md#pull-requests.

author: oshoemaker
body:
## Summary
- fix the shared ClickUp deploy-status workflow so merge/backport pushes do not silently skip task updates
- keep the existing commit-range and branch-name detection
- add a final fallback that inspects PR metadata associated with the pushed commit
- add safety rails for this shared workflow repo

## Root cause
The reusable workflow only looked for `CU-...` references in:
1. commit messages in the push range
2. the branch name / latest commit message fallback

That fails for production merge commits like crawlers PR #160, where:
- the push to `main` is a merge commit without `CU-...` in the message
- the target branch is just `main`
- the ClickUp ID exists in the merged PR body/title/head branch, but the workflow never checked PR metadata

Result: the workflow reported success but logged `No ClickUp task IDs found in any commits. Skipping.` and left the story stuck in `In Dev` after a successful prod deploy.

## Change
When commit and branch scanning find nothing, query:
- `GET /repos/{repo}/commits/{sha}/pulls`

Then extract `CU-...` references from:
- PR title
- PR body
- PR head branch

## Safety rails added in this PR
- new `.github/workflows/validate-workflows.yml` PR/push check using `actionlint` + `shellcheck`
- stronger warning output when a deploy-status update skips because no ClickUp task IDs were found
- fixed the inline-script hardening issue flagged by `actionlint` by passing `github.head_ref` through an env var instead of interpolating it directly in bash

## Validation
- reproduced against the real crawlers prod deploy merge SHA `209eb4a72623991817e7c77988f2b1bcf711828d`
- verified the new fallback extracts `CU-86b94z1be` from the associated PR metadata
- ran `actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml` locally after the changes

author: blitzy[bot]
body:
Introduces a new opt-in `qt.workarounds.locale` Bool config option (default `false`) that works around the QtWebEngine 5.15.3 Linux blank-page + Chromium `Network service crashed, restarting service.` crash loop triggered when the active BCP47 locale has no matching `qtwebengine_locales/<locale>.pak` shipped with Qt.

When every activation gate is satisfied — (1) the setting is enabled, (2) the OS is Linux, (3) the QtWebEngine version is exactly 5.15.3, (4) the `qtwebengine_locales` directory exists under `QLibraryInfo.TranslationsPath`, and (5) the current-locale `.pak` file is missing — the new `_get_lang_override` helper in `qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py` applies Chromium's own fallback mappings (e.g. `en-PH → en-US`, `de-CH → de`, `zh-HK → zh-TW`, `es-ES → es-419`) and ultimately falls back to `en-US` so that `_qtwebengine_args()` yields a single `--lang=<locale_name>` token that lets the Chromium subprocess find a valid bundle. If any gate fails, the workaround is skipped entirely and `qt_args()` output remains byte-identical to the pre-change behavior, preserving backward compatibility for every user who does not opt in.

Implementation scope (5 files, 536 additions, 0 deletions):
- `qutebrowser/config/qtargs.py` — adds `import pathlib`, `from PyQt5.QtCore import QLocale, QLibraryInfo`, new `_get_locale_pak_path` and `_get_lang_override` helpers, and the `--lang=<override>` yield in `_qtwebengine_args()` after `_qtwebengine_settings_args(versions)`.
- `qutebrowser/config/configdata.yml` — adds the `qt.workarounds.locale` Bool option as a sibling of `qt.workarounds.remove_service_workers`.
- `doc/help/settings.asciidoc` — adds the settings table row and reference detail block.
- `doc/changelog.asciidoc` — adds the `Added` bullet under `v2.1.0 (unreleased)`.
- `tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py` — adds 63 hermetic parametrized tests (all 5 activation gates, all 8 mapping rules × 16 BCP47 inputs × 2 test entry points, fallback-exists, en-US failsafe, single-token `--lang=` format, plus direct unit tests of both helpers).

All 180 tests in `tests/unit/config/test_qtargs.py` pass (117 pre-existing + 63 new), the broader `tests/unit/config/` suite runs 1908 passed / 1 skipped / 10 xfailed / 0 failed, flake8 and pylint E/F are clean, and mypy on `qtargs.py` itself reports 0 errors. No public API is introduced; all new symbols are underscore-prefixed private helpers confined to `qtargs.py`. No dependency manifests (`requirements.txt`, `misc/requirements/*`, `setup.py`, `tox.ini`) are modified.

Remaining path-to-production work is external to the AAP-scoped autonomous changes: maintainer sign-off, real-hardware integration validation on an affected 5.15.3 Linux system with a locale whose `.pak` is missing, targeted manual QA on 2–3 additional locales, upstream PR merge, and any distro-specific packaging-note coordination.

## Summary

Updates the `go` directive in `go.mod` from `1.25.5` to `1.25.9`.

## Motivation

Go 1.25.9 contains security fixes for 13 `stdlib` gobinary CVEs, including:
- **CRITICAL** CVE-2025-68121
- 12 additional stdlib CVEs

## How it works

The CI pipeline uses `go-version-file: go.mod` with `actions/setup-go@v5`, so updating the `go` directive in `go.mod` is sufficient to make the builder pick up Go 1.25.9 automatically — no workflow changes required.

---
### Kimchi Summary
### What changed
Updates Alpine packages before installing dependencies in the Docker build and bumps the Go version from 1.25.5 to 1.25.9.

### Why
Running `apk upgrade` before installing packages ensures Alpine packages are fully updated, reducing exposure to known CVEs.  A Go upgrade is also included in this change.

### Key changes
- Add `apk upgrade --no-cache` before installing packages in the `build/liqo/Dockerfile`
- Update Go version from 1.25.5 to 1.25.9 in `go.mod`

### Impact
The package upgrade may increase the Docker image build time by a small amount due to the extra apk upgrade.

## Summary

Implements item **#5** of the PR+1 backlog (`reflection.md`): a daily Vercel cron at `/api/cron/classify-backfill` that catches up the long tail of unclassified high-impact observations the ingest-time pipeline never reached.

- Walks `mv_observation_current` for `is_canonical = true AND llm_classified_at IS NULL AND impact_score >= 6`, sorts by `impact_score DESC, published_at DESC`.
- Routes the top N (default **10**, max 100) through the existing `processObservationClassificationQueue` with `reclassifyExisting: false`.
- Logs run summary to `scrape_logs(source_id = NULL)` (kept off the "Last synced" header chip via a filter in `/api/stats`); refreshes MVs at the end so the joined `llm_*` columns light up.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`, fail-closed 503 in production when unset. Kill switch via `CLASSIFY_BACKFILL_DISABLED=1`.

The cron's main visible payoff is the **AI Classifications tab** populating with rows that previously sat at "0 classifications" despite the corpus having 229 observations across 223 clusters.

## What shipped (7 commits)

```
add3715 review(tests+docs): pin candidate helpers + triage guard; add §3.5 + N-9/N-10 follow-ups
66dbd40 review(ux): guard heuristic-vs-LLM category namespace mismatch in AI Classifications tab
9e5d531 review(refactor): share env+repro fingerprint helpers across both candidate builders
346977f review(cron): canonical filter, lower default limit, kill switch, lastScrape filter, auth parity
5e4a5dd docs: extend §3.1d with classify-backfill cron, flip BUGS N-8 to partial
69b9ad3 route: add /api/cron/classify-backfill nightly LLM backfill
954a341 pipeline: extract ClassificationCandidate + report-text into deps-free module
```

| Layer | File | What |
|---|---|---|
| **Cron route** | `app/api/cron/classify-backfill/route.ts` | New. `maxDuration=60`, default limit 10, kill switch, fail-closed prod auth, `is_canonical` filter. |
| **Cron schedule** | `vercel.json` | New entry: `0 3 * * *` |
| **Pure helpers** | `lib/classification/candidate.ts` | New deps-free module. `ClassificationCandidate`, `synthesizeObservationReportText`, `buildEnvFromFingerprintColumns`, `buildReproFromFingerprintMarkers`. Single source of truth shared by ingest + backfill builders. |
| **Backfill projection** | `lib/classification/backfill-candidates.ts` | New. Pure `mv_observation_current` row → `ClassificationCandidate`. |
| **Pipeline refactor** | `lib/classification/pipeline.ts` | Extracted shared types + helpers to `candidate.ts`; re-exports preserve public API. |
| **Ingest builder** | `lib/scrapers/index.ts` | `buildClassificationCandidate` now delegates to the shared helpers — DRY with the cron path. |
| **Stats route** | `app/api/stats/route.ts` | "Last scrape" query now excludes `source_id IS NULL` rows. |
| **Cron parity** | `app/api/cron/scrape/route.ts` | Fail-closed in production when `CRON_SECRET` unset, matching the new cron's posture. |
| **Triage UX** | `components/dashboard/classification-triage.tsx` | Heuristic-vs-LLM category namespace guard (review §1 below). |
| **Tests (+24)** | `tests/classify-backfill.test.ts`, `tests/classification-candidate-helpers.test.ts`, `tests/classification-triage-filter.test.ts` | 8 backfill projection + 9 shared helpers (incl. ingest↔backfill parity) + 7 namespace-guard rule. |
| **Docs** | `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/BUGS.md` | New §3.5 "Scheduled jobs", refreshed §4.8 module map, §3.1d step 6 corrected, §2 ASCII tree updated, BUGS.md N-8 → partial, new N-9 / N-10 follow-ups. |

## Review findings addressed

Two parallel pre-merge reviews were run (senior-eng correctness + architectural integration). Findings landed across the four `review(...)` commits:

### Correctness blockers (all closed)
- **M1 — "Last synced" chip lies after backfill writes:** `/api/stats` `lastScrape` query now filters `source_id IS NOT NULL`. Backfill rows still go to `scrape_logs` for admin/audit; just don't masquerade as scrapes in the header.
- **M2 — `maxDuration=300` silently truncates on Hobby:** dropped to `60` to match `/api/cron/scrape`; `DEFAULT_LIMIT` lowered 25 → 10 so wall-clock fits comfortably under 60s. Without this, Hobby plans terminate mid-loop and leave zombie `status='running'` rows in `scrape_logs` forever.
- **M3 — wasted spend on non-canonical cluster members:** added `.eq("is_canonical", true)`. Cluster-level dashboard surfaces (Priority Matrix, AI tab clusters, hero) read off the canonical row; classifying members independently was burning ~$0.04/call without lighting anything up. Members can still be classified on demand via `/api/observations/[id]/classify`.
- **Arch #1 — heuristic-vs-LLM category namespace mismatch:** the dashboard's `globalCategory` filter uses heuristic slugs (`bug`, `feature-request`, `performance`, …); the AI tab filtered on the LLM enum (`code-generation-quality`, `tool-use-failure`, …). Only `other` overlapped. Clicking the hero "Review {category}" CTA → AI tab silently emptied the queue. Now the triage component computes `knownLlmCategorySlugs` from records and falls back to "all" with a small notice when the global filter doesn't apply. Pinned by `tests/classification-triage-filter.test.ts`.
- **Arch §2 — `/api/cron/scrape` was open in prod when `CRON_SECRET` unset:** mirrored the fail-closed 503 pattern from the new cron. Both crons now behave identically.

### Improvements
- **n3 — kill switch:** `CLASSIFY_BACKFILL_DISABLED=1` short-circuits at the top of `GET` so ops can stop the loop without unsetting `OPENAI_API_KEY` (which would also break the ingest classifier and SignalLayers Refresh).
- **m6 — duplicate env/repro logic:** `buildBackfillCandidates` and `buildClassificationCandidate` were 95% identical. Extracted `buildEnvFromFingerprintColumns` + `buildReproFromFingerprintMarkers` into `candidate.ts`; both call sites delegate. Parity test ensures they cannot diverge silently.
- **m3 — schedule docblock wrong:** "after the last scrape tick of the day" → corrected to "sits between 00:00 and 06:00 ticks".

### Documentation
- New **§3.5 Scheduled jobs** consolidates both crons (cadence, secret policy, kill switches, failure modes, deploy preconditions) — replaces ad-hoc cron docs scattered across §3.1d and route docblocks.
- **§4.8** rewritten to call out `candidate.ts` + `backfill-candidates.ts` and the heuristic-vs-LLM taxonomy split.
- **§2 ASCII tree** registers both new endpoints (`classify-backfill` + `/api/observations/:id/classify`).

## Deferred to BUGS.md (out of scope for this PR)

- **N-9 — TOCTOU race in `hasExistingClassification`:** `SELECT`-then-`INSERT` per observation is racy. Two overlapping runs can each pass the existence check and write duplicate rows (~$0.08 wasted). The obvious partial unique index `WHERE prior_classification_id IS NULL` would block large-model escalations (which write a second row pointing back via `prior_classification_id`). Right fix is either an advisory lock or a single-statement RPC. Defer until daily cadence shows duplicate rate matters.
- **N-10 — admin one-shot panel:** the cron caps at 10 obs/run by default; clearing an initial backlog needs a higher-cap manual trigger. `reflection.md` #5's "Watch-outs" called this out as a parallel to `/api/admin/backfill-derivations`. Smallest implementation outlined in BUGS.md N-10.

## Remaining PR+1 items (`reflection.md`)

- #1 cluster-level LLM synthesis (2–3 d) — biggest unlock; better after this cron has populated classifications for cluster members.
- #2 cluster workflow state (1 d) — independent.
- #3 pairwise cluster diff view (1–2 d) — soft-needs #2.
- #4 LLM-classification staleness indicator (0.5 d) — independent.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test` — **165 / 167 passing**. The 2 failing tests are the documented pre-existing `as_of` regressions (test 78 + test 109) called out in the MVP handoff brief; unchanged by this PR.
- [x] `pnpm build` — green; new route registered as `ƒ /api/cron/classify-backfill`.
- [x] +24 tests i

Fix annotation `startLine` mismatches across 3 proof entries where annotations were anchored to section divider comments or whitespace instead of named Lean constructs.

**erdos-1012-oq-03** (1 fix):
- `ann-1012-digraph-definitions`: startLine 74→79 (`variable` decl → `structure Digraph`)

**abel-ruffini-oq-04** (5 fixes):
- `ann-part-ii-header`: startLine 42→46 (doc comment of `symmetric_not_solvable`)
- `ann-part-iii-header`: startLine 67→71 (doc comment of `s0_solvable`)
- `ann-part-iv-header`: startLine 77→81 (doc comment of `five_is_the_threshold`)
- `ann-part-v-header`: removed (lines 88–92 pure comment block, no named construct)
- `ann-verification`: removed (lines 154–163: `#check` + `end`, no named construct)

**tractatus-ontology** (28 fixes):
- All 28 annotations updated from section divider lines to their nearest named Lean construct
- 4 annotation types corrected to match actual construct kinds

**Result:** Reduces annotation build errors by ~29 (3743→3714 in worktree builds). 0 errors for all 3 affected proofs.
